## Type-first release creation (2026-09-01, flag-off)

Founder request: "when a user creates a release, then next screen that pops up
is for them to select whether it's an EP or single or album — when they click
the one it is, the release is then created and they then go through the
release; if there is any need for them to input any data they are prompted
after they are seen scrolling around their release." Three founder decisions
confirmed at build time: **the compulsory team-login step does NOT intercept**
(straight into the release; Settings → Team keeps minting logins), **the
Rollout-plan / Blank chooser is dropped** (every type-first release is a
rollout release — "start blank" is covered by never setting a date and using
the date card's "Add an activity yourself" escape hatch), and **the deferred
prompt fires on "any exploring"** — first scroll, first scene open, or ~10s,
whichever comes first, because a brand-new dateless release has no activities
and a literal-scroll-only trigger could never fire.

Behind `NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_TYPE_FIRST_CREATE`, default `false`. **No API
change and NO MIGRATION** — the whole flow is composed from machinery that
already existed: title and date are already optional at `POST /api/releases`
(URG-230; title defaults to "Untitled release"), a dateless rollout release
already gets `template_pending`, and `POST .../schedule` already builds the
plan and is the only safe title+date write (the release PATCH is a full-row
PUT). Flag off, the two-step modal, the access step and the `?new=1` guide are
byte-identical to before.

**Four things worth knowing before editing this:**

1. **The tap IS the form.** Flag on, `CreateReleaseModal` renders ONE screen —
   a card per playbook from `CREATABLE_RELEASE_TYPES`, each quoting its own
   `getTemplateStats` numbers — and `handleTypeFirstPick` submits
   `{ releaseType, plan: 'template' }` directly, taking the option as an
   argument so it can never race the `setReleaseType` state update (which only
   drives the tapped card's spinner). `plan` state stays `null` all the way,
   which is what keeps step 2 and the footer unrendered without touching them.
   Mandatory mode (zero releases) keeps all its no-exit behavior.
2. **All three `onCreated` handlers branch the same way** (WorkspaceView,
   ChappiPageClient, AppShell): flag on → `router.push('/dashboard?release=…')`
   with no access step, no first-win, no `?new=1`. AppShell's instance
   deliberately breaks its own "stay on whatever page" rule for the flag-on
   path only — under type-first the release view is where the rest gets filled
   in, so landing there is the point. The `plannerPending → openIntake` branch
   is kept in all three for safety, though the flag is documented as
   incompatible with `NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_RELEASE_PLANNER` (the intake would
   intercept the landing) and `NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_FIRST_WIN` (it celebrates a
   plan a dateless release does not have).
3. **The deferred prompt is a bottom sheet plus the existing card, not a
   replacement.** `ReleaseSetupSheet` (name optional + date required →
   "Build my plan") follows the TaskOutcomeSheet contract — z-[170], the
   shared `task-outcome-sheet` keyframe, swipe on handle+header only, no
   Escape — but **portals to `document.body`**, because it mounts from
   WorkspaceView under AppShell's `lazy-fade` transform (the
   DeleteReleaseDialog trap; TaskOutcomeSheet skips the portal only because
   TaskUIProvider sits outside that subtree). It submits through
   `lib/schedule-release-client.ts`, the ONE client path to the schedule
   route, now also used by `SetReleaseDateCard` so the 207 handling and toast
   copy cannot drift (pure half in `lib/schedule-release-outcome.ts`,
   import-free so vitest can hold it without the supabase client's env
   requirement). Dismissing is quiet: the undismissable SetReleaseDateCard in
   the panel remains the persistent path to the same two fields.
4. **One nudge per release EVER, marked when the sheet OPENS.** The trigger
   (`useReleaseSetupPrompt` + the pure rules in `lib/release-setup-prompt.ts`)
   arms only for a plan-waiting, dateless, un-nudged release; listens with a
   single **capture-phase** document scroll listener (scroll doesn't bubble,
   but capture sees inner containers — so the desktop activities list and the
   mobile page scroll are both covered without threading a ref into
   TasksPanel); holds while the create modal is open; and persists the marker
   at `urganize.workspace.setup-prompted` (localStorage, capped list of 20,
   read only inside effects per the render-time-storage-read trap). Restricted
   storage fails open to once-per-mount.

- **Untouched on purpose:** the onboarding wizard (already type-first, its own
  flow), Chappi's `create_release` tool, `PlannerIntakeModal`'s own create
  path, and the caller-less `useReleaseStore.createRelease`.
- **Verified:** the full vitest suite (1346 passing, 18 of them new across
  `lib/release-setup-prompt.test.ts` and `lib/schedule-release-outcome.test.ts`),
  `eslint .` at the exact 3-error/66-warning baseline (the 3 warnings on
  touched files are pre-existing `set-state-in-effect` findings, confirmed
  present on a stashed tree), and `next build` green **by exit code** in both
  flag states with `/auth`, `/onboarding`, `/settings` still `○ Static`; the
  flag-on client chunks carry the type-first screen.
- **Not verified:** nothing has run against a real session — the tap-to-create
  flow, the landing, the exploring trigger and the sheet have never rendered
  in a browser (this sandbox cannot mint a Supabase session). Worth one manual
  pass at flag-flip: New release → tap EP → land in the release with no login
  step → scroll or open Metadata → sheet slides up → set name + date → plan
  builds (90 activities) → card gone.
- **Activation checklist:** (1) nothing to migrate — set
  `NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_TYPE_FIRST_CREATE=true` in Vercel `Web` → Production
  **with a commit that rebuilds `apps/web`** (the documented turbo-ignore
  trap), leaving `RELEASE_PLANNER` and `FIRST_WIN` off; (2) changelog entry +
  minor version bump across all 10 `package.json` files (the EPK precedent:
  the ledger entry lands at flag-flip, not at merge); (3) run the manual pass
  above.

## UrgAns prompt-coverage pass: two insight tools, and the honesty rule (2026-09-03)

Founder pasted a real-world ~70-prompt reference list (creative direction,
release planning, content ideas, marketing strategy, audience growth, show
prep, team management, career strategy, data intelligence) and asked whether
UrgAns can "handle these perfectly," plus asked to be moved onto a written
test-driven habit going forward. **Not a scope expansion** — no new tool
reaches outside a release or its tasks, and the audit that came first is the
part worth reading before touching either tool again.

**The mechanical finding, which is what made this a small change rather than
a large one.** `runner.ts`'s tool-calling loop already breaks cleanly the
moment a round returns zero tool calls — a pure creative-writing turn ("give
me 20 TikTok ideas") needs no new code path, it already works today. The gap
was never "no code exists," it was that the system prompt never told the
model this kind of question is welcome, and never told it what to do when a
prompt asks for data Urganize does not collect.

**A real chunk of the list cannot be answered honestly with real numbers.**
Streaming counts, campaign/ad performance, audience demographics — none of it
exists in the product (no DSP integration, no analytics dashboards, both
still correctly out of scope). Founder call: UrgAns says so plainly in the
first sentence rather than inventing a figure or refusing outright, then
still helps with what it does have.

**Two genuine tool-shaped gaps survived the audit against everything else in
the list; nothing else needed a new tool.** Every state-visibility prompt
("what's blocking this release," "identify overdue/high-priority tasks,"
"summarize the current state") was already covered, redundantly, by
`get_dashboard`, `get_release_context`, `list_tasks`, and
`generate_status_update`. What had no tool at all:

- **`compare_releases`** (read) — the N most recent releases side by side:
  date, status, task completion, days ahead of/behind today. Powers "compare
  my last three releases," "based on previous releases what should I
  change," "identify trends." Pure core: `compareReleases` +
  `compareByRecency` in `lib/chappi/tool-families/insights.ts` — later date
  first, an undated release sorts last rather than being dropped, and
  progress is a rounded percentage that never divides by zero.
- **`get_team_workload`** (read) — every teammate's open and overdue task
  count, plus how much is unassigned, tallied separately rather than folded
  into anyone's total. Powers "who should be responsible for each part."
  Pure core: `computeTeamWorkload` in the same file — a task assigned to
  someone who has left the team (present on the task, absent from
  `members`) is counted as neither theirs nor unassigned, since either would
  misreport whose it is.

**`get_team_workload` is Chappi-only, deliberately absent from
`lib/mcp/tools.ts`'s allow-list.** It proxies `GET /api/workspace/members`
via `callInternalApi`, and that handler does not accept the internal actor —
the exact reason `list_workspace_members` itself was never allow-listed
either. Adding it anyway would have advertised an MCP tool that 401s, the
precise mistake `tool-registry.test.ts`'s "only proxies routes whose handler
accepts the internal actor" check exists to catch (and did catch, on the
first attempt at this — the fix is leaving it out, not touching the route).
`compare_releases` has no such dependency — it reads through
`listVisibleReleases`/`TaskService` directly, like `get_dashboard` does — so
it is allow-listed, and `protocol.test.ts`'s tool-count tripwire moved
13 → 14.

**Show-prep prompts are a known, deliberately deferred gap, flagged rather
than silently built.** Events (shows/setlists/DJ packs) has zero Chappi
tools. It is a sibling surface to releases, and every existing Chappi tool
reads or mutates a release or its tasks — the founder-sanctioned rule this
file has stated since Chappi's own sanction in 2026-07-13. Wiring Events in
is its own tool family with its own confirmation-gating calls (a DJ pack
send is already gated in the UI's own terms) and was explicitly out of "a
few closing tools." Left for its own pass.

**The system prompt gained two sections**, not a rewrite of what was there:
one line sanctioning creative-direction/content-idea/marketing-strategy/
career-strategy conversation in plain prose with no tool call required
(mirroring the existing "suggesting activities is welcome" line for tasks),
and one line requiring the model to say plainly it has no streaming/audience/
campaign data rather than invent a number. `ROLE` is now exported specifically
so both lines get a direct content assertion (`system-prompt.test.ts`) rather
than resting on nothing — nothing type-checks a sentence, and a future prompt
rewrite silently dropping either line would otherwise go unnoticed.

**This is also the first pass under the new "write the test first" habit**
(see the new Conventions → Tests subsection) — `insights.test.ts` was written
and confirmed red (module didn't exist) before `insights.ts` did.

- **Verified:** 2118 tests passing (19 new: 16 in `insights.test.ts`, 3 in
  `system-prompt.test.ts`), `eslint .` at the exact pre-existing baseline
  (3 errors / 70 warnings, all in `WorkspaceView.tsx`, unrelated to this
  work), `tsc --noEmit` clean apart from the documented pre-existing
  `confirmed-action.test.ts` errors, `next build`'s compile + typecheck steps
  both clean (the static-export step cannot run in this environment — no
  `.env.local`, no Supabase URL — a pre-existing sandbox limitation, not
  something this change introduced).
- **No new flag, no migration.** UrgAns is already gated by
  `NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_CHAPPI`; these are two ordinary additions to its
  existing tool registry, live for any account UrgAns is already live for the
  moment this merges to `main`.
- **Not verified, and it is the whole remaining risk:** no live model call has
  run from this sandbox (no network route to either urganize domain), so
  whether the two tools' descriptions are clear enough for the model to reach
  for them unprompted, and whether the system prompt's two new lines actually
  change real answers, rest on the tests above plus a traced read of the
  runner loop — not on anything observed. Worth one real pass against the
  deployed assistant: ask a handful of prompts from the founder's original
  list spanning each category (a pure ideation one, a data-gap one, and
  "compare my last three releases" / "who should be responsible for each
  part" specifically) and confirm the tone, the tool calls, and the honesty
  line all land as designed.

## Report an issue, straight into Linear (2026-09-03, flag-off)

Founder request: let users report bugs and make requests from inside Urganize,
and have each one create a Linear issue automatically.

**What the support path actually was before this**, which is most of the reason
it was worth building: the `?` HelpMenu offering Docs, a raw
`mailto:contact@urganize.app`, and a WhatsApp community link — and that menu is
`hidden md:block`, so **on a phone there was no support surface at all**. The
dedicated "Report a bug" affordance had been the WhatsApp pill in
`components/support/SupportChat.tsx`, deleted 2026-08-17 (`d9c9fa68`) along with
`lib/support-contact.ts` and the dock/rail footer links. Nothing replaced it.
The External services entry above described that pill as live until this pass
corrected it, and the `profiles.artist_name` reader count in the artists section
was one too high for the same reason — both flagged rather than silently fixed.

**Not a scope expansion in the out-of-scope sense** — the nearest line,
"third-party music platform integrations", is not crossed (Linear is not a DSP)
and this is not the v2 notifications inbox. It IS, like Notes, deliberately
**global rather than release-scoped**: a bug report is about the product, not
about a release. Behind `NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_REPORT_ISSUE`, default `false`.

**Founder decisions taken before building:** entry points are the HelpMenu plus
a Settings → Account section (no new floating chrome — the bottom-right slot is
already contested by the UrgAns dock, the install card and the notification
ask); a report is stored in Urganize FIRST and pushed to Linear second; and the
attached context is page + app version, name + email, team + plan + role, and
the scoped release.

### Seven things worth knowing before editing this

1. **`POST /api/issue-reports` is deliberately NOT behind the paywall**, and a
   source-reading test enforces it. It uses `getAuthenticatedUser`, never
   `requireActiveAuthenticatedUser` — the `app/api/account/export` call, for a
   stronger version of the same reason: the gated helper runs
   `requireActiveAccount`, which answers **402**, which `lib/access-redirect.ts`
   turns into a browser redirect to `/locked`. A walled or read-only team would
   be ejected from the app **by the act of reporting that it ejected them**. The
   property rests on one import and a comment cannot defend it, so
   `lib/issue-reports-route-guard.test.ts` comment-strips the route source and
   fails if any paywall wrapper appears (mutation-tested).
2. **Identity is resolved server-side; the client sends only what only it
   knows.** The browser supplies the page path, and a release id it read off its
   own URL. Name, email, team, plan and role are read from the database against
   the authenticated user id in `resolveReporterContext`. Accepting a plan tier
   from a request body would let anyone write whatever they liked onto the
   Linear board, and the same guard test asserts no identity field is ever read
   off the payload.
3. **`lib/issue-reports-server.ts` does its own narrow reads rather than calling
   `loadWorkspaceAccessContext`.** That resolver carries provision-on-miss
   WRITES and a fair amount of machinery, and this is the one endpoint that has
   to keep working when the rest of the app does not. A support path should
   depend on as little of the thing being reported as possible. Every field
   degrades independently and an unreadable one is left ABSENT, never set to a
   misleading value — `buildIssueDescription` omits absent fields entirely, so a
   Linear issue simply does not claim a team rather than claiming an unknown
   one (the `buildTeamAlertContext` posture).
4. **Linear never fails the submission.** The row is written first and is the
   durable record; the push is a follow-up whose outcome lands in `status`
   (`pending` / `synced` / `failed`), retryable from `/admin/issue-reports`. The
   reporter is told we have it either way, because by then we do. With
   `LINEAR_API_KEY` unset the whole feature still works — reports just sit
   `failed` until somebody configures it and retries.
5. **The personal API key goes in `Authorization` with NO `Bearer` prefix.**
   A `lin_api_…` key is passed raw; prefixing it fails auth with a 401 that
   looks exactly like a bad key. It is the single easiest thing to get wrong
   here, so it has its own unit test, mutation-tested. (OAuth access tokens are
   the ones that take Bearer — we do not use those.)
6. **GraphQL answers HTTP 200 for a rejected mutation.** Reading `response.ok`
   alone would record a `synced` report that does not exist in Linear, so the
   body is parsed and inspected for an `errors` array and a `success: false`
   before anything is called a success. Also tested.
7. **There is a per-user rate limit, and it is the only one in this repo.**
   Ten reports per rolling hour, counted off the table itself — no new infra.
   Principle 6 says build for the case we have, and everywhere else that means
   no rate limiting; this endpoint earns one because it is authenticated but
   open to every user and each call writes to a third party. It **fails open**
   on an unreadable count, like every other counter here (seats, releases,
   UrgAns actions): wrongly refusing somebody's bug report is worse than
   wrongly allowing an eleventh.

### Smaller decisions

- **Two entry points, one dialog, one store.** `useReportIssueStore` bridges
  them because the HelpMenu and Settings live in different ownership islands —
  the `usePlannerStore` reasoning verbatim. The Settings section is what makes
  the feature reachable on a phone at all, via the "You" tab.
- **`ReportIssueSection` sits mid-tab in Account**, not in the
  password/sign-out/delete tail: reporting a bug is not a rare
  high-consequence account action. It is there for the same structural reason
  `AdminSection` is — that tab is the only mobile surface it can be reached
  from.
- **The dialog portals to `document.body`** (AppShell's `lazy-fade` transform
  breaks `position: fixed` for descendants — the `DeleteReleaseDialog` trap) and
  owns Escape, because unlike the UrgAns rail it is a real modal.
- **`/admin/issue-reports` is deliberately NOT flag-gated** — the `/admin/teams`
  precedent. A report that failed to reach Linear must stay visible whether or
  not the reporting feature is currently switched on.
- **Migration `20260903150000_issue_reports.sql`** — RLS on, **zero policies**
  (the `pricing_validation_responses` / `mcp_oauth_*` posture; every path is
  service-role). Three different delete rules, each argued in the file header:
  reporter CASCADE, workspace and release SET NULL.
- **Only the `NEXT_PUBLIC_` flag goes in `turbo.json`.** `LINEAR_API_KEY`,
  `LINEAR_TEAM_ID` and the two optional label ids are server-only request-time
  reads — the `CHAPPI_API_KEY` / `RESEND_API_KEY` / `GENRE_PREDICTION_URL`
  precedent.

### Verified

`vitest run` — **2302 passing** (42 new across `lib/issue-reports.test.ts`,
`lib/linear-server.test.ts` and `lib/issue-reports-route-guard.test.ts`), 30
env-gated skips unchanged. `eslint .` at **3 errors / 75 warnings** against a
measured clean-tree baseline of 3 / 73 — the two new warnings are both the
documented React-19 `set-state-in-effect` downgrade and both match an existing
finding byte-for-byte (the admin page's fetch-on-mount mirrors
`TeamsAdminPageClient.tsx`; the dialog's portal mount guard mirrors
`DeleteReleaseDialog.tsx`, confirmed by linting those two files). `next build`
green **by exit code** in BOTH flag states with `/auth`, `/onboarding` and
`/settings` still `○ Static` in each.

Runtime probes against `next start`, rebuilding between flag states because
`NEXT_PUBLIC_*` is inlined at build time even server-side: **flag on**,
`POST /api/issue-reports` **401**s unauthenticated (so auth precedes everything
after the gate); **flag off**, it **404**s with body exactly `{"error":"Not
found."}` while the ungated `/api/releases` still **401**s — that 404-vs-401
discrimination is what proves the gate rather than a routing accident. The admin
route answers the same `ADMIN_EMAILS is not configured` 500 as the pre-existing
`/api/admin/teams` under this sandbox's env, verified side by side rather than
assumed.

**Three mutation passes**, each failing exactly its own test and nothing else:
adding a `Bearer` prefix to the Authorization header, importing
`requireActiveAuthenticatedUser` into the route, and (checked while writing) the
absent-field omission in the description builder.

**Sandbox note for the next session:** `next build`'s static-export step needs a
`.env.local` that does not exist here. A throwaway one with
`NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=https://placeholder.supabase.co` plus an anon and a
service-role placeholder is enough to get a real exit code and real runtime
probes; it is gitignored, and it was removed again afterwards.

## Pullout explanations, and one place the copy lives (2026-09-08, v1.35.0)

Founder ask, from a screenshot of Vercel's side menu (a nav row hovered, a short
dark panel beside it saying what that page does): *"I need this kind of pullout
explanation for all the places where there are too much text, like inside the
metadata capture feature... check around every single pixel in the app... so easy
a fifth grader can use the app."*

**Not a scope expansion, no migration, no new flag** — the back-arrow /
mobile-scene-nav / Collect-metadata precedent for a founder-driven UX rework of
shipped surfaces. Revert is `git revert`.

### The fifth-grader bar is a test, not a preference

`lib/help-copy.ts` holds every explanation in the app, and
`lib/help-copy.test.ts` enforces the bar: at most 2 sentences, 18 words a
sentence, 160 characters, a full stop, no double space, and no jargon from an
explicit list. **A bar a person has to remember lasts until somebody is in a
hurry**, which is the same reasoning `lib/press-kit-copy-guard.test.ts` already
records for the house rules — and `help-copy.ts` is listed in THAT guard's FILES
too, so the em dash, the banned words and the never-says-workspace rule have one
definition rather than two.

Three properties of that guard worth keeping:

1. **`metadata` is ON the jargon list, even though a scene is named Metadata.**
   That is the point: the label already says the word, so a pullout repeating it
   explains nothing. The list is deliberately NOT "long words" — "distributor"
   and "publisher" are long and are what the things are actually called.
2. **No entry may lean on its own label.** Each carries the label it sits beside,
   and the guard refuses copy containing any of that label's words of 5+ letters.
   It is what forced "One page about the artist that you can send to writers and
   radio stations" instead of a sentence with "press kit" in it. Words under 5
   letters are skipped, or "name" and "line" would push copy into vagueness,
   which costs a beginner more than a repeated short word.
3. **A key with no call site FAILS.** Derived by scanning `components/` and
   `app/`, the mechanism that holds the tool registry and the icon set in step.
   Dead copy reads as covered in review and renders nowhere.

### The primitive, and why it portals

`components/shared/HelpTip.tsx` is two layers: `HelpTipPanel` (the positioned
panel, taking the element to point at) and `HelpTip` (a small round `i` button
that owns its own panel). Four things a later change will be tempted to get
wrong:

1. **TAP IS THE BASELINE FOR THE BUTTON; HOVER IS THE ENHANCEMENT.** A real
   `<button>` that toggles on click, so it works on a phone — most of this
   product's traffic. Hover is gated on `matchMedia('(hover: hover) and (pointer:
   fine)')` rather than a width breakpoint, because a touch laptop is wide and
   cannot hover. **The SIDE MENU is the deliberate exception and is hover-only**,
   which costs nothing: that card is `hidden lg:block` and never renders on a
   touch device at all.
2. **IT PORTALS TO `document.body`, and it has to.** Both target surfaces clip
   their own children — the side menu's nav list is `overflow-y-auto`, every
   metadata step card is `overflow-hidden` — and inside AppShell a `fixed` panel
   is broken by the `lazy-fade` transform, the trap `DeleteReleaseDialog` already
   portals around. `document.body` is read DURING RENDER, which is safe by
   construction rather than luck: `anchor` is a DOM element, so the early return
   fires during SSR and that line is unreachable. Doing it with a mount effect
   instead cost a `set-state-in-effect` warning for nothing.
3. **THE PLACEMENT DECISION IS PURE, in `lib/help-tip-position.ts`.** Prefer a
   side (the screenshot's shape) or below, flip when there is no room, clamp
   inside the viewport, never return a negative. It falls back to below when
   neither side fits, **which is what makes it responsive with no media query**.
   Note a phone does not always land there — a trigger near either edge of a
   375px screen still has room on one side, and gets it.
4. **The trigger element lives in STATE via a callback ref, not a `useRef`.** The
   panel needs it as a prop, and reading `ref.current` during render is a
   `react-hooks/refs` ERROR in this config — the rule that accounts for all three
   pre-existing errors in the repo. Writing it the obvious way added a fourth.

**Screen readers keep the sentence.** The metadata `Field` renders the same
HELP_COPY text as an `sr-only` paragraph wired to the input with
`aria-describedby`, exactly as the old visible hint was. Moving an explanation
behind a hover would otherwise have taken it away entirely from the people who
cannot see the icon; both read one entry, so they cannot drift.

### What changed, surface by surface

- **The side menu** (the screenshot's own case): all ten rows. Expanded rows had
  no explanation at all; only the collapsed rail carried a native `title`. ONE
  panel serves the whole list, because only one tip is ever visible and the rows
  are built inside a `.map` where a per-row hook would break the rules of hooks —
  so rows report which one they point at and `WorkspaceNavList` owns the panel.
  The collapsed rail is deliberately excluded: its `title` is already carrying the
  label, which matters more there, and two popups on one row is worse than either.
- **Metadata** (the named feature): nine field hints became nine pullouts, the
  scene intro went 3 sentences to 1, and each step's helper paragraph was split —
  **the visible line says what to DO, the pullout says who is asking and why**,
  complementary rather than the same sentence twice. Step 2's was four sentences,
  the worst in the file. The two `℗`/`©` labels lost their parentheses, which were
  an explanation wearing a label's clothes.
- **Settings**: four section intros of 3, 3, 4 and 5 sentences (Artists, Your
  directory record, Your data, Team brief). The team brief's rewrite also drops an
  em dash its old sentence carried.
- **The test-release banner**: 4 sentences standing permanently, one of which
  ("when you are done, delete it below") was redundant with the Delete button
  directly underneath it.

### The sweep, and what was deliberately LEFT

The founder asked for every pixel, so the whole of `components/` was scanned for
static paragraphs of 3+ sentences or 150+ characters. **27 remain, and most
should.** The classification is the useful output:

- **Consequential choices stay visible.** The metadata link paragraph was
  TRIMMED (3 sentences to 2) rather than pulled, because it is the difference
  between Close link and Regenerate, one of which kills a link that may already
  be in somebody's inbox. Same call for `DeleteReleaseDialog`,
  `ArchiveReleaseDialog` and the capture page's delete confirmation: a warning
  about something irreversible is not clutter.
- **Money and access stay visible.** `TeamWall`'s two paragraphs and the artist
  plan limit are read by somebody deciding whether to pay. Hiding terms behind a
  hover is the wrong instinct there.
- **Security detail stays visible.** `McpConnectionsSection`'s "they can see your
  releases... they cannot see your password or your card" is about third-party
  access to a workspace's data.
- **A surface whose whole job is explaining keeps explaining.**
  `NewReleaseGuide` is a one-time orientation card; a pullout inside it would be
  odd.
- **Nine were false positives of my own scan**, which sums both branches of a
  ternary — each branch of `ReportIssueDialog`, `CreateShowModal`,
  `CaptureEditor`, `TeammatesSection` and the rest is one or two sentences
  already. One match was a code comment, not copy.

**The discriminating rule, if a future pass wants one: pull an explanation when
it teaches, keep it when it warns.**

### Verified

**2998 tests** (33 new across `lib/help-copy.test.ts` and
`lib/help-tip-position.test.ts`) against a **measured** clean-tree baseline of
2965 — measured by stashing rather than trusting a figure from an earlier
session, which is what caught that the recorded 2922 was three commits stale.
`eslint .` at **exactly** the 3-error / 81-warning baseline with **zero** new
findings; the first run was 4 errors / 82 warnings and both were fixed rather
than accepted (see point 4 above and the portal-host note). `tsc --noEmit` clean
apart from the documented pre-existing `confirmed-action.test.ts` errors.
`next build` green **by exit code** with the affected flags on and with them off,
`/auth`, `/onboarding`, `/settings` and `/dashboard` all still `○ Static` in
each. Compiled CSS checked rather than trusted from source: `z-[150]`,
`max-w-[17rem]`, `align-text-bottom` and `sr-only` all present — worth noting
`z-[150]` arrives via a `PANEL_Z` const and IS still extracted, since Tailwind
scans raw file text, but that is the interpolated-class trap this repo has hit
before and is the reason to check.

**Three mutations, each killing exactly its own test** and each printing
`APPLIED` first (the recorded lesson that a mutation which never landed is
indistinguishable from a survivor): the placement flip removed, the sentence cap
raised to 99, and the jargon check reduced to a bare substring match.

**A test premise I got wrong, recorded because the arithmetic is reusable:** the
"neither side fits" case was first written with a trigger at x=20 on a 375px
screen, which DOES fit (20 + 16 + 8 + 260 = 304, against a 363 right margin). The
fixture is mid-screen now, and a second test pins the near-edge case that legitimately
takes a side.

### Not verified

**Nothing has rendered in a browser.** This sandbox cannot mint an authenticated
session and has no route to app.urganize.app, so the panel's placement against
real text, the hover on a real pointer, the tap on a real phone, and the
`sr-only` description in a real screen reader all rest on the unit tests plus the
build. Worth one pass: hover a side-menu row at 1280px and confirm the panel
lands beside the card rather than inside it, then open Metadata on a phone and
tap an `i` beside a field near the bottom of a step card — that is the case the
`overflow-hidden` portal and the flip-above branch both exist for.

## Repositioned as an AI Music Manager (2026-09-09, v1.35.0)

> **SUPERSEDED 2026-09-24** by "Everything after the music" at the end of this
> file. The machinery described here (one module, a byte-identical homepage
> mirror, the guard, the share card generator) is unchanged and still works the
> way this section says; the strings in it changed, and the product is no
> longer introduced by a category. Read the newer section first.

Founder brief, locked: the product is an **AI Music Manager for artists,
managers and labels**, and the promise is **"Plan, organize and execute
releases from one place."** Applied everywhere a person can read a description
of the product. **No feature work, no pricing change, no data model change** —
copy, metadata, one image and one new doc.

**It consciously REVERSES two rules from the 2026-08-19 executive positioning**
(now marked superseded where it is stated). That brief banned container
metaphors ("one home", "lives in one place") and explicitly ALLOWED the word
"workspace". This one bans "workspace" in anything a person reads and makes
"from one place" the product's own promise. Both reversals are the founder's;
every other rule that brief set still binds — fifth-grade readability, no
Oxford comma in house copy, verbatim customer quotes only.

### The canonical strings live in a module, and it is duplicated on purpose

`apps/web/lib/positioning.ts` holds eight exports and everything else derives
from them. `apps/homepage/lib/positioning.ts` is a byte-identical mirror below
its header comment.

**Why a module rather than the string at each call site:** this repo has
shipped the display-vs-reality gap four times with prices, once with the share
card's alt text against the card's own baked tagline, and twice with a landing
title that existed in two files. Positioning drifts worse than a price does,
because nothing errors — two pages simply describe a different product and
nobody notices for a month.

**Why a duplicate rather than a package:** `apps/homepage` cannot import from
`apps/web` (separate Next apps, no shared path alias), and a package for eight
strings adds an eleventh `package.json` to bump on every release. That is the
trade already recorded for `lib/deploy-version.ts`, whose homepage twin is a
deliberate 20-line copy — and its own note, **"a third consumer is the moment
to promote it"**, applies here unchanged. What makes it safe is that the copy
is not trusted to stay in step by care: the guard strips both files' comments
and fails if a single string differs.

**`AUDIENCE` is a list, not a sentence.** Artists always lead, and the order is
artists, managers, labels, never reordered for emphasis. Keeping it as data
lets the guard pin the ORDER rather than pin one sentence that happens to
contain it.

### Nine things worth knowing before editing any of this

1. **`lib/positioning-guard.test.ts` is what makes the retirement permanent
   rather than a sweep somebody has to repeat.** It walks all of
   `apps/homepage/app` and `apps/homepage/lib`, six named `apps/web` files,
   `README.md` and `docs/store-listing.md`, and fails on twelve retired
   patterns plus "workspace" in any user-readable string. The brief's own step
   5 (a final grep) is a one-off; this is the version that runs on every
   change.
2. **It scans strings, template literals AND JSX text nodes**
   (`lib/copy-scan.ts`, `readableCopy`). Extracting only string literals would
   have missed most of the marketing site, where the copy is prose between
   tags. `userFacingStrings` is lifted from the press-kit copy guard so the two
   share one extractor.
3. **IT HAS TWO BLIND SPOTS, and they are now PINNED BY TESTS rather than
   only documented in a header.** Comments are exempt by design (the press-kit
   guard's own reasoning: the working record holds dates, prose and quotations,
   and holding it to product-copy rules would either gut it or teach everyone
   to work around the test). And a string with no whitespace is treated as an
   identifier, so `aria-label="Workspace"` is invisible to it — three of those
   existed in `AppTopbar` and were found by reading, not by the guard.
   `lib/copy-scan.test.ts` asserts both as deliberate behaviour, because a
   header comment is exactly what somebody closes in good faith; it also pins
   that `readableCopy` COLLAPSES whitespace where the raw readers do not, so a
   phrase split across an interpolation closes up and a verbatim pattern would
   miss it. Every retired pattern is a phrase nobody would interpolate through
   the middle of, which is what makes that acceptable.
4. **`ALLOWED` contains exactly one entry, `'Google Workspace'`**, which is
   somebody else's product name in the MCP setup copy. Anything else added
   there is a hole.
5. **The meta-description check reads the description's OWN EXPRESSION, not
   the file.** This is the one mutation that survived the first pass and it is
   worth knowing why: dropping `${CUSTOMER_LINE}` from a page's description
   passed, because the fallback tested the whole file source and matched the
   leftover `import { CUSTOMER_LINE }` line. It now extracts the expression
   between `description:` and the next known key. Tightening it then
   over-caught seven pages, because `PRODUCT_CATEGORY` had been dropped from
   the allowlist — safe to re-add once only the expression is scanned.
6. **Next's `title.template` applies to CHILD segments only.** So the root
   layout's `"%s | Urganize"` gives every nested page `Page name | Urganize`
   automatically, while `app/page.tsx` renders `BRAND_LINE` alone — which is
   exactly the acceptance criterion (the homepage title is
   "Urganize, AI Music Manager", not "… | Urganize"). `app/download/page.tsx`'s
   own comment already recorded this.
7. **The UrgAns prompt tripped the guard on its own instructions**, and the fix
   is the shape to reuse: telling the model "never call Urganize a workspace"
   puts the banned word in a scanned file. Both rules are consolidated into one
   exported `URGANS_COPY_RULES` and exempted by identity — the
   `bannedCopyInstruction()` precedent. A first attempt split the value on the
   constant and failed, because the constant is a two-literal concatenation and
   the scanner extracts each literal separately; the check is now "the whole
   trimmed value appears in the instruction".
8. **UrgAns is NOT the product, and `URGANS_LINE` is the whole distinction.**
   Asked what Urganize is, it answers with the category; asked what IT is, it
   answers "the personal AI for music professionals inside it". Collapsing the
   two would make the assistant the product, which is the error this brief
   exists to correct.
9. **`SHARE_IMAGE_VERSION` and `SHARE_IMAGE.alt` must move with the card.** The
   version busts the platform caches that do not refetch on a silent file swap
   (URG-156); the alt text is the only machine-readable record of what the
   image says, and the guard reads it, so a regeneration that skipped it fails
   the build.

### The share card has a template now

`apps/homepage/scripts/generate-og-image.mjs` renders the card from `next/og`
and the brand TTFs already checked in for the recap poster, writing the SAME
bytes to both apps' `public/opengraph-image.png` (both reference
`/opengraph-image.png` on their own origin, and a card that disagreed between
the two hosts would be worse than a stale one). **This closes a gap this file
recorded for three weeks** — "a new card needs a founder-approved line and a
`SHARE_IMAGE_VERSION` bump, no template for it exists in the repo".

One trap: `import { ImageResponse } from 'next/og'` throws
`ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` under ESM, because next's exports map does not declare
that subpath for it. `createRequire` + `pathToFileURL(require.resolve(...))`
resolves it.

### Four naming decisions, so they are not re-litigated

- **Settings' "Workspace" tab is "Profile".** Account is you, Profile is your
  team's name, logo and artists, Team is the people. The skeleton's placeholder
  width moved with the label (`w-[79px] sm:w-[83px]` → `w-[66px] sm:w-[70px]`),
  per the loading-skeleton-sync rule.
- **The topbar's "Workspace" controls are "Catalog"**, which is what their own
  icon and action were already called (`CatalogIcon`,
  `CatalogTopbarAction`) — the label was the half that disagreed.
- **`/for-executives` is titled "For roster teams" and KEEPS its route.**
  Renaming routes is out of scope, and a live URL is not a copy decision.
- **The roadmap's "Shipped" label is "Delivered"**, and its `shipped` key is
  untouched — the brief exempts code identifiers.

### What was deliberately left alone

- **The changelog is history** (founder: "leave the changelog entries alone").
  Two entries contain "ship"/"shipped" and stay as written; rewriting a shipped
  ledger entry would falsify the log, which is the same reasoning already
  recorded for the v0.9.0 trial entry.
- **`AUDIT.md`'s one hit is a quotation** of a past keyword brief.
- **Code identifiers, routes, database columns and env vars** containing
  "workspace" — explicitly out of scope, and roughly 120 of the 190-odd hits
  swept were logs, SQL fixtures, CSS class names, storage path prefixes and
  section keys.
- **`apps/homepage` earns no changelog entry**, per the app-only scope rule, so
  v1.35.0's single new highlight covers only the in-app rename. (This work was
  written as v1.33.0 and landed as v1.35.0: two other sessions delivered 1.33.0
  and 1.34.0 while the branch was open, and appending to an already-delivered
  entry would edit a shipped one, so it became its own increment instead.)

### Verified

3039 tests passing / 30 skipped, **23 new** — 10 in `positioning-guard.test.ts`,
12 in `copy-scan.test.ts` and 1 in `system-prompt.test.ts` — against a
**measured** clean-tree baseline of 3016. That baseline was taken by stashing
rather than trusting the 2998 figure an earlier session recorded, which is what
caught that the rebase onto main had brought 18 tests of its own. `eslint .` at
**exactly** the measured 3-error / 81-warning baseline in `apps/web` and its own
0-error / 2-warning baseline in `apps/homepage`, both with zero new findings, `tsc --noEmit` clean apart from the
documented pre-existing `confirmed-action.test.ts` errors, and `next build`
green **by exit code** for both apps with `/auth`, `/onboarding`, `/settings`
and `/dashboard` all still `○ Static`. The built homepage `<title>` was read
out of the prerendered HTML rather than trusted from source. The card was
rendered and looked at: ink ground, cream text, spring accent on the category,
wordmark top left, two lines and nothing else, 1200x630.

**Seven mutation passes**, each killing exactly its own test, and three of them
worth recording: the description-expression fix above; one attempt that **never
applied** (PATTERN NOT FOUND), caught per the standing lesson that a mutation
which never landed is indistinguishable from a survivor and redone against the
exact string; and the two on the extractor itself (dropping the `[^:]` URL guard
from the comment strip, and letting `userFacingStrings` accept a string with no
whitespace), which are the two filters every guard built on it depends on.

Two tests pinned the old copy and were inverted with it
(`email-templates.test.ts`'s "invited you to a workspace",
`team-logins.test.ts`'s "added to a workspace") — the same move
`isContactSalesPlan('label')` made when Label changed meaning.

### One known gap, named rather than quietly widened

**`URGANS_COPY_RULES` tells the model to use no em dashes, and ROLE still
contains 26 of them** in its tool list and guidance sections. Those are strings
this pass did not write: the voice and formatting paragraphs, which are the two
a model would imitate for style, were rewritten without them (the formatting
one is the paragraph the instruction is interpolated into, so it was
demonstrating the punctuation it forbids), and the ROLE opening and the copy
rules themselves are clean. The remaining 26 are appositive dashes inside tool
descriptions, and rewriting them is a mechanical sweep of the
highest-consequence prompt in the app for a rule the brief scopes to strings
touched. Left as the obvious follow-up, with the note that the structural test
asserting every tool name appears in ROLE is what makes such a sweep safe to
attempt.

### Not verified, and it is two of the brief's own steps

**The brief asked for a social card preview and a click-through of login,
onboarding, dashboard, settings and the upgrade modal, with screenshots.
Neither is reachable from here:** this sandbox cannot mint an authenticated
Supabase session, and the agent proxy answers 403 to CONNECT for both urganize
domains, so no social debugger can be asked to fetch the card either. What
stands in for them is the guard, the build, and the card rendered locally.

Worth one pass after deploy: paste the homepage URL into a social debugger and
confirm the new card, then sign in and read the login headline, the onboarding
intro, Settings' Profile tab and the upgrade wall.

## The team trial shortened to 3 days (2026-09-10)

Founder call: shorten the free trial from 14 days to 3. Not a scope
expansion, no migration, no new flag — the mechanism (`NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_HARD_PAYWALL`,
see "Team trial + hard paywall" above) is untouched; only the length changes.

**`TEAM_TRIAL_DAYS` in `lib/team-billing.ts` is the ONE place this is a
number** — `ensureOwnedWorkspace`'s provisioning stamp, the founder-alert
"trial started" event, and every UI surface (`TeamTrialStrip`, `/admin/teams`,
`/locked`) all read it or a value derived from it, and none of them carry a
second hardcoded day count. That single-source property is what made this a
constant edit rather than a hunt.

**Two things needed more than the constant, both because they were sized
against the OLD 14-day length rather than against the trial itself:**

1. **`TEAM_TRIAL_PILL_THRESHOLD_DAYS`** — the countdown strip's "show only
   near the end" rule — was `10`, i.e. the last 10 of 14 days (~71% of the
   trial). At `10` against a 3-day trial the pill would show for the ENTIRE
   trial from day one, which is exactly the "nagging countdown" the constant's
   own comment says it exists to avoid. It is `1` now: the strip appears only
   on the trial's final day. The invariant test
   (`TEAM_TRIAL_PILL_THRESHOLD_DAYS < TEAM_TRIAL_DAYS`) still holds and would
   have caught getting this wrong in the other direction.
2. **The founder-alert "trial ending soon" sweep
   (`runTrialEndingSweep` in `lib/billing-alerts-server.ts`) had ITS OWN
   hardcoded `3 * DAY_MS` horizon**, sized as "the last 3 of 14 days" and
   coincidentally the same digit as the new trial length — a trap for anyone
   skimming rather than reading the comment. Left as a literal `3`, every team
   would trip the "entering its last 3 days" alert on the day it is CREATED,
   since `now + 3 days` always lands on-or-past a 3-day trial's `trial_ends_at`
   from day one. It now imports `TEAM_TRIAL_PILL_THRESHOLD_DAYS` from
   `team-billing.ts` and derives the horizon from that shared constant instead
   of a second hardcoded number — the same "one source of truth" property the
   rest of the file already had, extended to close the one place it was
   missing. This was a real behavioural bug caught by tracing the sweep before
   shipping, not by a test — it has no test file, per this codebase's own
   documented pattern of manual-pass-only coverage for I/O-heavy server
   sweeps.

**The marketing site cannot import `TEAM_TRIAL_DAYS`** (the established
`apps/homepage` cannot import `apps/web` constraint, the same one that forces
`lib/positioning.ts` to be duplicated byte-for-byte across both apps), so
"14 days" / "14-day" is duplicated as literal prose across the homepage:
the hero, the final CTA, `/features`, all three self-serve persona pages,
`/signup`, `/terms` §04, the pricing strip, the tier-card footnote, and the
FAQ. All of it now reads "3 days" / "3-day". `PricingTierCards.tsx`'s own
comment already named the three places that have to move together (the
constant, its own copy, and `/signup`) — this is that move, done for real
with the trial length as the second thing (after the annual-only reprice)
to actually require it.

`docs/store-listing.md` (the paste-ready, never-yet-submitted App Store /
Play Store copy) is not history — it is a draft awaiting the founder's first
store submission — so it moved too, along with its stated character count
for the block that changed (`1,777` → `1,776`, one character shorter for
"3 days" versus "14 days"). By contrast, `packages/changelog/src/index.ts`'s
own v0.60.0 entry announcing the ORIGINAL 14-day trial is left exactly as
written — changelog history is never rewritten, the same rule that keeps the
v0.9.0 trial entry and the pre-tier pricing entries untouched through every
later change.

**Verified:** `pnpm test` (3190 tests, same count as before — the constant
and its test file's three assertions were rewritten together, so nothing
about test coverage shrank), `eslint .` at the exact 3-error / 78-warning
baseline, `tsc --noEmit` clean apart from the documented pre-existing
`confirmed-action.test.ts` errors, and `next build` green **by exit code**
for both apps with `/auth`, `/onboarding`, `/settings`, `/dashboard`,
`/pricing`, `/signup` and `/terms` all still `○ Static`. The prerendered HTML
was read directly rather than trusted from source (this repo's habit for any
copy change): every marketing page checked shows "3 days" / "3-day" and zero
occurrences of "14-day" or "14 days free" survive anywhere in the built
output.

**Not verified:** nothing has run against a real database, so no team has
actually been provisioned with a 3-day `trial_ends_at`, the shortened pill
window has never rendered against a real countdown, and the corrected
founder-alert sweep has never fired for real. Worth one live pass once
deployed: create a team, confirm `workspaces.trial_ends_at` is ~3 days out,
watch the strip stay silent until the final day, and confirm the sweep does
not fire the "trial ending soon" alert on day one.

## The card trial is retired (2026-09-10)

Founder report, from a real signup on a phone: the prices on `/start-trial`
"have not changed in app to match the new pricing", and then **"Couldn't
confirm payment — that card couldn't be saved for future billing"** when they
tried to start the trial. Two symptoms, one root cause.

**`/start-trial` was the last live checkout still reading the frozen legacy
price table.** `StartTrialPageClient` renders `getPlan('monthly'|'annual')`
from `BILLING_PLANS` and charges the matching legacy Paystack Plans through
`PAYSTACK_PLAN_{MONTHLY,ANNUAL}_NGN`. Every reprice since pricing-v2 went into
`PRICING_TIERS` instead — that table is deliberately frozen, and its own
comment says why ("editing BILLING_PLANS would change what a real checkout
advertises"). Nobody noticed that the sentence had stopped being a reason to
leave it alone and become a description of a bug:

| | `/start-trial` showed | What the product sells |
|---|---|---|
| Intervals | Monthly **and** Annual | Annual only, since 2026-09-08 |
| Price | ₦80,000/mo · ₦800,000/yr | Solo ₦5,000 · Manager ₦22,000 · Label ₦50,000 /yr |
| Trial | 28 days, card required | 3 days, card-free (`TEAM_TRIAL_DAYS`) |

₦800,000 against Solo's ₦5,000 is **160×**, and monthly is an interval that no
longer exists in the data at all (`PricingTierDefinition.prices` is
`{ annual }` — the shape is the enforcement).

**The founder call: turn `NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_CARD_TRIAL` off.** Both symptoms
go with it — the wrong prices become unreachable, and no card is collected so
the card-save failure cannot happen. New signups fall to the 3-day team trial
plus the hard wall, which is the newer decision and the one already announced.

**The clinching argument was the ledger's own words.** v1.41.0 reads *"The free
trial is now 3 days instead of 14. Same terms otherwise: your whole team, **no
card**."* That entry shipped the same day this report came in, so the card
funnel being on is what made an announced promise false. **So there is no new
ledger entry for the flip and no version bump: it delivers what v1.41.0 already
says rather than announcing anything.**

### Five things worth knowing

1. **⚠️ THE FLIP DOES NOT CANCEL PAYSTACK SUBSCRIPTIONS THE FLOW ALREADY
   CREATED, and this was NOT hypothetical — the audit found one.** A successful
   card trial writes `subscriptions.status = 'trialing'` AND creates a remote
   Paystack subscription whose `start_date` is trial end, so anyone who got
   *through* is charged the legacy amount on their day 28 whatever this flag
   says. **The founder's query returned one row: `plan: annual`, amount
   ₦800,000, `SUB_zogd3gidljj5h3n…`, still `trialing`.** Left alone, day 28
   fires a `charge.success` with a fresh reference, which matches by
   `paystack_subscription_code`, takes the ordinary renewal path, and bills that
   customer **₦800,000 for a plan the ladder no longer contains** — 16× Label's
   real ₦50,000. Turning a funnel off is not the same as unwinding it.

   **The fix is to disable it at Paystack, and the app handles the rest
   correctly with no code change** (verified rather than assumed):
   `subscription.disable` → `handleSubscriptionDisable` stamps
   `status: 'cancelled'` and **keeps `expires_at`** → `resolveSnapshot` grants
   access for `cancelled` while not expired. So that customer keeps the trial
   they were given, to the day it was going to end, and then meets the wall at
   real prices. Nobody is charged and nobody is cut off early.
   `POST /api/billing/cancel-trial` reaches the same end from inside the app and
   is deliberately un-flag-gated for exactly this rollback.

   Audit with:
   ```sql
   select s.user_id, p.email, s.plan, s.amount / 100.0 as naira,
          s.paystack_subscription_code, s.expires_at
   from public.subscriptions s
   left join public.profiles p on p.id = s.user_id
   where s.status = 'trialing'
   order by s.started_at desc;
   ```
   Each row needs its Paystack subscription disabled by hand, or that customer
   is billed at a price we do not sell.

   **DONE 2026-09-11, and the audit query now returns the same one row with
   nothing left to do to it.** `SUB_zogd3gidljj5h3n` was disabled at Paystack
   (`POST /subscription/disable`) and reads `non-renewing`, so the 2026-09-30
   charge will not fire. It had **0 invoices ever raised**, so that customer has
   never paid us anything and there was nothing to refund. Their access is
   untouched: the app row still reads `status: 'trialing'` with `expires_at`
   2026-09-30 intact, and `resolveSnapshot` (`subscription-access.ts:166`) maps
   `trialing` + not expired to `free_trial` — so they keep everything to the day
   it was always going to end, and then meet the wall at real prices.

   ⚠️ **The app row was NOT restamped to `cancelled`**, which is what the
   paragraph above predicts the `subscription.disable` webhook would do. Either
   it had not arrived when this was checked, or it does not fire for this
   transition. It makes no difference to the customer — `trialing` and
   `cancelled` both grant access while not expired — but **do not read
   `cancelled` as proof that a disable landed.** Read Paystack; the app row is
   not the record of it.

   The only other live subscription on the account is `SUB_9zh3as2lfeeb1th`, the
   founder's own ₦8,000/mo row, sitting in `attention` (Paystack cannot charge
   the card). Left alone deliberately.
2. **`POST /api/billing/cancel-trial` is deliberately NOT flag-gated**, and
   this is exactly the rollback it was written for: "an in-flight trial must
   stay cancellable after a rollback — money is on the line". Do not tidy a
   flag check into it.
3. **The funnel is retired, not deleted, and reviving it is a rewire rather
   than a flag flip.** The precondition is moving the picker, the checkout
   route's plan validation, the webhook's plan resolution and subscription
   create, `subscriptions.plan`, and the recorded amount onto
   `purchasableTiers()` at `SELLING_INTERVAL`. Recorded at both sites
   (`lib/trial-card.ts`'s header and `StartTrialPageClient`'s) rather than only
   here, because a flag flip is a dashboard action and whoever takes it reads
   the code, not this file.
4. **Nothing else forces the flag on:** `.env.example` documents it commented
   out as `false`, `isCardTrialEnabled()` requires the literal string `'true'`,
   and it is declared in `turbo.json`. So an explicit Vercel value is the only
   thing that can revive it.
5. **The 28-vs-3 day split is not drift to reconcile by picking one number.**
   `TRIAL_DAYS = 28` belongs to this retired funnel and is still load-bearing
   copy for anyone mid-trial; `TEAM_TRIAL_DAYS = 3` is the live one. They mean
   different things and must not be merged.

### The failure copy was blaming the customer, and that is fixed

`failTrialCardCharge` writes one of three reasons and the callback page
rendered the same sentence for all three: *"That card couldn't be saved for
future billing… Try a different card."* Only `card_not_reusable` is about the
customer's card. `subscription_create_failed` and `plan_unresolvable` are our
own Paystack plan config, and there "try a different card" is advice that
cannot succeed however many cards they own — it sends someone round a loop
instead of to us. Fixed regardless of the funnel's fate, because the copy is
wrong either way:

- **`classifyTrialCardFailure` is COARSE ON PURPOSE.** It crosses
  `/api/payments/verify`, which is **unauthenticated** and keyed only on a
  query-string reference, so it is an allowlist of two values rather than the
  stored reason — and `failure_detail`, which can carry a Paystack message,
  never leaves the server. The `lib/upload-failure-report.ts` posture: a string
  designed to be read by a stranger has to be safe to hand a stranger.
- **An unrecognised reason classifies as `'setup'`, never `'card'`.** A reason
  we do not know is not evidence the customer did anything wrong.
- Mutation-tested both ways: blaming every reason on the card fails 2 tests,
  and putting "try a different card" back into the setup copy fails 1.

**ANSWERED, from the founder's own query the same evening:
`subscription_create_failed`, one row, and it is the only failure on record.**
So the card was never at fault — the ₦100 charge succeeded, and Paystack
refused to create the delayed subscription against the plan code we handed it
(`PAYSTACK_PLAN_ANNUAL_NGN`, the legacy ₦800,000 Plan from 2026-08-22). That is
precisely the case the old copy got wrong, and this user is the one who read
it.

**AND THE BLAST RADIUS IS CONFINED TO THIS FUNNEL, which is the reassuring
half.** Checked rather than assumed: `TIER_PLAN_CODE_ENV_VAR` points every
sellable tier at `PAYSTACK_PLAN_{SOLO,MANAGER,LABEL}_YEARLY_NGN` — names
nothing had set before 2026-09-08, chosen for exactly this class of reason
("the newness is the safety mechanism"). Only the retired card funnel still
reads `_ANNUAL_`, so no live checkout shares the broken plan and the flag flip
closes the whole exposure. Note `_YEARLY_` is not `_ANNUAL_`: synonyms in
English, different vars here.

**What is STILL open is Paystack's own message, and it is worth reading even
though the flip makes it moot**, because it decides whether reviving the funnel
needs more than a reprice. "Plan not found" means the legacy Plan was
deactivated or is in the wrong Paystack mode — config, already handled. Anything
about `start_date` or the request body means
`buildDelayedSubscriptionPayload` itself is wrong (it sends
`toISOString()`, milliseconds included) and would fail again on any revival.
The column was truncated on the founder's phone; it is one field:

```sql
select paystack_response->>'failure_detail' as detail
from public.payments
where plan = 'trial_card' and status = 'failed'
order by created_at desc limit 1;
```

The original query, for the record — `plan_unresolvable` was nearly ruled out
before it ran, since `/api/trial/start-checkout` already 400s on an
unresolvable plan code before Paystack is touched:
```sql
select created_at, reference, status,
       paystack_response->>'failure_reason' as reason,
       paystack_response->>'failure_detail' as detail
from public.payments
where plan = 'trial_card' and status = 'failed'
order by created_at desc limit 20;
```
`card_not_reusable` means the card; `subscription_create_failed` means our
Paystack plan, with `detail` carrying Paystack's own message — and a stale or
deactivated legacy Plan, or a test/live mode mismatch, is exactly what the
reprice would have produced. Vercel logs carry the same line under
`[trial-card] charge failed`.

### Verified

3197 tests (+7 against a **measured** clean-tree baseline of 3190), `eslint .`
**byte-identical** at 3 errors / 78 warnings with zero new findings,
`tsc --noEmit` clean apart from the documented pre-existing
`confirmed-action.test.ts` errors, and `next build` green **by exit code** with
`/start-trial` and `/payment/callback` both still `○ Static`.

**Not verified:** the copy has not rendered in a browser, and it cannot be
without a failing card trial against live Paystack — which the flip removes the
ability to produce. It rests on the unit tests plus a traced read of the
callback's failure branch. **The flip itself is a Vercel dashboard change and
needs a deploy that rebuilds `apps/web`** (`NEXT_PUBLIC_*` is inlined at build
time — the documented `turbo-ignore` trap), so confirm `/start-trial` bounces to
the dashboard before believing it took.


## Monthly is the price, yearly is arithmetic (#580, activated 2026-09-11)

Founder call: *"make the pricing monthly not yearly any more then calculate the
yearly based off"*, at **₦5,000 / ₦22,000 / ₦50,000 per month**. This reverses
the annual-only shape from two days earlier (see "Annual only, at new prices"
above) and is roughly a **12× reprice per customer**, confirmed explicitly when
the three figures turned out to be the previous pass's *yearly* prices.

**The shape is the enforcement, and it is the inverse of the one it replaces.**
A tier declares `monthlyPrice` and nothing else; `getTierPrice` multiplies by
`ANNUAL_MONTHS_BILLED` (10) for the yearly figure. There is exactly one
multiplication and nowhere else a yearly number can enter the system — where the
annual-only pass guaranteed the same property by having no monthly field at all.
Repricing is now one number per tier and the "2 months free" badge is derived
from the same constant as the gap it describes.

### Activation — DONE 2026-09-11, and nothing here is outstanding

Six Paystack Plans minted on the **live** account and six Production env vars
set on the Vercel `urganize` project:

| Env var | Plan code | Charges | Paystack interval |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PAYSTACK_PLAN_SOLO_PER_MONTH_NGN` | `PLN_s5gl9tcxqetgu8k` | ₦5,000 | monthly |
| `PAYSTACK_PLAN_SOLO_PER_YEAR_NGN` | `PLN_62yzge8f7ra4pyv` | ₦50,000 | annually |
| `PAYSTACK_PLAN_MANAGER_PER_MONTH_NGN` | `PLN_ag8u3p0l9gu9lwr` | ₦22,000 | monthly |
| `PAYSTACK_PLAN_MANAGER_PER_YEAR_NGN` | `PLN_p0m3un66lb0mzvz` | ₦220,000 | annually |
| `PAYSTACK_PLAN_LABEL_PER_MONTH_NGN` | `PLN_9b8bkya2tjchga2` | ₦50,000 | monthly |
| `PAYSTACK_PLAN_LABEL_PER_YEAR_NGN` | `PLN_6xj3i1wweis6tka` | ₦500,000 | annually |

**No existing Plan could be reused, and the near-miss is worth knowing.** The
three minted on 2026-09-09 hold the right *amounts* — ₦5,000, ₦22,000, ₦50,000 —
at interval `annually`. A ₦5,000/**year** Plan cannot serve a ₦5,000/**month**
slot, so pointing `_PER_MONTH_` at one would have sold a year for the price of a
month. Amounts alone are never enough to identify a Plan; the interval is half
of it.

Verified end to end rather than assumed: every one of the six was cross-checked
by pulling the var back out of Vercel, resolving it at Paystack, and comparing
the Plan's `amount`/`interval`/`currency` against the kobo figure
`getTierMinorUnit` will actually send to `transaction/initialize`. All six
matched and `purchasableTiers()` resolves all three tiers as OFFERED. The DB
side was checked too — `subscriptions_plan_check` permits all three tier ids and
`subscriptions_billing_interval_check` permits both intervals, so nothing was
waiting on a migration.

⚠️ **The vars were first written SENSITIVE and then redone non-sensitive.**
`vercel env add` defaults to sensitive on this account, and a sensitive var
reads back as the literal string `[SENSITIVE]` — which makes the verification
above impossible and leaves the founder unable to read the codes in the
dashboard. `--no-sensitive` is the flag. A plan code is not a credential; it
identifies a Plan and authorises nothing. Match the 2026-09-09 vars, which are
non-sensitive for the same reason.

### ⚠️ A correction: "no deploy" is wrong, and it is written into the code

`billing-plans.ts` said *"Set the var and the tier starts being offered with no
deploy"* and called the order of operations "unnecessary". **Vercel snapshots
env vars per deployment**, so a var set after a build does not reach the running
one — production had to be rebuilt before any of the six existed as far as the
app was concerned. That comment is corrected in place.

What the fresh-var-name guarantee actually buys is still real and still worth
the awkward names: shipping the code before minting the Plans **withholds the
tier** instead of charging a stale Plan. That is a guarantee about the failure
MODE, not about deployment mechanics, and the two were conflated.

The rebuild was a `vercel redeploy` of the live production deployment — same
commit `cfe29af`, `builtAt` 20:38 → 23:47 — so no new code shipped, only a fresh
env snapshot. `/api/version` is the cheapest way to confirm one landed.

### The changelog question, left open deliberately

**#580 took no ledger entry and no version bump**, on the recorded reasoning that
a pricing *display* change counts as marketing under the app-only scope rule
(the 2026-08-16 precedent). Production is still v1.41.0.

That was a defensible call at merge, when nothing was purchasable. It is worth a
second look now that activation has landed, because what changed in the app is
not only display: **a monthly option a customer can actually buy now exists on
the wall, and did not before.** By the EPK precedent the entry lands at the flip,
which is this. Flagged rather than decided — minting Plans is not a licence to
mint a version number, and this file already records how perishable a version
bump is when several sessions hold a claim on one.

### Not verified

**No card has been charged and the wall has not been seen.**
`purchasableTiers()` is exposed only through `/api/subscription-status`, which
needs a session, so the chain is proven as far as "the env var resolves to a
correctly priced Plan" and no further. The manual pass is: open the wall, confirm
three cards and a monthly/yearly toggle, buy Solo monthly, confirm Paystack
quotes ₦5,000 and `subscriptions.billing_interval` reads `monthly`.

## The pricing cards are uniform, and the CTA is "Try Urganize" (2026-09-11)

Two founder asks on the marketing site, in one pass. **No migration, no flag, no
API change, no test change** — and **no changelog entry or version bump**, since
everything a user sees here is `apps/homepage`, which the app-only scope rule
excludes. Production stays at v1.41.0.

**The highlight was the leftover half of the badge removal earlier the same
day.** That pass took the "Most teams" label off both marketing surfaces and
deliberately left `tier.recommended`, whose own doc comment recorded what it
still did: *"leaving this flag to do elevation and CTA emphasis only."* The
elevation is what got reported ("one has a highlight around the border"). It was
exactly **three conditional expressions**, all keyed on that flag — a card
border, a background tint, and the CTA fill. Confirmed by grep: no scale, ring,
shadow, z-index or negative margin anywhere, so the highlight was only ever
colour.

**Five things worth knowing before editing this:**

1. **THE MARKETING SITE NO LONGER READS `tier.recommended` AT ALL, AND THE FLAG
   IS NOT DORMANT.** It stays in `packages/pricing` because `apps/web`'s
   `TierPlanPicker` still renders its badge on the upgrade wall — a separate
   surface and a separate founder call, confirmed again here — and because
   `entitlements.test.ts` pins it to exactly `['solo']`. So the flag is live
   somewhere else, and reaching for it to re-emphasise a marketing card reopens
   what was just closed. Its doc comment now leads with that.
2. **THE CTA CHOICE IS FILLED, AND IT WAS A CHOICE RATHER THAN A DELETION.** The
   two branches differed in box model — the non-recommended one added its own
   `border` — so uniform meant picking one, not dropping a ternary. Filled won
   because `TrialButton` (the site's one primary ask, twelve mounts) and the
   header pill both carry those exact three classes, so it is the site's CTA
   look rather than a per-tier emphasis; the other branch is explicitly the
   de-emphasised treatment, and demoting all three to it would have left
   `/pricing` with **no filled CTA at all** — quieter than today, which is more
   than "uniform" asks for. `TrialButton`'s drop shadow was deliberately not
   taken with it; three shadowed buttons in one card row is a different change.
3. **The interval toggle is deliberately untouched.** Its selected Monthly /
   Yearly pill is a fill, and that is selection feedback — making it uniform
   would mean you cannot tell which interval you are looking at. The founder's
   words point at the cards anyway: the card's was literally
   `border-[var(--marketing-accent)]/50`, a border, where the toggle's is a
   fill. `/pricing`'s hero eyebrow pill (`accent/30`) is likewise unrelated.
4. **THE CTA STRING WAS `"Start free"`, NOT "Start free trial"** — three places
   in this file plus a comment in `PricingPageClient` claimed otherwise, and all
   of them were wrong before this change. Only **three** places render the
   label: `TrialButton.tsx` (covering 12 of the 15 mounts), the hand-rolled
   header pill, and the tier card's `selfServe` ternary.
5. **`start_trial_click` and every `data-location` value are IDENTIFIERS and did
   not move** — the rollout-rename rule that rendered copy changes and
   identifiers do not. They carry GA history, and `LandingAnalytics` returns
   **early and silently** on a mismatch, so breaking one is invisible rather
   than loud. The label and the tracking attribute are fully decoupled: nothing
   derives the event or the location from the button text.

- **The longer label had to pay for itself in the header.** "Try Urganize" costs
  about 20px more than "Start free", and at 375px that row had roughly 15px
  spare — logo (56.9px: a 13px-tall render of a 7726x1766 wordmark) plus
  "Product" plus the CTA plus the theme toggle, with "Log in" already stepped
  aside, against the 327px left once `px-6` is off both sides. So the gaps
  tighten below `sm` only (outer 24 to 12, inner 16 to 12), which gives back the
  same 20px. **Nothing above `sm` changes and nothing wide changes**, because
  with `justify-between` a gap is only a floor — it binds at exactly the tight
  widths and nowhere else. A control added to that row means re-measuring.
- **Left alone deliberately, flagged rather than widened:** three places say
  "Start free" as prose describing the offer rather than as the ask — the
  pricing strip's sub-paragraph, `/pricing`'s hero lead, and
  `docs/store-listing.md` (a never-submitted draft, whose stated `1,776
  characters.` count would need redoing). The request said "CTA", and prose
  describing an offer does not contradict a button that performs it.
- **Verified:** 3200 tests (unchanged — nothing here is testable, and
  `apps/homepage` has no test runner at all), `eslint .` at the exact measured
  baselines in both apps (3 errors / 78 warnings in `apps/web`, 0 / 2 in
  `apps/homepage`) with **zero** new findings, and `next build` green **by exit
  code** with `/` and `/pricing` still `○ Static`. **The proof is in the emitted
  HTML rather than the source**, this repo's habit for any copy or CSS change:
  `uniq -c` over the card wrappers on both surfaces reports **3 against a single
  class string**, and the same over the three card CTAs reports **3 against one
  string** — that is the uniformity, measured. All 21 tracked CTA anchors across
  six pages carry the new label, with the tracking-attribute count unchanged,
  and **zero** anchors still read "Start free". In the compiled CSS the accent
  token now appears at 10% and 30% alpha and **no `/50` rule exists at all**,
  because nothing references it any more.
- **A probe error of my own, since the shape recurs:** the first CSS check
  reported zero references to every class and nearly sent me chasing a
  non-existent bug — it globbed `.next/static/css/`, a directory this build does
  not produce. The stylesheet is at `.next/static/chunks/*.css`, the same place
  `apps/web` keeps it.
- **Not verified:** nothing has rendered in a browser — this sandbox has no
  route to either domain. The header at 375px in particular is arithmetic, not a
  measurement, so it is the one thing worth a real look. Both themes are covered
  by construction rather than by checking: uniformity here comes from deleting
  the conditional, not from matching two colours, so the three cards carry one
  identical class string and cannot differ per palette.
