## The textile character layer (2026-09-05; LIVE 2026-09-07 as v1.27.0)

**Back-filled 2026-09-07, and LIVE the same day.** Behind
`NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_TEXTILE` (#498, `b420acc`), which was **flipped on in
production hours after this section was written** and shipped as v1.27.0 —
see the two paragraphs below for what has and has not been seen with it on.
(This sentence said "has never been flipped" until the flip; corrected rather
than left contradicting the heading directly above it.)

**Its sibling pass is a SEPARATE section: "The house icon set" below** (#500,
`c064a00`), which ships **unflagged and is live**. They were built the same day
in the same voice and are deliberately independent — read that section's first
paragraph for why tying the icons to this flag would have been the wrong call.
Neither had a working-notes section until now; both were written from the code
rather than the commit messages, and where the two disagreed the code won.

**What this layer is:** the woven character of the founder's textile reference
— ikat weaves, Kuba cloth, gold embroidery on oxblood, Adinkra tooth borders —
applied as a class on `<html>` in `app/layout.tsx`, **without touching the
palette**. That was the finding that made it cheap: the reference board and the
Brand Bible are already the same family (ink ground, cream thread, sage and
forest), and `--status-warning` is literally the gold-thread/umber pair. What was
missing was not colour but MATERIAL — weave, edge treatment, pattern instead of
flat digital fill.

### Six things worth knowing before editing the ornament

1. **EVERY ORNAMENT COLOUR DERIVES FROM AN EXISTING TOKEN AT LOW ALPHA**
   (`--color-stroke`, `--color-status-warning`), and that is three guarantees at
   once rather than a style preference: nothing new enters the palette, **ornament
   can never be mistaken for state**, and both themes are covered for free by the
   same cascade that already flips those tokens. The `--urg-*` tokens are
   declared unconditionally (a few custom properties, cheap) and only ever
   CONSUMED under `.urg-textile`, which is what keeps flag-off byte-identical.
   **The alphas are NOT shared between themes** — ink-on-cream reads visibly
   heavier than cream-on-ink at equal opacity, so `html[data-theme='light']`
   carries its own set at roughly 0.55–0.7×, tuned against both real grounds
   rather than derived.
2. **BOTH HOOKS ALREADY EXISTED, and finding them is why this is CSS-only.**
   `body::before` was already a fixed inset hairline — the framed-cartouche motif
   hiding in plain sight — and gains an inner rule (`outline` with a NEGATIVE
   offset draws inward) plus corner ticks. `body::after` was already an ambient
   texture, but a 36px graph-paper grid **hardcoded to
   `rgba(255,255,255,…)`, which means the app's only texture has been invisible
   in paper mode for as long as it has existed**. Routing it through
   `--color-stroke` fixes that and makes it cloth: weft at 3px, warp at 4px,
   twill at 45° and 6px. The near-coprime pitches are deliberate — 36/36 locked
   into a visible checkerboard, and that difference is the difference between
   "spreadsheet" and "woven". The old grid rule is left exactly as it is,
   because it is the flag-off baseline.
3. **AN SVG `data:` URI IN `background-image` CANNOT READ CSS CUSTOM
   PROPERTIES**, so it can never be theme-aware. Where a motif is too complex for
   gradients (the tooth border, the Kuba glyph) the **SHAPE
   comes from an SVG `mask-image` and the COLOUR from a token via
   `background-color`**. Both `-webkit-` and unprefixed properties are required;
   the floor is iOS 15.4, which the app already hard-requires because Next 16's
   framework chunk uses `Object.hasOwn`.
4. **Ornament sits at `z-index: 0` behind `.app-layout` (`z-index: 1`), which
   has no background of its own.** So it shows through transparent regions, is
   occluded by any opaque card, and **can never render over text** — the
   per-token contrast budget is preserved by construction rather than by
   checking. `position: fixed` for the same reason the grid it replaces was: the
   grain reads as the surface the app is printed ON, not a pattern that scrolls.
5. **`.urg-above` exists instead of Tailwind `relative z-[1]`, and that is not
   fussiness.** A `z-index` establishes a stacking context, and with the flag OFF
   those pages must keep exactly the stacking they have today — so the marker
   class is completely inert until the layer is switched on. Same reasoning
   one level up: the ~15 copy-pasted blur-blob decorations (redeem, invite
   accept, payment callback, settings, curator join, the artist-name gate and
   both password pages) are **hidden by one `.urg-textile .urg-blob { display:
   none }` rule rather than deleted**, because soft glowing gradients are the
   opposite aesthetic to woven cloth and running both reads as two design
   systems sharing a page — but flag-off has to stay identical. **If this layer
   is ever made permanent, that is the moment to delete the blob divs and that
   rule together.**
6. **Three tiers, and the tier decides where a motif may go.** Tier 1 is the
   ambient grain on `body`'s pseudo-elements. Tier 2 is opt-in structural
   utilities (`urg-cartouche`, `urg-rule-teeth`) applied through
   the app's **shared className constants rather than per component**, which is
   why a handful of edits reach most surfaces — `components/settings/panelClass.ts`
   is the widest seam. Tier 3 is the loud one (`urg-ground-sunburst`,
   `urg-ground-ikat`, `urg-glyph-kuba`), reserved for surfaces with no dense
   content to compete with — the entrances, the public share pages, the
   first-release reveal — and always applied to a `pointer-events: none`
   absolutely-positioned CHILD, never the page element, so nothing can sit
   between a user and a control.

### Smaller ornament decisions

- **Settings gets teeth on its divider, not a keyline.** `panelClass` uses
  `urg-rule-teeth` and deliberately not `urg-cartouche`, because a keyline would
  re-draw the box the 2026-07-23 founder call removed for reading as plastic.
  The `relative` the tooth border needs as a positioning context was already
  there.
- **The empty state's dashed border becomes solid with teeth.** A dashed border
  is the universal "nothing here yet"; a finished woven edge is the right note
  for a state that is inviting the first action rather than apologising for a
  gap.
- **The cartouche uses `outline`, not a second pseudo-element or an inset
  shadow.** `body` has only `::before` and `::after` and both are spoken for; an
  inset shadow fills a band from the edge and cannot draw a hairline at an
  offset. On the element utilities it also costs no pseudo-element, so it never
  fights a component that already uses one, and it inherits the corner radius.
- **The frame's inner rule and ticks tighten with it below 768px**, because the
  frame itself goes to `inset: 10px` there and they would otherwise collide with
  the border on a phone.
- **Nothing in the layer animates**, so the `prefers-reduced-motion` clamp
  needed no additions.
- **`html` still carries no `overflow` property**, so the #318/#321 sticky
  landmine is untouched. Do not add one here.
- **The public islands get the richest treatment and break two of this layer's
  own rules on purpose** (`.epk-island`, `.credits-island`, `.capture-island`,
  `.kit-island`): the thread colours are HARDCODED cream rather than tokenised,
  because those islands deliberately do not participate in the theme cascade and
  a themed token would be the one thing on them that could flip; and the texture
  goes on `background-image` of the island element itself, because each page sets
  only `backgroundColor` inline and `::before`/`::after` stay free for the page
  components. `.kit-island` was folded in during the #499/#500 merge — the
  standing press kit is the successor to the EPK surface this rule was written
  for, and leaving it out would have given the new kit less character than the
  thing it replaced.
- **NONE OF IT PRINTS, and that reset is required rather than tidy (2026-09-07).**
  The `@media print` block far above redefines the island's own variables so
  every colour follows without a single print-specific override in the component
  — the kit island's ground goes white and its text goes ink. The ornament is the
  one thing that CANNOT follow, because its threads are hardcoded cream by the
  bullet above, so on a white sheet the grain is invisible and the gold wash is a
  faint yellow band across the top. A second `@media print` sets
  `background-image: none` on all four, placed immediately after the rule it
  corrects rather than in that block 1,600 lines earlier, so a reader editing one
  sees the other. Mostly belt-and-braces — `print-color-adjust` is `economy` by
  default, so browsers already drop backgrounds — but "Print backgrounds" is a
  checkbox in every print dialog, and the press kit is the one page in this
  product designed to be printed.

### The selvedge motif was built and then deleted (2026-09-07)

**`.urg-selvedge` had ZERO consumers** — fully implemented (mask, uneven 24px
tile, both prefixes) and applied by no component, found by grepping for each
utility's consumers rather than trusting the list of them. It was recorded
rather than removed at the time, because deleting a motif is a design call and
not a cleanup; the founder made that call the same day and it is gone.

**Worth knowing if a frayed bottom edge is ever wanted again:** it is one block
in git history, and the technique it used is the same one `.urg-rule-teeth`
still uses (SVG `mask-image` for the shape, a token via `background-color` for
the colour). What made it a real motif rather than a variant of the teeth is the
UNEVEN path on a wider 24px tile, so it reads as a cut edge instead of a
pattern. The word survives once in `globals.css`, in the island-pages comment
("the brocade selvedge a bolt of cloth carries") — that is prose describing the
live gold header band, not a reference to this utility.

### Status, and what was never verified

**LIVE as of 2026-09-07 (v1.27.0)** — `NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_TEXTILE=true` on the
Vercel `Web` project, with the version bump as the commit that rebuilt
`apps/web` and inlined it (a `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` value is read at build time, so
setting the variable alone changes nothing until something rebuilds). The ledger
entry landed at the flip rather than at merge, per the EPK precedent.

**The order was env var first, then the rebuild**, and it matters: merged the
other way round, the rebuild carries the flag still false and the variable then
sits inert until the next commit — the trap recorded on the EP/album flip.

**SEEN IN PRODUCTION, in the default dark theme (founder, 2026-09-07):** the
grain, the frame and the entrance ray fan all render as intended on the
authenticated app. So the layer shipped on a green build and a compiled-CSS
check, and was confirmed by eye immediately after — which is what closes the
gap the paragraph below names, for dark mode.

**THE AMBIENT WEAVE WAS REACHING NONE OF THE CONTENT AREA, found 2026-09-07 by
rendering paper mode locally with the flag on.** The layer sits on `body::after`
at `z-index: 0` and `.app-layout` sits at `1`, so anything inside it with an
opaque background covers it entirely — and **every** page wrapper carried
`bg-bg-base`: auth, onboarding, locked, redeem, start-trial, the `<main>` on
dashboard/settings/admin, TeamWall, CuratorShell, ArtistNameGate and four
skeletons, 24 sites in 21 files. Measured on `/auth` at 1280px: the wrapper
spanned x=38.4 to 1241.6, so the grain and the frame showed only in the ~38px
margins either side. Proved rather than inferred — cranking the weave to bright
red at 90% still rendered a flat field, and the same 340x170 clip of empty field
went **571 bytes (flat) to 13,142 light / 24,821 dark** once the wrappers were
made transparent.

**What was visible all along, and why "texture is showing" was true anyway:** the
cartouche frame and corner ticks live in those margins, and every Tier 3 moment
(the ray fans, the ikat and sunburst grounds) is a child element INSIDE the
wrapper, so it paints above it. The two loudest parts worked; the subtlest and
most pervasive one did not arrive.

`body` already carries `bg-bg-base`, and neither `.app-body` nor `.app-layout`
sets a background, so removing it from a wrapper **changes no colour** in either
theme or either flag state — verified: with the flag OFF the same clip is 571
bytes before and after, because the pre-textile grid it uncovers is
`rgba(255,255,255,0.018)` at `opacity: 0.18`, an effective 0.3% and
sub-perceptible. **`lib/textile-ground-guard.test.ts` holds the rule**, because
the symptom is ornament that silently does not arrive rather than anything that
looks broken.

**That guard was wrong twice before it was right, and both mistakes are worth
knowing.** It stripped block comments before line comments, so the line comment
at `WorkspaceView.tsx:923` mentioning the legacy `/plan/*` route group opened a
comment the non-greedy regex closed 300 lines later — eating 431 real lines and
**hiding three of the 24 offenders while passing**. The counting check then
written to catch that cried wolf on `AdminNav.tsx` and `AdminPageSkeleton.tsx`,
whose comment BODIES mention `/admin/*`; a `/*` inside an already-open comment is
text, and no count of the two sequences can tell the difference. Both are gone in
favour of a single-pass scanner that also preserves newlines, so reported line
numbers are the real ones rather than indices into a stripped copy.

**PAPER MODE IS CONFIRMED IN PRODUCTION (founder, 2026-09-07), and it reads
SOFTER than dark rather than heavier** — the lower light alphas (`.02` against
dark's `.03`) did their job, so the worry this file carried about ink on cream
needs no tuning. That closes the half nobody had ever seen: the ambient ground
was hardcoded `rgba(255,255,255,…)` from the day it was written, so it had been
invisible in light theme for as long as it existed, and flag-on light mode was
its first appearance anywhere.

**THE ISLANDS ARE VERIFIED TOO, which closes this layer's last open item
(founder, 2026-09-07).** All four island classes were first rendered locally
against the real compiled stylesheet, and all four resolve the gold header wash
plus the warp/weft/twill grain, with the ground staying `rgb(13, 18, 14)` even
under a `light` root class — so the dark-lock holds, which was the likeliest
thing to have broken. Measured on empty ground beside the content column: 19,851
bytes inside the gold band and 7,312 below it, against the 571-byte flat
baseline. That pass is also what found the print gap in the bullet above, and
the before/after on one harness is the evidence for the fix. **Then the founder
printed a REAL published press kit and the sheet came back clean**, which is
what takes this past the harness: a real page, real content, real cover art, and
the print reset doing its job on paper rather than under emulated media.

**Read what that does and does not settle.** It confirms `/k/{slug}` — a real
kit, at print and therefore on screen — and it says nothing about `/credits/` or
`/capture/`, which have their own content and their own layouts and have still
only been seen as bare classes. Their thread colours are hardcoded cream rather
than tokenised, on purpose (those islands do not participate in the theme
cascade), so neither theme tells you anything about how they look, and the print
reset covers all four by construction rather than by having been checked on each.

**The paragraph below is the build-time record and is kept as written.**

**What the pass recorded at build time**, worth trusting because it names its
method: the eslint baseline was measured **by stashing rather than assuming**
and matched exactly; the build was green in BOTH flag states with `/auth`,
`/onboarding`, `/settings` and `/locked` all still `○ Static` and the auth form
still server-rendered; and **the compiled CSS was checked rather than the
source**, which is this repo's standing habit for anything CSS-dependent and
the only way to catch a minifier collapsing a declaration.

**Not verified at build time:** the authenticated surfaces and the public island
pages need a live session and a real share token, which this sandbox has neither
of. Both manual passes it was waiting on have since been done in production and
are recorded above — paper mode, where the ambient texture had been invisible
since it was written, and a real published press kit at print. `/credits/` and
`/capture/` are the remainder, and only because nobody has had reason to open
one.

## The house icon set (2026-09-05, live)

**Back-filled 2026-09-07** (#500, `c064a00`). Thirty of the app's icons are
Urganize's own marks, drawn in the Adinkra/Kuba voice of the brand's textile
reference; the other 68 are still lucide, pulled to the house stroke weight by
one CSS rule.

**It ships UNFLAGGED, and that is the decision to understand first.** It was
built the same day as the textile ornament layer above, in the same voice, and
is deliberately NOT gated by `NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_TEXTILE`: an icon swap at
identical viewBox and sizing changes no layout and no behaviour, so there is
nothing for a flag to protect — while tying it to a flag that has never been
flipped would have left the long tail mismatched indefinitely, since the
stroke-weight normalizer would have been dark too. Revert is `git revert`.

Not a scope expansion and no migration. It extends the founder's 2026-07-23
call, which pulled stock lucide out of the topbar for reading like "another
SaaS" — `BrandIcons.tsx`'s eleven music-coded marks were the pilot, and this is
the same decision applied to the icons a user actually touches.

### The design was settled by evidence, and both rejections are worth keeping

**Three directions were drawn and compared at REAL ICON SIZE before any of them
shipped**, which is the part that matters: two lost, and they lost for reasons
that would repeat.

- **"Hand-cut"** (deliberate wobble, squared terminals) was **invisible at
  24px**. Irregularity that reads across a metre of cloth does not survive a
  16px glyph. Do not reach for it again.
- **"House line"** (lucide's forms at stroke 1.8) was **indistinguishable from
  what it replaced** — the right weight, no character.

What survived is a carved-stamp voice, reduced in `components/icons/house.tsx`
to four rules: **contain it** (cut a vessel around the concept — a diamond, a
ring, an arch; the strongest Adinkra signal, and what makes `Check` and `Search`
read as marks rather than as UI), **nest it** (concentric repeats, echoing the
mudcloth panels), **four elements maximum**, and **symmetry wherever the meaning
allows** (stamps are symmetric; break it only for directional glyphs).

Stroke is **1.6 on structural geometry and 1.8 on the interior gesture** that
carries the meaning, so the container recedes and the meaning reads first. Round
caps only on interior gestures — structure is cut square.

### Six things worth knowing before adding or changing an icon

1. **THE FOUR-ELEMENT CEILING IS A HARD ONE, and a test enforces it.** The two
   glyphs that failed the comparison sheet failed by carrying five and six
   shapes: at 16px anything more turns to mud. `lib/icons-registry.test.ts`
   counts the `<path|circle|rect|ellipse|line|polygon>` elements in every mark's
   body and fails on any over four, so this is a finding held in place rather
   than a preference written down.
2. **LEGIBILITY OUTRANKS CHARACTER, and it decided real marks.** `X` is a single
   crossed path whose only concession to the voice is a square terminal, and the
   chevrons are nearly plain: a dismiss control that takes a beat to recognise
   is a worse control however handsome the mark. `Loader2` is one arc, because
   it is used with `animate-spin` at 46 call sites — the most-seen glyph in the
   app — so it stays the simplest thing in the file, with nothing to blur when
   it rotates. **Four marks were also redrawn after the first render rather than
   defended:** `Users` read as a rendering glitch, `Inbox` as a photo frame,
   `BellRing` had a stub on top, and `Loader2`'s original ghost arc added
   nothing to something judged in motion.
3. **IT IS A SHIM, not 130 hand-edited import lists.** 98 distinct icons are
   imported across ~130 files, most of them mixing covered and uncovered names,
   so everything comes from `components/icons` and **a call site only ever
   changes its import PATH** — no import splitting, no per-file judgement about
   which set a name belongs to, and no way to get that judgement wrong. Adding
   an icon means adding it to the passthrough list. Promoting one means drawing
   it in `house.tsx` and deleting it from that list, with the export name
   unchanged, so **no call site moves.**
4. **HOUSE ICONS ARE `forwardRef` COMPONENTS MATCHING LUCIDE'S EXACT TYPE, and
   that is a build requirement rather than a style.** `AdminHubClient` holds
   `{ label, icon }` rows of both kinds, and TypeScript infers the array's type
   from the FIRST entry — a plain function component and a
   `ForwardRefExoticComponent` are not assignable to one another, so the build
   failed on the first mixed array it met. Patching that one call site would
   have moved the problem, not solved it. Every mark therefore goes through one
   `icon()` factory, which also fixes `viewBox="0 0 24 24"`, `fill="none"`,
   `stroke="currentColor"`, `aria-hidden` and `focusable="false"` in a single
   place; the children are captured at module scope rather than rebuilt per
   render.
5. **THE TWO SETS STOP CLASHING THROUGH ONE CSS RULE**, not because 98 marks
   were redrawn. `.lucide { stroke-width: 1.7 }` in `globals.css` reaches the
   whole long tail, and it works for a specific reason: **lucide emits
   `stroke-width` as a PRESENTATION ATTRIBUTE** (verified in `node_modules` —
   its `defaultAttributes` carries `strokeWidth: 2`), and CSS beats presentation
   attributes in the cascade regardless of specificity. It also emits
   `class="lucide lucide-<name>"`, which is the hook. **The consequence to know:
   a call site passing `strokeWidth` arrives as an attribute too, so this rule
   overrides it** — a genuine per-icon override needs a Tailwind arbitrary class
   (`[stroke-width:2.4]`), never the prop. And the rule is deliberately NOT
   scoped under `.urg-textile`, or the long tail would mismatch until that flag
   flips.
6. **`packages/ui` is deliberately untouched.** It cannot import from
   `apps/web`, so its primitives keep whatever they already use. A shared
   primitive that wants a house mark needs the set moved into the package first,
   which is a bigger change than it looks.

### Scope was chosen on measured usage, not taste

Of the 98 icons, **48 appear in exactly one file.** The **30** carrying the
visible chrome are drawn — grouped in `house.tsx` as structure and status,
objects and actions, music and motion, direction, and people/AI/finding. The
**68** on surfaces almost nobody opens stay lucide, several of which lucide
already draws better than we would, and all of which the normalizer above pulls
into the same family. Hand-cutting 68 marks for admin tables and rare settings
rows would have been the expensive half of the work for the invisible half of
the benefit.

### The guard, and why it scans source

`lib/icons-registry.test.ts` is four cases, all reading the real files rather
than asserting a fixed list — the `tool-registry.test.ts` approach, for the same
reason: **a fixed list catches a rename and not a new file breaking the rule.**
It fails if

1. any file imports from `lucide-react` directly (which would reintroduce the
   stroke mismatch the shim exists to remove — the shim itself is exempted),
2. a name imported from the shim is not exported by it (type-only exports are
   skipped, since they are erased at runtime and `next build` type-checks
   those),
3. a house mark is not a 24-viewBox `currentColor` SVG with a `displayName`
   matching its export — and it asserts the count is exactly 30, so a deletion
   is a decision rather than a drift, and asserts the mark is an OBJECT rather
   than a function, which is what pins point 4 above, or
4. any mark exceeds the four-element ceiling.

Comments are stripped before matching, and **that was mutation-tested: a comment
merely MENTIONING `lucide-react` must not trip the rule, and does not.**

### One thing the code said and the commit message did not

**The `.lucide` rule's own comment undercounted the long tail, twice** — "the
other 66" and "all 66 at once" — where the shim's own comment and the export
list both say 68 (30 + 68 = 98). Corrected in place while writing this section:
a comment-only fix, no behaviour. A wrong count sitting beside the rule it
describes is exactly the drift this file exists to catch — though note it was
wrong in the direction that matters least, since the rule reaches every lucide
glyph regardless of how many the comment thinks there are.

### Status and verification

**Live and unflagged since 2026-09-05.** No changelog entry, and that is
deliberate rather than an omission: the swap is invisible by design — identical
geometry, identical sizing, no layout change — so an entry announcing it would
describe nothing a user could see.

**What the pass recorded at build time:** 2555 tests passing including four
structural guards, **all four mutation-tested**; eslint identical to the
clean-main baseline (82 problems, 3 errors, 79 warnings), measured by checking
out `main` in place rather than assumed; `next build` green with `/auth`,
`/dashboard`, `/onboarding` and `/settings` all still `○ Static`; and the
compiled CSS confirmed to carry `.lucide{stroke-width:1.7px}` after
minification. It was **merged with #499 (standing press kits) mid-review**,
which forced two follow-ups that were necessary rather than optional: the 97
files that PR brought in still imported lucide directly (the registry guard
caught it by design, and the re-run had to widen to the double-quoted import
sources #499 introduced), and `.kit-island` was folded into the textile island
ornament. Re-run while writing this section: the icon guard's 4 cases pass and
the full suite is green.

**Not verified, then or now:** most of the 30 marks live on authenticated
surfaces this sandbox cannot reach. The set was reviewed at 30px and 16px on a
rendered sheet, and `Mail` was confirmed live on `/auth` — which is not the same
as seeing the chrome. Worth one pass through the workspace, a task pop-up and
Settings.

## Standing press kits (2026-09-05, LIVE as v1.24.0)

**This section was back-filled 2026-09-07 and is the surface's first entry in
this file.** It shipped, went live and took two follow-up releases with no
working-notes section at all — only an `.env.example` block — the same failure
mode already flagged here for Web Push, the mobile shell, the team brief and
`workspace-summary.ts`. Written from the code rather than reconstructed from the
commit message; where the two disagree, the code won. The fullest account of the
build itself is still `3b3e002`'s commit message.

**What it is:** one standing press kit per ARTIST at one permanent public link
(`/k/{slug}`), kept current by the team. Twelve sections — header, bios, latest
release, music, assets, video, credits, numbers, press, live, contact, links —
each with its own status, its own history and its own hide toggle. Urganize fills
in what it already knows, an interview asks for the rest, photos carry their
photographer credit, and publishing is a deliberate act with one precondition.

**It REPLACES the release-scoped EPK** (the third sanctioned expansion,
2026-07-30, URG-196), so it is not a twentieth expansion of its own — it is the
same sanctioned surface, re-shaped after the release-scoped version turned out to
answer the wrong question. `lib/epk-server.ts` assembles a kit live from ONE
release on every request, so it goes stale the moment the next release lands and
an artist accumulates one link per release. A press kit is not a release
artifact; it is a standing document about an artist that press, editors and
bookers hold one permanent link to. **What makes it legal against Principle 1 is
the 2026-08-30 amendment**: the kit hangs off the ARTIST, not a release, which is
the same move Events made. It is the third object beside Release and Show, and it
reuses the artist-scoped access rule rather than growing one.

**Flag:** `NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_PRESS_KITS` (default `false`, **on in
production**). Gates the side menu entry, the topbar icon, the last tab in the
mobile bar, the search catalog entry, `/dashboard/press-kits` (which bounces when
off), and every one of the ten `/api/press-kits` routes (404 when off).

**Schema:** `20260905100000_press_kits.sql` — five tables, **applied in
production**. Its header argues eight load-bearing decisions and is the thing to
read before changing any of this; the four that shape everything else are
repeated below.

### Nine things worth knowing before editing this

1. **THE KIT OWNS ITS CONTENT, and that was a founder call rather than a
   shortcut.** `artists` is a name and a slug — no bio, photo, genre, socials,
   hometown or contact exists anywhere in the schema — so every field here is
   net-new rather than a duplicate. It was deliberately NOT promoted onto
   `artists`: there is no artist-profile surface to edit it from, and a half-built
   profile only one feature writes to is worse than a contained one. If a second
   consumer ever wants an artist bio, promote it THEN, with a migration and a real
   reader.
2. **DRAFT AND PUBLISHED ARE TWO COLUMNS ON ONE ROW**, not a snapshot table.
   `content` is what the team edits; `published_content` is what `/k/{slug}`
   serves. Publishing copies one to the other, so "what changed since the last
   publish" is a straight comparison and **editing a live kit cannot change the
   public page**. A null `published_content` means that section has never been
   published and the public page skips it. `publicSections` renders published
   content only, drops hidden sections (hiding one is the whole point of being
   able to) and drops empty ones (an empty heading reads as a product fault).
3. **THE SLUG IS GLOBALLY UNIQUE, and this is the ONE public page in the product
   meant to be FOUND.** Every other public surface here is `robots: noindex`
   behind an unguessable token; someone searching an artist's name plus "press
   kit" should land on this. A per-team namespace would need the team in the URL
   and would not serve that purpose, so the first team to claim a name holds it
   and a taken slug is refused at the API. Indexing is still opt-in —
   `isKitIndexable` returns true only for `public_listed`, so `link_only` and
   `public` both work for anyone holding the link and both stay out of search.
4. **`press_kit_assets` exists because `assets` CANNOT hold an artist's photo.**
   `assets_scope_check` requires every row to belong to a release or a task, and a
   standing press photo belongs to neither. Weakening that constraint would
   degrade it for every existing asset, so this follows `song_versions`, added for
   exactly the same reason: same bucket, its own path prefix, **its own size
   ceiling**. `MAX_PRESS_PHOTO_BYTES` must never alias
   `ASSET_SIZE_LIMITS.cover_art` — that number has already silently raised two
   different avatar limits (the curator photo and the workspace logo), and there
   are tests asserting it stays separate.
5. **`press_kit_section_versions` is the FIRST history table in this schema, and
   `team_brief_sections` explicitly cut one.** The brief asked for 30 days and
   one-tap restore per section, so it is built, and the deviation is recorded in
   the migration rather than left to be rediscovered. Two rules keep it from
   exploding, both pure and unit-tested: a version is written BEFORE an autosave
   overwrites content, and it **coalesces** into the newest row when that row is
   younger than five minutes and by the same person — without which an 800ms
   debounce writes a row per keystroke. `shouldCoalesceVersion` fails toward
   writing a NEW version on every uncertainty (no history, another person, an
   unreadable or future timestamp), because an extra version costs a row and a
   missing one costs somebody their words. **Pruning happens ON WRITE, never on a
   cron** — the Vercel plan caps crons at one a day and both slots are taken.
6. **`ensurePressKitAccess` reuses `decideReleaseAccess`, and cloning it would be
   the bug.** That function is named for releases and is generic in fact: it reads
   an owner id and an artist id and consults the caller's memberships and artist
   scope. A kit carries exactly those two fields and wants exactly that rule — a
   member sees the team's kits, an artist-scoped member sees only their artist's,
   a guest is read-only, a non-member gets a 404 that does not confirm existence.
   **One rule, three object types now.** It lives in `lib/press-kit-access-server.ts`
   rather than the route group's `_shared.ts` because the embedded-actions runner
   needs it too, and a lib module importing from `app/api` points the dependency
   the wrong way.
7. **`PRESS_KIT_NOT_FOUND_MESSAGE` is `'Press kit not found.'` and must never
   become `'Not found.'`** — `lib/chappi/tool-families/shared.ts`'s `isFlagGateOff`
   reads that exact string as "the feature flag is off", so the two would become
   indistinguishable and the assistant would tell a manager the feature was
   switched off when they had simply asked about somebody else's kit. That is a
   bug this repo has already shipped once, on `generate_status_update`.
8. **AUTOFILL WRITES ONLY WHILE A SECTION'S SOURCE IS STILL `'autofill'`.** The
   moment a person types into a section the PATCH flips it to `'user'`, and the
   moment UrgAns drafts one it becomes `'ai'`; either way autofill never returns
   to it. That is what makes re-running it safe **by construction rather than by
   care**, and it is the one rule `lib/press-kit-autofill.ts` exists to keep. It
   fills six of the twelve sections (`AUTOFILLABLE_SECTIONS`: header, latest
   release, music, credits, live, contact) and the credit builder reconstructs
   each entry field by field rather than spreading its input — the submissions
   table also holds an email, a phone number, a PRO affiliation, an IPI number and
   both splits, none of which belongs on a page anyone with the link can read.
9. **`press_kit_events` has a SELECT policy and no write policy.** Rows are
   written by the public page on behalf of somebody with no session, through the
   service-role client, and nothing signed in should be able to manufacture or
   erase a view record. Know what it can and cannot answer: counts, timestamps and
   per-asset downloads, but **never WHO opened the kit** — one permanent link per
   artist forecloses the per-recipient tokens that let `dj_pack_recipients` answer
   that.

### Rolling a release in, and why it is not autofill

`lib/press-kit-rollout.ts` is the answer to the six-months-later problem: autofill
runs once and refuses any section somebody has touched, which is right for a
first fill and wrong when a release has landed and the kit still points at the
last one. It differs in exactly two ways, both deliberate:

- **IT NEVER WRITES.** It returns proposals and a person accepts each one.
- **It proposes over hand-written sections too, and says so** (`handWritten` on
  each proposal), because refusing to mention a stale release would be worse than
  offering to replace a sentence somebody wrote.

The content comes from `buildSectionContent`, the same builders autofill uses —
one set, so the two can never disagree about what a release puts on a kit. It
**excludes contacts** (`ROLLABLE_SECTIONS`), because autofill fills a contact with
a blank role on purpose (the only role the product holds for a teammate is a
permission level, not a job title), so re-proposing it would offer to replace a
contact somebody completed in the interview with an incomplete one. And
`composite()` returns EMPTY when every part is empty rather than the naive `"|"`,
which is a truthy string that would give a nameless row an identity and add it
again on every roll-in.

### Smaller decisions worth not undoing

- **Publishing has ONE precondition: a reachable contact** (`canPublishKit`). A
  press kit whose reader cannot find who to email is a dead end, and it is the one
  thing the brief makes a precondition rather than a suggestion. Checked on the
  server, not only in the button.
- **Unpublishing leaves the published copy in place**, so re-publishing is not a
  re-authoring job.
- **THE EMBARGO IS A NOTICE, NOT A GATE.** A standing kit holds the bio, the
  photos and who to email; hiding all of that behind a date would break the kit for
  the ordinary reader to protect one piece of news, and a manager who wants it dark
  already has unpublish. So `embargoNotice` renders a line press are expected to
  honour, which is what an embargo means in this trade. A past date says nothing.
- **`deriveSectionStatus` has three shapes, not one**, because the sections
  genuinely differ: some are a handful of fields, some a list where any entry is
  worth having, and some a list where a half-filled entry is worse than none (a
  contact with no email, a number with no date). `assets` is decided by the photo
  count, since photos are their own table and its content is always empty.
- **Published outranks everything in `deriveKitState`:** once a kit is live it
  stays live while the team edits, because the public page is serving the last
  publish. A hidden section is a decision, not a gap, so it never holds the kit
  back.
- **`sameContent` is key-order independent**, or the editor treats a
  re-serialised object as an edit and autosaves the same values back on every
  mount.
- **Press photos are graded on ONE number, the long edge**, and reaching for
  `lib/cover-art-dsp.ts` here would be the bug rather than the shortcut: its
  second tier BLOCKS anything non-square, and most press shots are landscape, so
  it would refuse the entire input this feature exists to collect. A magazine
  running a photo at page width wants about 2000px; below roughly 1000px there is
  nothing to run. Too small still UPLOADS — the manager may have nothing better
  today, and an empty Assets section is worse than a thin one.
- **Photographer credit and usage rights are per FILE, not per kit**, because
  press cannot legally run a photo without them and different shoots have
  different photographers.
- **The interview's questions are COMPUTED from what the kit already holds**, so
  nobody is asked for something autofill found and somebody who answers half and
  comes back tomorrow is asked only about the rest. Eight per pass at most —
  more than that stops being an interview and becomes the form this exists to
  avoid. Every question is skippable and captioned with what press use it for.
- **`PostPlanKitPrompt` is OFFERED, NOT FORCED**, and renders nothing unless the
  kit exists AND the roll-in has real proposals. The moment is chosen rather than
  convenient: approving a rollout plan is when a manager has just decided a
  release is real, which is exactly when a kit pointing at last year's single is
  worth knowing about. Nobody goes looking for a press kit six weeks later.
- **`applyKitToRoster`** folds a freshly-loaded kit back into the cached roster,
  so a kit you just created or published does not sit absent or stale on the tab.
  Two rules: the ROSTER decides who is on it (a kit whose artist is not listed is
  ignored rather than added), and the roster's NAME wins over the kit's copy.

### The copy guard, and two structural guards

`lib/press-kit-copy-guard.test.ts` holds every user-facing string in this feature
(and, since 2026-09-05, the directory's) to five rules the brief states as rules
rather than preferences — **each one broke at least once during the build and was
caught by reading**: no em dash, never "ship" (a release is DELIVERED), never
"workspace", no placeholder stat or invented number or fake quote, and job titles
rather than titles borrowed from software. **Comments are exempt on purpose**:
they are the working record and hold dates, prose and the odd quotation, so
holding them to product copy rules would either gut them or teach everyone to
work around the test.

`BANNED_COPY_WORDS` / `BANNED_COPY_CHARS` / `bannedCopyInstruction()` live in
`lib/press-kits.ts` so **the model's instruction and the guard read one list** — a
house rule stated in two places is one that ends up meaning two things.

Two more guards, both scanning real source rather than asserting a fixed list, so
a NEW route violating the rule fails too:
`lib/press-kit-assets-guard.test.ts` (the asset routes' ordering, with the import
block stripped so an import of the auth helper cannot read as auth coming before
the flag) and `lib/press-kit-public-guard.test.ts` (the public page renders
published content and never the draft, is noindex unless deliberately listed,
never puts `next/image` on a signed URL, the public asset routes scope the photo
to the kit the slug resolved to and never proxy bytes, and the view beacon never
reports whether a kit exists).

### The assistant reaches it two ways

- **`presskit.draft_section`** — the embedded UrgAns action (propose → review →
  Apply). Note its registered id has **no underscore in "presskit"** while the
  object type is `press_kit`; the readable guess is wrong. It is `team_write`,
  honestly rather than by copying `release.draft_plan`'s `owner_write`, because
  every press-kit route already goes through `ensurePressKitAccess` and there is
  no owner-keyed legacy route underneath waiting to 404 a teammate.
- **Seven chat tools** in `lib/chappi/tool-families/press-kits.ts`:
  `list_press_kits`, `get_press_kit`, `create_press_kit`, `update_press_kit`,
  `write_press_kit_section`, `publish_press_kit` (confirmation-gated — it puts an
  artist's page on the public internet) and `unpublish_press_kit`.

`write_press_kit_section` and the embedded action are **not duplication**, and the
relationship is worth knowing: both import `DRAFT_ALLOWED_FIELDS` /
`isDraftableSection` from `lib/press-kit-draft.ts`, so "prose never facts" holds
on both paths — the model may write a bio, and never a number, a press quote or a
contact. The embedded one additionally owns `buildDraftMessages`,
`parseDraftOutput` and `decideDraftApply`, because it calls a model of its own and
has a draft→apply window to go stale in. The chat one composes in the transcript
and writes on assent, which IS a review step, just not a card (founder call).
`update_press_kit`'s PATCH replaces a section's `content` object, so it must
read-then-merge — the trap recorded for every sparse-looking PATCH in this
codebase.

### The retired EPK, and why its flag stays on

**`NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_EPK` now has ONE job: whether an old `/epk/[token]` link
still resolves. LEAVE IT ON.** Nothing in the app makes an EPK link any more —
the scene, its API routes and its UrgAns tools are gone — but links already sent
are sitting in press inboxes and each one renders a working page. So an old link
is never broken: `resolveEpkSuccessorPath` keeps rendering the EPK until that
artist's standing kit is **published**, and only then hands over. The old page
retires itself artist by artist as kits go live, and turning the flag off breaks
every link anyone was ever sent — that is the LAST step of the retirement rather
than part of it.

Three details of the handover:

- **It is a 307, never a 308.** A permanent redirect would be cached by the
  reader's browser forever, so unpublishing a kit would leave a journalist stuck
  on a page that had gone back to a 404 with nothing we could do about it. Same
  reasoning the release-detail stub records for its own 307.
- **`successorPathForKit` requires BOTH halves** — a slug and a publish. A kit
  with no slug has nowhere to send anyone, and an unpublished kit is a 404 the
  reader could not get out of, which is strictly worse than the page they had.
- **Every uncertainty answers null**, and null means "render the EPK". A database
  blip costs nobody their page.

Several sections above this one still describe the EPK as the press-kit mechanism
(the 2026-07-30 EPK section, the footer-pill placement history, the
scoped-header pill lists). Those are the historical record of what that surface
was and are deliberately not rewritten; this section is what is true now.

### Status and what is not recorded here

**LIVE in production**, shipped as **v1.24.0** (2026-09-05, PR #501 after the
build in #499), with two follow-ups the same week: **v1.24.1** put Press kits at
the end of the mobile bar and moved Song off it, and **v1.24.2** made the press
kits tab paint from cache while it revalidates and stopped the single-kit screen
asking the server twice. The migration is applied and the flag is on — the ledger
entry landing at all is what says so, per the EPK precedent.

**v1.26.1 (2026-09-07) cached the single-kit payload too, and the two halves are
cached DIFFERENTLY on purpose.** The roster is metadata and lives in
localStorage (`stores/usePressKitsStore.ts`, the `useNotesStore` mechanics). The
single-kit payload is memory only (`lib/press-kit-detail-cache.ts`), because
every photo in it carries a signed Supabase URL — a persisted copy would outlive
the session and hand back URLs that 403, the trap already recorded for the files,
song and capture scenes. **Its five-minute TTL is derived, not chosen:** the
server re-signs only once a URL is 80% through its hour, so a URL handed to us
can already be 2880s old, leaving a worst case of twelve minutes; five minutes
keeps the oldest one we serve at 3180s. Redo that arithmetic before raising it.
It is read PRE-PAINT (`useIsomorphicLayoutEffect`) because the map is empty on
the server, so a render-time read is a hydration mismatch and a plain effect
flashes the skeleton for a frame; and it is WRITTEN from an effect mirroring live
state rather than from `loadDetail`, which is what covers the three mutations
that update `sections` locally and never re-fetch.

**The hazard that fix had to close, and the reason to read
`canAdoptServerContent` before touching the autosave.**
`usePressKitSection`'s section-change effect early-returns on an unchanged
section id — correctly, since a changing `persistedContent` identity must not
interrupt typing. That is exactly why the plan scene is excluded from the scene
cache ("painting a cached copy of a document under live edits could overwrite
newer text with older"). So a cached body the revalidate then disagreed with
would have survived in the draft and been saved back over the server's on the
next keystroke. That effect now adopts server truth when there is nothing to
lose, and the rule fails toward KEEPING the draft: never while a save is in
flight, and never while a failed save is waiting to resend — where the save
path's own `lastFlushed` bookkeeping makes the two bodies match despite the edit
never having landed, so matching bodies alone would adopt over it.

**The build's own verification record was never written down**, and this
back-filled section deliberately does not invent one: nothing here was re-run
while writing it. What IS checkable from the repo today is that the feature
carries seven unit-tested pure modules (`press-kits`, `press-kit-autofill`,
`press-kit-rollout`, `press-kit-public`, `press-kit-draft`,
`press-kit-interview`, `press-photo`) and the three structural guards above.
If a claim about this surface matters, read the code — that is what this section
was written from.
