## The timeline becomes the release's main view (2026-09-06, flag-off)

Founder, with a phone screenshot of a scoped release (`Ohema`, MOTION 9/63):
*"Let's retire the view and let the Timeline view be the main view — it
represents how creatives think and is better and more peaceful."*

**The complaint is fair and the screenshot proves it.** Buckets ship COLLAPSED
(the 2026-06-11 default), so a release with 63 activities opened onto five
closed drawers — Catch Up (1), Due Today (1), Due This Week (9), Upcoming (43),
Done (9) — and every item on the screen was a count. Nothing on it could be
acted on without a tap.

**Not a scope expansion, no migration, no API route, no new flag.** The
timeline (2026-08-30) already existed behind `NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_TIMELINE`,
which now decides which view a release LANDS on rather than merely whether the
scene is reachable. **With the flag off every path here is byte-identical to
before.** It shipped in one commit (`6c9e23e`, PR #451), untouched since, and
**has never rendered in a browser** — which is why this merges flag-off.

### Two founder decisions taken before any code

1. **The buckets survive, one tap away.** They are a scene of their own now
   (`?scene=activities`) rather than being deleted, which is what lets him see
   the timeline on his own releases before anything is thrown away.
2. **Completion stays in the pop-up.** Tapping a timeline row already called
   `onOpenTask`, and the pop-up carries the `○` beside the title (v1.23.1), so
   this needed **no code at all** — no tick-boxes were added to timeline rows,
   which would have put a control on every dot and bar in a view chosen for
   being calm.

### Six things worth knowing before editing this

1. **THE BLOCKER, and it would have been silent.** `activitiesBanner` rendered
   only inside `TasksPanel`'s non-scene branch, and that slot carries
   `kitPromptBanner ?? testReleaseBanner ?? planBanner ?? setReleaseDateBanner`.
   Making the timeline the body would have dropped the date form, the "Draft
   the plan" card and the test-release delete exit — each the ONLY path to the
   thing it offers — while the timeline's own empty states are text with **no
   button**. A dateless release would have read "Set a release date first" with
   nothing to tap. The banner is hoisted above the body now and renders for the
   MAIN VIEW, whichever that is; it stays suppressed over the named scenes,
   because a "Draft the plan" card on top of the Metadata scene is noise.
2. **The timeline renders BARE as the main view**, not through
   `ReleaseScenePanel`. That wrapper adds a "Timeline for <release>" heading and
   a back control, both wrong on the view you land on — there is nothing to go
   back from, and the release header directly above already names the release.
   The buckets have always been chromeless for the same reason.
3. **Phases now default EXPANDED** (`collapsed[phase] ?? false`). They shipped
   collapsed, which was fine for a scene you chose to open and is exactly wrong
   for a landing view: replacing five closed drawers with four closed drawers
   would have answered nothing. The narrow week list always rendered expanded
   and needed no change — it is also the better half of this feature, and the
   one the founder's phone actually gets (grouped by week, a "This week" pill,
   overdue flagged, an unscheduled section below).
4. **The rails hide for the timeline, and that is load-bearing rather than
   cosmetic.** Its grid/list swap is a container query at 34rem; leave the two
   release rails in (220 + 24 + 24 + 220 = 488px) and a 1280px desktop hands
   the timeline ~450px, silently degrading the week GRID to the phone's
   vertical list. `hideRailsForLayout` is `panelBody !== 'activities'` now.
5. **One resolver, three consumers.** `resolvePanelBody` in `lib/scene-cache.ts`
   is what the body (WorkspaceView), the lit pill (TasksPanel) and the reserved
   layout (WorkspaceSkeleton) all read, so they cannot disagree — the drift this
   module already exists to end. It never returns null: an absent, unknown or
   flag-gated-off param all mean the main view, which is what keeps a bookmark
   to `?scene=timeline` useful after a rollback instead of blank.
   **A real drift was caught mid-build by writing it this way:** the skeleton
   first mirrored the rule as `resolveMainView() !== 'activities'`, which hides
   the rails on `?scene=activities` where the real view shows them. Both now
   evaluate the identical expression.
6. **The menu slot swapped rather than gaining an entry.** `RELEASE_MENU_ORDER`
   is a closed union pinned by tests, and `'timeline'` became `'activities'` at
   the same rank: that slot has always pointed at whichever of the two views you
   are NOT looking at. It is gated on the timeline flag either way — flag off,
   the timeline is unavailable AND the buckets are already the default, so
   neither belongs. Same for the desktop pill, which now reads "Activities".

### Smaller decisions

- **The Motion bar follows the main view**, not the bucket list. It was hidden
  "while a scene is open" on the reasoning that it describes the ACTIVITY list;
  it describes the release, the founder's screenshot leads with it, and removing
  it from the landing surface was not part of the ask.
- **"New activity" follows the main view too** — gating it on `activeScene`
  would have hidden it on `?scene=activities`, the one view it most belongs to.
- **`suppressEmptyState`** lets the timeline drop its own empty states when a
  banner above already says the same thing and carries the button. Only ever
  true as the main view; opened as a scene there is no banner, so they stay.
- **`BackToMainView`** (was `BackToActivities`) derives its label, and
  `PlanScene` carries its own copy of that control which had to move with it —
  a control promising "Activities" that hands you a week grid is a lie.

### Verified

2571 tests (13 new in `scene-cache.test.ts`), `eslint .` at **exactly** the
measured clean-tree baseline of 3 errors / 78 warnings with **zero** new
findings, `tsc --noEmit` clean apart from the documented pre-existing
`confirmed-action.test.ts` errors, and `next build` green **by exit code** in
BOTH flag states with `/auth`, `/onboarding`, `/settings` and `/dashboard` all
still `○ Static` in each. Compiled CSS checked rather than trusted from source:
the `@container (min-width:34rem)` rules driving `.tl-grid-view` /
`.tl-list-view` survive, and the skeleton's literal width classes are present —
its legend placeholders were briefly written as interpolated `w-${n}`, which
Tailwind cannot extract, so they would have rendered at zero width.
**Mutation-tested:** making `resolveMainView` ignore the flag, and making
`resolvePanelBody` stop falling back, each fail four named tests.

### NOT verified, and it is the whole risk

**Nothing has rendered in a browser, and the timeline never has.** This sandbox
cannot mint an authenticated session and has no route to app.urganize.app. The
banner hoist in particular has no unit test and cannot have one — this repo has
no component tests (node environment, no jsdom) — so it rests on a traced read
of the JSX. Do NOT try to prove the flag state by grepping the client bundle:
both ternary branches compile in, a false positive this file records five times.

### Activation

Merged with the flag OFF, so nothing changes for anyone at merge. Flip
`NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_TIMELINE=true` on the Vercel `Web` project with a commit
that touches `apps/web` (the `turbo-ignore` trap); the ledger entry and version
bump land **at the flip, not at merge** — the EPK precedent, and the right call
for a view no one has seen.

**Manual pass at the flip, which is the only real verification:** open a real
release and check the week list on a phone and the grid on desktop; a DATELESS
release still offers the date form; a PLAN-LESS one still offers "Draft the
plan"; a TEST release still offers its delete exit; tap an activity and tick it
off in the pop-up; switch to Activities from the menu and back.

## UrgAns learns the rest of the product (2026-09-07)

Founder: *"Update the AI UrgAns about all the new features in Urganize and it
should be able to do agentic actions on all of them."*

**Not a scope expansion, no migration, no new flag, and nothing that reaches a
user until the surface it serves is itself switched on.** Every new tool
inherits its feature's existing flag through `isFlagGateOff`, so a switched-off
surface stays politely unavailable. Revert is `git revert`.

The registry goes **48 → 91 tools**, and the capability list in `ROLE` finally
names all of them.

### The root cause is a hand-maintained list nothing checked

`ROLE` in `lib/chappi/system-prompt.ts` is a prose list of every tool, grouped
into labelled families. **The model's entire idea of what this product can do
comes from that block** — a tool absent from it is never reached for even
though its schema is still sent on every turn. Nothing generated it and nothing
verified it, so it fell three months behind: shows, press kits, the roster, the
directory, cover art, capture and credits were all invisible. Ask UrgAns "what
is Dorian's set for Friday" and it had no concept of a show.

**`system-prompt.test.ts` now asserts both directions** — every registered tool
name appears in `ROLE`, and `ROLE` names no tool that is not registered. That
is the house's registry-invariant pattern, and it ends the drift class rather
than this instance of it: the next family cannot be added without the model
being told. Mutation-tested by deleting one name from the prose.

### Six new families, and one bug the guard found

`shows.ts` (14), `press-kits.ts` (7), `artists.ts` (5), `files.ts` (3),
`capture.ts` (4), `directory.ts` (6), plus four into existing families
(`archive_release`, and the three credits tools) and an `isTest` parameter on
`create_release`.

**Verb-shaped, not one per endpoint.** Sixteen event routes became fourteen
tools because `get_show` answers the whole question in one read: the show, its
run of show, every setlist with its running total against the slot, and who
has the pack. A tool per route would have made the model chain four calls to
answer "is Friday's set going to overrun".

**A second guard checks the flag-off contract**, and its first honest run found
a real pre-existing bug: `generate_status_update` was reporting an ownership
404 as "that feature isn't enabled", so a manager asking about someone else's
release was told the status generator was switched off. It also surfaced that
**thirteen routes across five surfaces spell the flag-gate body without a
period** (`'Not found'`), so `isFlagGateOff` now accepts both spellings —
fixed in the one place that reads the contract rather than in thirteen routes.

### Seven things worth knowing before adding to this

1. **`remove_setlist_item`, not `delete_setlist_item`, and the name is the
   point.** `tool-registry.test.ts` requires every `delete_*` tool to be
   confirmation-gated. Taking one song out of a list is trivially reversible
   and does not deserve a card, so the honest name keeps the rule intact
   instead of carving an exception into it. Same reasoning for
   `remove_artist`, which is additionally ungated because the server refuses
   any removal that would lose something (releases, scoped teammates, the last
   artist), so what can reach it removes an artist with nothing attached.
2. **Nothing was added to the MCP allow-list, and that is inaction rather than
   an omission.** Every new tool proxies a route whose handler does not accept
   the internal actor, so allow-listing one would 401 for every MCP client —
   which `tool-registry.test.ts` asserts structurally. `protocol.test.ts`'s
   count stays **14**. Widening MCP needs route-level auth changes first.
3. **The read-then-merge trap applies to two of the new PATCHes.**
   `PATCH /api/events/[eventId]` is genuinely sparse and `update_show` sends
   only what changed. But the press kit's section PATCH **replaces** that
   section's `content` object, and the capture page's runs every field through
   `normalizeCaptureDraft`, so a sparse update there would blank the
   destination link and unpause a paused page. Both read first.
   `update_capture_page` additionally refuses to unpause a page with no
   working destination, because taking an email and returning nothing is the
   one outcome that feature must never produce.
4. **`upload_cover_art` needed new UI, for the reason `upload_song` already
   records:** no tool can be handed a file. A model turn is text, and
   `input.click()` only opens a dialog inside a user gesture, while a tool
   result arrives from a network response. So the tool resolves the release and
   the BROWSER uploads, through a picker card in the transcript
   (`ChappiCoverArtUploadCard`, mirroring the song one). Choosing a file
   REPLACES the current artwork, which the tool description says out loud.
5. **`write_press_kit_section` writes what the model composed in
   conversation**, and only the three prose sections. For a bio, the model
   writing it is the point; numbers, press quotes and contacts are facts a
   manager enters and `ROLE` forbids filling them in. The embedded
   `press_kit.draft_section` action is the propose-then-apply version of the
   same thing and is untouched — the chat cannot render a review-and-apply
   card.
6. **`list_release_files` returns no download links**, deliberately. Asset
   URLs are signed and short-lived, so a link in a transcript is a link that
   403s by the time anyone taps it.
7. **The three outward actions are gated** (founder call): `send_dj_pack`
   reaches a real person's phone, `send_work_request` lands in a stranger's
   inbox, and `publish_press_kit` puts an artist's page on the public
   internet. None can be unsent, which is the whole gating rule.

### Deliberately given no tool, and `ROLE` says so

A new "not yours to do" paragraph extends the existing negative-capability
precedent, so UrgAns points at the right screen instead of denying a feature
exists. **Task outcomes lead it:** the app asks a person how an activity went
and that answer is theirs, so the assistant must never write one or offer to.
Then billing, data export, issue reports and MCP connections, and finally the
two things the product genuinely cannot do — send email to fans, or talk to a
DSP or distributor.

### The deterministic router

Production runs with no model configured for long stretches, and that router
IS the assistant then. Shows is live, so it gets one branch — and the
collision is the whole difficulty: **"show me my releases" contains "show".**
So the pattern matches `setlist`, `set list`, `gig`, `dj pack`, `run of
show`, `my shows`, `venue`, `soundcheck` and **never the bare word**, and it
sits before the planner and release branches, which claim `plan`, `song` and
`track` between them — every one a word a conversation about a set is full of.
A test asserts "show me my releases" still routes to releases. No new chip:
that row is lg-only and already up to six wide.

### The cost, measured rather than assumed

Tool schemas are sent on **every turn**. Measured: **~5,700 → ~10,100 tokens**
of schemas, with `ROLE` at ~2,600, so fixed per-turn overhead goes roughly
8,500 → 13,000 on `openai/gpt-4o-mini`. Money is negligible at this scale.
**Tool-selection accuracy is the real risk**, and the mitigation is the `ROLE`
grouping (which the model reads as a map) plus tight descriptions. The
tempting alternative — one `manage_setlist` tool with an `action` parameter —
is worse on both counts: a vaguer schema the model gets wrong more often, and
it defeats the confirmation gate, which is per-tool.

### Verified

2744 tests (46 new across `shows`, `shared`, `intent-router` and the two
guards), `eslint .` at the exact measured 3-error / 81-warning baseline with
zero new findings, `tsc --noEmit` clean apart from the documented pre-existing
`confirmed-action.test.ts` errors, and `next build` green **by exit code** in
both flag states with `/auth`, `/onboarding`, `/settings` and `/dashboard`
still `○ Static` in each. Runtime probes, rebuilding between flag states:
flag on, a new surface's route 401s unauthenticated; flag off it 404s with the
body the contract requires while the ungated `/api/releases` still 401s.
**Three mutation passes**, each failing exactly its own test: a tool name
deleted from `ROLE`, `isFlagGateOff` dropped from a tool that needs it, and
`confirm` removed from `delete_show`.

**NOT verified, and it is the whole residual risk: no live model call.** This
sandbox has no route to either urganize domain and cannot mint a session, so
whether the model reaches for the right tool among 91 rests on the schemas and
on `ROLE`, not on anything observed. The manual pass is the real test: ask
"what shows has Dorian got coming up", "build me a 25-minute set from his
catalogue", "is the set going to overrun", "send the pack to Tunde the DJ"
(expect an approval card), "write Dorian's short bio for the press kit", "put
the press kit live" (expect a card), "add Victony to the roster", "archive
Midnight EP" — then ask about something switched off, "collect credits for
Ohema", and confirm it says that isn't switched on rather than inventing a way
round.

## The status update moved into the chat (2026-09-07, v1.28.0)

Founder, immediately after confirming the feature works: *"this feature should
be inside urgans chat not a seperate button"*.

**Mostly a subtraction.** `generate_status_update` has been a Chappi tool since
the original twelve, and it already returned the paragraph as its summary — so
asking UrgAns for a status update worked before this change. What was wrong was
that the same capability also had a pill, a modal and ~90 lines of duplicate
fetch logic in `WorkspaceView`. Those are gone: the action, the modal mount, the
dynamic import, four pieces of state, the generator function, the
`statusUpdateAction` prop through `WorkspaceDesktopFocused` and `TasksPanel`,
the pill, the release-menu entry, the skeleton reservation, and
`components/releases/StatusUpdateModal.tsx` itself.

**Two things had to move WITH it, and they are the whole risk in this change:**

1. **The deterministic branch pointed AT the button.** `resolveIntent` has had
   a `status` keyword branch all along, and `ChappiConversation`'s handler for
   it navigated to the release and said *'Taking you to the release — use
   "Generate status update" there.'* With the pill deleted that is a pointer at
   nothing, so it **generates in the conversation now**, calling the same route
   the tool calls. That matters because it is the no-model path: production has
   run with `CHAPPI_MODEL` unset for long stretches, and this is what keeps the
   feature reachable when the agent loop is unavailable.
2. **The stat tiles were the only verification affordance**, and they died with
   the modal. `components/shared/StatTiles.tsx`' own header says the point of
   the tiles is that a reader can CHECK a generated paragraph against the data
   it was written from, and the route's comment records `stats` as read by the
   modal alone. So `describeStatusFacts` (`lib/release-status.ts`) renders the
   same figures as one line — *"Based on 12 of 64 done, 3 in progress, 2
   blocked."* — appended to the paragraph on BOTH chat paths. It mirrored
   `buildStatusTiles` exactly (same order, same never-print-a-zero rule, `''`
   when there is nothing to verify) so the line and the tiles could not
   disagree about which figures are worth showing; the tiles and their builder
   were deleted the SAME DAY when the recap followed the status update into the
   chat, so the line is the whole surface now. In agentic mode it also gives
   the model real numbers to quote instead of inferring them from prose.

**What deliberately did NOT change:** the route, its flag and the tool.
`NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_STATUS_UPDATE` still gates the route, and the tool still
translates that 404 into a refusal through `isFlagGateOff` rather than a bare
404 — the release-not-yours case must not read as "the feature is off".
`components/shared/StatTiles.tsx` was ALSO left in place, on the reasoning that
`RecapModal` still used it; hours later the recap moved into the chat too and
took the modal with it, so both are now deleted — see the section below.

**One residual, stated rather than papered over:** the capability now depends on
`NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_CHAPPI`. The deterministic fix covers a missing MODEL, not
a missing assistant — if UrgAns were ever switched off, the status update would
have no entry point at all. Acceptable because UrgAns is the front door and has
been on since 2026-08-03, but it is a coupling that did not exist before.

- **Verified:** 2825 tests (11 new in `lib/release-status.test.ts`, written red
  first), `eslint .` at the exact 3-error / 81-warning baseline, `tsc --noEmit`
  clean apart from the documented pre-existing `confirmed-action.test.ts`
  errors, and `next build` green **by exit code** with the status/Chappi flags
  on and with them off, `/auth`, `/onboarding`, `/settings` and `/dashboard`
  all still `○ Static` in each.
- **A near-miss worth recording:** the regex that removed the modal's
  `dynamic()` import took `RecapModal`'s declaration with it — a non-greedy
  `(?:.*\n)*?\);\n\n` ran past the first closer because the two blocks are
  adjacent with no blank line between them. `tsc` caught it. When deleting one
  of several adjacent `dynamic()` blocks, match the import path, not the shape.
- **Not verified:** nothing has rendered in a browser. Worth one pass: ask
  UrgAns for a status update on a real release and confirm the paragraph AND the
  facts line come back, then confirm the pill is gone from the release header
  and from the mobile release menu.

## The recap moved into the chat too (2026-09-07, v1.29.0)

Founder, straight after the status update landed: *"same for the release
recap, put it in urgans"*.

**NOT the same subtraction, and that is the whole design problem.** The status
update's output is a paragraph, so moving it into the conversation was mostly
deletion — the assistant could already say it. The recap's output is two PNGs,
and no amount of prose hands those over. So this one needed a real surface:
`components/chappi/ChappiRecapCard.tsx`, the mirror image of
`ChappiSongUploadCard` — that card exists because a tool cannot be HANDED a
file, this one because a tool cannot GIVE you one.

**Only ONE of the modal's four steps needed it.** `RecapModal` ran
`loading | form | generating | preview`, and the first three were already
conversational: `get_recap` answers "is there one and what are the numbers",
the optional highlight is collected by ASKING (the tool's own description
already told the model to), and `generate_recap` is the build. Only handing the
image over could not be said in words.

**Two things the modal carried that the card deliberately does not:**

1. **No Regenerate.** Asking again IS the regenerate, and it is better, because
   the highlight is part of the request — `POST …/recap` renders both sizes and
   uploads them BEFORE it touches the row, so a replace is already safe on
   every call. A Regenerate button here would rebuild with whatever highlight
   the last turn happened to use, which is the one thing a manager would want
   to change.
2. **No stat tiles.** On the poster the figures ARE the design
   (`lib/recap-card.tsx` lays them out), so tiles above it were in-app chrome
   explaining an artifact that already says it. The status update needed its
   figures in text because a paragraph can assert a number it did not check;
   an image of the numbers cannot. The model still has them from `get_recap` if
   anyone asks.

**Five things worth knowing before editing this:**

1. **The card fetches its own signed URLs on mount, and only the release id
   travels through the tool.** Those URLs are short-lived, so carrying them in
   the tool result would put a credential in the model's context AND leave a
   link in the transcript that expires while it sits there. One read per mount,
   exactly as the modal did per open. `ChappiClientAction`'s `open_recap`
   variant carries `{ releaseId }` and nothing else for this reason.
2. **`'recap'` was taken by the status update, and reassigning it is the fix
   rather than a side effect.** `resolveIntent`'s status branch matched
   `has('status', 'update', 'report', 'summary', 'recap')` — a reasonable
   grouping while the recap had a button of its own, and wrong once the word had
   to reach a card. `recap` is now its own branch, and it **must stay BEFORE the
   release branch**: that one claims `release`, so "release recap" would
   otherwise be read as "start a new release". Mutation-tested both ways —
   deleting the branch and moving it after the release branch each fail exactly
   one named test.
3. **The deterministic path builds the card too, and sends no highlight.**
   Production has run with `CHAPPI_MODEL` unset for long stretches, so the
   keyword branch has to do the real thing rather than point at a button that
   no longer exists (the status update's own lesson, one day old). There is no
   model in that path to hear "say it went platinum", and the route treats the
   highlight as optional — anyone who wants one asks in a sentence, which is the
   agentic path.
4. **Outcomes are reported as transcript lines, not toasts.** `onReport` feeds
   `appendAssistantReply`, matching how the two upload cards report
   (`handleSongUploaded`): this component renders in three surfaces — the page,
   the dock and the rail — and `ChappiConversation` has no toast channel at all.
   "Saved your recap card." is also a thing the assistant just did, so the
   conversation is the right place for it.
5. **The card gets its own state slot, keyed by release.** Not shared with the
   two upload pickers: a manager can plausibly be finishing one release while
   uploading art for another, and one slot would swallow whichever card was
   already open. Like them it survives later turns (a permission card must never
   outlive its proposal; a poster is not destructive) and is cleared by "New
   chat".

**Deleted with it:** `components/releases/RecapModal.tsx`, the `recapAction`
prop through `WorkspaceDesktopFocused` and `TasksPanel`, the pill, the
release-menu entry, the `RELEASE_RECAP_ENABLED` read and modal mount in
`WorkspaceView`, and the skeleton's note about not reserving that pill.

**And two things that lost their last consumer, deleted rather than left
dead:** `components/shared/StatTiles.tsx` and `buildStatusTiles` /
`StatusTile` in `lib/release-status.ts`. Both were kept a few hours earlier on
the reasoning that `RecapModal` still used them (the v1.28.0 section said so);
with the modal gone nothing does. `describeStatusFacts` — the prose line that
replaced the tiles for the status update — survives and is now the only
verification affordance either feature has.

**`isRecapEligible` in `WorkspaceView` STAYS**, and it is worth saying why it
is not orphaned: the archive action gates on it, because "worth celebrating"
and "safe to shelve" are the same moment. It also keeps its recap name, because
that is what the shared predicate in `lib/recap-eligibility.ts` is — its other
two callers are the recap route and `lib/delivery-records.ts`.

**AND THE PATTERN STOPS HERE. The Plan pill stays a pill — founder call,
2026-09-07, asked and answered the same day.** Two AI actions moved into the
conversation on two consecutive days, which makes "so the third one goes too"
an easy and wrong inference; taking it would be re-litigating a settled call.
The reasons it is not the same move: the seven-question intake **already runs
in chat** (`generate_release_plan` collects the answers, `approve_release_plan`
commits behind a confirmation card), so the conversational half is not missing;
what the pill opens is not a modal emitting a paragraph or an image but an
editable ~60-task document with autosave, per-phase redraft and an Approve that
writes the whole plan into `tasks` — a transcript is a poor place to edit sixty
rows, and deleting the scene would leave no way to edit a draft before
approving it; and the pill is self-removing anyway (shown only while a release
has no activities or a draft is waiting), so it never becomes the permanent
chrome the other two had become.

**SUPERSEDED 2026-09-15 — half of this reasoning was overtaken by a founder
call, not disproven.** There is no review scene, no draft, no `approve_release_plan`
and no per-phase redraft any more; the pill (still a pill) now opens the
intake, and finishing it writes the plan straight into `tasks` — see "The plan
is built, not drafted" near the end of this file. The "a transcript is a poor
place to edit sixty rows" argument is moot rather than wrong, because there is
no longer a DRAFT DOCUMENT to edit before commit at all: the manager edits the
created activities through the ordinary release view, the same surface every
other task uses. What survives from this paragraph is the actual reason the
pill stays a pill — the eight-question interview itself is still a poor fit
for the transcript's own turn-taking compared to a modal's discrete steps —
and the self-removing behaviour, unchanged.

- **Verified:** 2827 tests (10 new across `lib/recap-share.test.ts` and
  `lib/chappi/intent-router.test.ts`), `eslint .` at the exact 3-error /
  81-warning baseline (all three pre-existing in `WorkspaceView.tsx`),
  `tsc --noEmit` clean apart from the documented pre-existing
  `confirmed-action.test.ts` errors, and `next build` green **by exit code**
  with the recap flag on and with it off, `/auth`, `/onboarding`, `/settings`
  and `/dashboard` all still `○ Static` in each. Four mutation passes.
- **A mutation that SURVIVED, and the test that now kills it.** Dropping
  `recapFileName`'s post-slice hyphen trim failed nothing: the cap only leaves a
  trailing hyphen when it lands exactly on a word boundary, and no fixture did.
  A 47-character title that caps on its 40th character — the hyphen after
  "deluxe" — closes it. **Trimming before slicing is not enough, and the order
  is the property**; without the second trim the file reads
  `…-deluxe--recap-story.png`.
- **A mutation that never applied, which is the reusable half.** The first
  attempt at the branch-deletion mutation asserted a pattern with a trailing
  blank line the file does not have, so the write never happened and the suite
  passed — indistinguishable from a survivor. Both later attempts print
  `APPLIED` before running. **Confirm a mutation landed before believing it
  survived** (the same lesson the directory's Phase 5 recorded for a `sed`
  indentation miss).
- **CONFIRMED IN PRODUCTION the same day: the founder asked UrgAns for a recap
  on a finished release and the card came up.** That is more than a render — the
  card only reaches that state after its own `GET …/recap` resolves and returns
  a row with a `storyImageUrl`, so the tool's new `open_recap` action fired, the
  client dispatched it, the route answered and the signed URLs came back. It
  also settles the deploy: the v1.29.0 build was triggered at 16:16 UTC and
  Vercel's account-wide deployment rate limit closed at 16:19 (see the note
  under Deployment), so this landed in the last window before it.
- **Download is confirmed too, the same day: the founder pressed it and the file
  saved.** So the payload works end to end — `shareOrDownloadImage`'s web branch
  fetched the signed URL and `recapFileName` produced a name the browser
  accepted, which is the whole reason that builder exists (a file called `blob`
  or `download.png` is what it was written to prevent).
- **Two paths remain unexercised, both narrow:** the Story/Square toggle (the
  press was on whichever size was showing, and story is the default), and the
  NATIVE share sheet, which cannot be reached until a store build ships —
  `@capacitor/share` was added but the only APK on record predates it, so
  `lib/share-file.ts`'s plugin probe degrades to opening in the system browser
  by design. Same blocker as native push: the binary.

## An explicitly requested scene was disposable (2026-09-08, v1.32.1)

Founder report: he drafted an EP rollout plan with UrgAns, tapped **"Review
your draft plan"**, and landed on the **Metadata** scene instead. Repeatable.
The account has **exactly one release**, which turns out to be the trigger.

**The button was never wrong.** `WorkspaceView.tsx:888` calls
`openScene('plan', id)`, which writes `?release=X&scene=plan` and pushes it —
and there is exactly one control in the whole app whose label contains
"Review", so there was no mis-targeted link to find. The scene was being
**rewritten after the click**.

### Root cause: two owners, one param, no contract

`useReleaseScope.setScope` threw away whatever `scene` the URL was carrying and
substituted the one it remembered for the incoming release:

```ts
const resumedScene = releaseId ? recallScene(releaseId) : null;
if (resumedScene) params.set(SCENE_PARAM, resumedScene);   // clobbers it
else params.delete(SCENE_PARAM);                            // or drops it
```

`openScene` treated that param as an explicit request, `setScope` treated it as
its own to overwrite, and the `?new=1` effect deleted it outright. Nothing said
which won, and **no test anywhere asserted that a requested scene survived
anything** — which is why it shipped.

**MEMORY IS A DEFAULT, NEVER AN OVERRIDE.** That inversion is the whole bug.

**Why one release makes it fire.** `WorkspaceView.tsx:293-327` auto-scopes a
single-release account to its only release on arrival — through `setScope`, so
through the clobber. Its guard (`hasAutoScopedRef`) is **per mount**, and
`WorkspaceView` unmounts on every trip to Settings, Notes, UrgAns or the
catalog, so the auto-scope re-arms on every return to `/dashboard`. Once
Metadata was the remembered scene for that release — written by any release-card
tap or deselect, neither of which passes `forgetScene` — every later arrival
resolved to `scene=metadata` over the top of whatever had just been asked for.

### The rule now, and where it lives

`decideIncomingScene` in `lib/scene-memory.ts`, pure and unit-tested. Highest
precedence first:

1. **`requested`** — the caller said so outright. `null` is a real answer
   ("no scene"), so the field's ABSENCE is what means "no opinion", tested with
   `in` rather than truthiness. Same absent-vs-null distinction the metadata and
   curator PATCH routes make, and for the same reason: three states, not two.
2. **`urlScene`, and ONLY when `previousReleaseId` is null.** That is the one
   case where the scene in the address bar was authored for the release being
   scoped TO — a deep link, a shared URL, or the single-release auto-scope
   firing under one. Switching from release A to B must NOT carry A's scene
   across; that leak is the reason scene memory exists at all.
3. **`remembered`** — `recallScene`'s answer, flag-filtered here.

**That second condition lives INSIDE the pure function rather than in the
hook**, deliberately: `useReleaseScope` renders nothing and has no unit test, so
a decision left inline there is a decision nothing checks. That is how the
original bug survived.

`SetScopeOptions` also gained **`scene?: SceneName | null`**, so a caller can
say "go to this release and show this scene" in ONE navigation. Before, that
meant `setScope` then `openScene` — two navigations where the first resolves the
scene from memory and the second corrects it, so the wrong scene paints for a
frame and either call can lose the race.

### Five adjacent instances of the same class, all fixed

1. **`WorkspaceView`'s `?new=1` effect** rebuilt the URL as
   `/dashboard?release=<id>`, discarding `scene` **and** the calendar's
   `calendar`/`month`. It deletes only `new` now. A create flow that landed on a
   scene lost it the instant the guide was consumed.
2. **`resolveActiveScene` gated five scenes and skipped four.** The comment
   claimed metadata / files / pitch / plan "gate themselves inside
   `ReleaseScenePanel`" — **that file reads no feature flag at all, and never
   has**, so those four had no URL-level gate anywhere. Files has been off in
   production since v0.16.4, so `?scene=files` was a header with a dead fetch
   under it for anyone holding an old link. All nine flag-gated scenes are gated
   here now (founder call: an old link lands on the release), leaving
   `activities` as the only ungated name — it is `resolveMainView`'s fallback,
   so gating it would leave the panel blank after a rollback.
3. **`SCENE_PREFETCH_ORDER` warmed `files` and `pitch` unconditionally.** With
   those flags off their API routes 404 and `readJson` throws, so the prefetch
   spent a guaranteed 404 per scoped release and then threw — the identical bug
   metadata's own entry was fixed for on 2026-08-27.
4. **A remembered scene outlived the flag that allowed it.** Switch Content off
   and a release last showing the calendar got `scene=calendar` written back
   into its URL, where `resolveActiveScene` nulled it on render: address bar
   said one thing, panel showed another, pill lit for a scene not on screen.
5. **`WorkspaceSkeleton` reserved the wrong body.** `hideRails` read the real
   `?scene=` param while the body read `resolveMainView()` alone, so every scene
   URL reserved a timeline (or bucket) body and then painted a scene over it —
   the exact shift the file's own comment says it exists to prevent. Both read
   ONE threaded value now, which is the point: a skeleton that contradicts
   itself is worse than one that guesses.

`ReleaseScenePanel` also bails on a scene it has no body for rather than
rendering a header whose title is `undefined`. That IS reachable: `'activities'`
is a legal `SceneName` a caller can pass today.

### One reported defect that turned out not to be real

An exploration pass flagged that the pills light from the URL alone while the
body additionally needs `scopedReleaseSlim`, so a release not yet loaded would
light "Plan" over the main view. **Checked, and it does not happen:** all nine
pills are gated on `scopedRelease` (the same object), and `showOutboundPills`
carries `Boolean(scopedRelease)`, so no pill renders without one. Left alone
rather than "fixed" — recorded here so nobody re-chases it.

A compile-time scene-coverage type was also written and then deleted, proven
redundant by mutation: `SCENE_LABELS`, `SCENE_PERSISTED` and `ScenePayloadMap`
are all `Record<SceneName, …>`, so a new scene already fails the build in three
places. Decoration, by this file's own standard.

### Comment drift corrected in place

`useSceneOverlay` said the URL and data layers "key off the same **four**
names" (ten), its `activeScene` docstring said "one of the four known scenes",
`TasksPanel` said "the four release scenes", and `scene-cache.test.ts` had a
case titled "the five ungated scenes" asserting four.

### The edge-case sweep

The ask was for exhaustive coverage. **"At least 10,000" is emphasis, and
inventing a count would be dishonest** — what was actually done is the matrix,
with a fix or a test for every combination that can produce "asked for A, got B
or nothing":

- **10 scene names × 2 flag states.** `resolvePanelBody` now has a case
  asserting every name in `SCENE_NAMES` resolves to itself with the flags on,
  so a new scene cannot be added without it; and every flag-gated name resolves
  to the main view with them off.
- **5 param shapes** — absent, valid, unknown, wrong-case, empty. All covered;
  case and whitespace are deliberately NOT normalised, since the app only ever
  writes this param itself, so a near-miss is a hand-typed URL.
- **4 scope transitions** — no release → release (preserve the URL scene),
  release A → release B (resume B's memory, never carry A's), same release (the
  branch does not run at all), release → none (scene deleted).
- **4 navigation kinds** — push, replace, mount, remount. The per-mount ref is
  what made remount the interesting one, and it is why the fix is in the
  precedence rule rather than in the guard.
- **`?release=undefined` from a template literal over an optional id** — ruled
  out rather than assumed: every client navigation that interpolates a release
  id either throws first (`useStartTestRelease`), guards the whole entry
  (`WorkspaceIdentityPanel`), or creates the release and throws unless it gets
  an id back (`PlannerIntakeModal`).
- **Two owners writing one param** — the class itself. `openScene` and
  `setScope` now have a stated contract, and it is enforced by the one function
  both funnel through.

### Verified

**2993 tests** (13 new; clean-tree baseline measured at 2980 first), `eslint .`
at **exactly** the measured 3-error / 81-warning baseline with **zero** new
findings, `tsc --noEmit` clean apart from the documented pre-existing
`confirmed-action.test.ts` errors, and `next build` green **by exit code** with
the four newly gated flags ON and with them OFF, `/auth`, `/onboarding`,
`/settings` and `/dashboard` all still `○ Static` in each.

**Four mutations, each killing exactly its own tests** and each printing
`APPLIED` before running, per the recorded lesson that a mutation which never
landed is indistinguishable from a survivor: reverting to "memory always wins"
(the original bug, 2 failures), truthiness instead of `in` for `requested` (1),
carrying the URL scene across a release switch (1), and dropping the flag filter
on a remembered scene (1). The file was restored byte-identical after each.

### Not verified

**Nothing has run in a browser.** This sandbox cannot mint a session and has no
route to app.urganize.app, so the founder's own repro is the real test. On the
one-release account: open Metadata on the release, tap the release card twice to
deselect and reselect, then tap **"Review your draft plan"** and confirm it
opens the plan. Then go to Settings and back to `/dashboard` and confirm you are
not dumped into Metadata.

The `?new=1` fix is **comment-guarded rather than test-guarded** — it is four
lines of standard `URLSearchParams` inside a React effect, and this repo has no
component tests to reach it. Said plainly rather than implied.

## The object is a rollout (2026-09-09, v1.37.0)

Founder call: the thing a manager creates and runs is a **rollout**, not a release. Until this the word "rollout" named only a PLAN TYPE ("rollout plan" vs "blank"), while every label, heading, email, UrgAns reply and error message called the object a release. Now every string a person reads in `apps/web` says rollout. **Everything in this file above this section says "release" as historical record and is deliberately not rewritten.**

The rules, so the next label does not drift back:

| Case | Rule |
|---|---|
| The object (singular, plural, possessive) | rollout / rollouts / rollout's. "New rollout", "Archive rollout", "No rollouts yet", Settings → "Rollouts". |
| "Release title" | **"Title"** alone — the title names the record, so neither "Release title" nor "Rollout title" is right. |
| "Release type" (Single / EP / Album) | **"Format"**. The values are unchanged. |
| release date / release day / release week, the Timeline axis label `Release`, `PlanTaskRow`'s "Release day", the `released` status | **KEEP** — these name the day the music comes out, not the object. |
| Public and outward pages: `/epk`, `/credits`, `/capture`, `/pack`, the press-kit prose an editor reads, the printed recap card (`RECAP_EYEBROW`), collaborator- and fan-facing emails | **KEEP** "release" — those readers do not know our word. The in-app labels that OPEN those surfaces say rollout. |
| Playbook task copy (`lib/release-templates/*`) | **KEEP** in this pass. Dominated by date phrasing, versioned as `.md` + `.ts` pairs, test-pinned. The few "the release" object references in task bodies are an optional follow-up. |
| Identifiers | never touched: URLs (`?release=`, `/dashboard/releases/`), DB tables and enums, env flags, tool names (`create_release`), TS symbols, DOM ids, storage keys, analytics event names, comments. |
| API error bodies | `'Rollout not found.'`, `'Rollout id is required.'` — the flag gates still match exactly `'Not found.'` (`isFlagGateOff`), which is untouched. |

Three mechanisms hold it:

- **`lib/rollout-vocabulary.test.ts`** scans an explicit list of high-traffic UI files (the create modal, the workspace, the nav, UrgAns's conversation and system prompt, the emails, the notification presets, `help-copy.ts`, the pricing package) and fails on the object word inside string literals, template literals or JSX text, letting the date phrases, URLs, table names and tool names through. **It reads through `readableCopy` from `lib/copy-scan.ts`, not a reader of its own** — that module's header states the rule ("two guards would drift the moment one of them gained a rule"), and a first draft of this guard that hand-rolled an extractor was deleted for it. Two of copy-scan's documented behaviours come free and both are wanted: comments are exempt, and a whitespace-free string reads as an identifier, so a bare `'Release'` (a table name, a key, the timeline axis label) is invisible here exactly as intended. Two skips ARE local, each with a test: a segment carrying JS punctuation (copy-scan's `>...<` rule can read an arrow-function body as JSX text), and `URGANS_COPY_RULES` by identity. **AMENDED 2026-09-25: the code skip applies to JSX text only, and nothing exempts a whole segment any more.** The code skip used to run on every segment, so one `);` in UrgAns's 12,000-character prompt (a template literal) marked the whole prompt as code and it was never scanned, which hid 11 places where it called the object a release; all 11 are reworded. A second skip exempted an entire segment whenever an allowed phrase (a release date, a tool name like `create_release`) appeared anywhere in it; an allowed phrase now exempts only its own match, through the window check. `lib/copy-scan.ts` gained `readableCopySegments`, the same pieces `readableCopy` returns tagged with the reader that found them, so the guard can tell JSX text from strings; `readableCopy` is built from it and its output is unchanged, which a test pins. The guard's own test for the code skip had been vacuous: its example produced no text at all, so it passed with the skip deleted. It uses the real `AppTopbar.tsx` shape now, and asserts the example yields a segment. A new test puts one object-word sentence into the real prompt and requires the guard to find it, so the prompt cannot silently drop out of scope again. Failures now report a short excerpt around each hit rather than the whole segment.
- **UrgAns is told the word, in `URGANS_COPY_RULES` rather than in `ROLE`.** That constant is already exempted from the positioning guard by identity — the `bannedCopyInstruction()` precedent — and a rule that names a banned word has to live somewhere exempt or the instruction enforcing it fails the guard enforcing it. It says: say rollout, never release, when you mean that object; the tools stay `*_release`; "release date" and "release day" stay as they are. The typed keyword router (`intent-router.ts`) ACCEPTS "rollout" alongside "release" rather than replacing it — someone who learned the old word is not stranded — and the test asserts both route the same.
- **The changelog voice** uses rollout from v1.37.0 forward; history is not rewritten.

`packages/pricing` moved with the app ("3 rollouts at a time"), which the marketing site also reads — so `/pricing` showed the new word one PR ahead of the rest of `apps/homepage`.

**The marketing site followed the same day, in its own PR and with no version bump** (the app-only scope rule). Every page speaks the new word; four things deliberately do not:

- **`LANDING_KEYWORDS` keeps "music release planning" and "release rollout plan".** Those are not read, they are typed into a search box, and nobody searches for a word we coined last week. Revisit once the term has an audience — the reasoning is written beside the constant so it is not "fixed" by the next sweep.
- **Verbatim testimonials.** Three customer quotes still say "release" and stay that way; a quote is not ours to edit. The `before`/`them` strings beside them ARE our prose and moved — and one of them, Antoine's, is documented as byte-identical between `content/testimonials.ts` and `/why-urganize`. **The rename broke that mirror and it had to be restored**; check both when either changes.
- **`/for-curators`, `/privacy`, `/terms`, `/subprocessors`.** Curators are not our users and legal copy is not marketing copy.
- **"Release fast without releasing messy."** (`/for-ai-artists`). Both are the VERB. The plan called for rewriting it to avoid a double meaning, and that was written when the OBJECT was also a release — with the object renamed, the pun is *less* ambiguous, not more, so it stays.

**THE FOUNDER-LOCKED POSITIONING MOVED TOO, and it could not be deferred to that next PR.** Asked whether the rename should reach `lib/positioning.ts`, the founder answered "rename them too", so `PROMISE` is now *"Plan, organize and execute rollouts from one place"*. Three consequences worth knowing:

- **`CANONICAL_DESCRIPTION` is a hand rewrite, not a substitution.** It already ended "keep every part of a rollout moving from one place", so a mechanical pass says the word twice in one sentence; the second is dropped, leaving "keep every part moving from one place".
- **It is one unit across BOTH apps.** `positioning-guard.test.ts` lives in `apps/web` but walks `apps/homepage/app`, `apps/homepage/lib`, `README.md` and `docs/store-listing.md`, and asserts the homepage mirror is byte-identical below its header — so splitting positioning across PR1 and PR2 would have landed one PR with a red guard. `⚠️ /music rollouts/i` is on that guard's RETIRED list, so the rename must never produce that phrase.
- **The OG card bakes the promise**, so it was regenerated (`apps/homepage/scripts/generate-og-image.mjs`) and `SHARE_IMAGE_VERSION` bumped to `2026-09-09-rollout`. The `alt` needed no edit: it composes from `ONE_LINER` and `PROMISE`. A stale comment beside it claiming there is "no generator in the repo" was corrected in the same pass — that generator landed 2026-09-09.

**A rebase lesson worth keeping, because it changed the resolution rule mid-flight.** This branch sat unmerged while #569 (positioning), #570 (the draggable side menu) and then #572/#573 (the Pitching page) landed on `main` underneath it — TWO rebases in one afternoon, the first colliding on 53 files. The first attempt resolved them by taking THIS branch's version and replaying main's small diffs on top — which quietly reintroduced the word "workspace" into user-facing copy across a dozen files, because this branch predates the brief that banned it. **Main's wording is the base; the rename goes on top of it.** The direction matters more than the mechanics: when a rebase collides two copy changes, the newer editorial decision wins and the older mechanical one is re-derived. That is also why the plan called for re-running the rename rather than hand-merging 187 files.

**Verified:** the full vitest suite green (3119 passing) including the new guard and router cases; `eslint .` at the measured 3-error / 81-warning baseline with zero new findings, measured by stashing rather than assumed; `next build` green by exit code with `/auth`, `/onboarding`, `/settings` still `○ Static`. **Not verified:** nothing rendered in a browser — this sandbox cannot mint a session — so the "Title" and "Format" labels in the create modal and the onboarding wizard are the two things worth a look.

## Annual only, at new prices (2026-09-08, shipped as v1.39.0)

Founder spec: move every tier to annual-only pricing at new rates, with no
monthly option anywhere. **Solo ₦5,000/year, Manager ₦22,000/year, Label
₦50,000/year, Group "Let's talk".** No migration, no new flag — the whole thing
rides `NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_PRICING_V2`, which is already on in production, so it
is live at merge.

**RENUMBERED SIX TIMES ON ONE DAY — v1.32.0, v1.33.0, v1.36.0, v1.37.0,
v1.38.0, v1.39.0 — across seven merges of `main`, and the last three are the
useful record because of when they happened.** Built as v1.32.0, it sat
unmerged while another session shipped v1.32.0 and v1.32.1 on `main`;
renumbered to v1.33.0, and within the hour #568 took **v1.33.0**, the same
number and the same ledger date; renumbered to v1.36.0 after #569 (v1.35.0) and
#570 (v1.34.0) both landed; renumbered a fourth time when #572/#573 took
**v1.36.0**; a fifth when #571 took **v1.37.0** in the ~15 minutes it took
to merge, verify and push the fourth; and a sixth when #574 took **v1.38.0**
in the same window again. (A seventh merge, #575, was the only one that did
not collide — marketing-site only, so by the app-only scope rule it earns no
ledger entry and no bump.) `CURRENT_VERSION` derives from the changelog's top
entry, so merging on any of the six would have sent the product version
BACKWARDS. Nothing about the change itself moved any of the six times; only
the number and the ledger date.

**A branch that carries a version bump is perishable, and the last two
collisions measure how perishable.** The first three each took about an hour;
the fourth took minutes; the fifth landed *inside the merge that resolved the
fourth*. So "re-check `packages/changelog/src/index.ts` against `origin/main`
immediately before merging" is not a formality and not a once-per-session
check — it is what caught both, the second time against a base that had been
verified clean minutes earlier, in the same turn.

**The real fix is to stop claiming the number early:** a version bump wants to
be the LAST commit before merge, not part of the feature work, precisely
because several sessions can hold a claim on one number at once and none of
them can see the others. Everything else about a branch can wait; the number
cannot. **The corollary the last three add: on a busy day, budget for the re-check to
fail, and shorten the window it has to survive.** `main` landed a commit every
six to fifteen minutes that afternoon, while a merge-plus-gates-plus-wait-for-CI
cycle took about fifteen — so the branch lost the race by construction until the
wait was dropped. **The Vercel status is a PREVIEW DEPLOYMENT, not a test
suite** (this repo runs no GitHub Actions; the gates are local), so blocking a
merge on it buys nothing and costs exactly the minutes that let `main` move
again. Run the gates locally, push, and merge. The only thing that made seven
merges cheap at all was that the resolution rule never changed — main's entry
preserved byte-for-byte, mine renumbered above it.

**⚠️ READ THE ACTIVATION BLOCK AT THE END BEFORE MERGING.** Every amount moved
and a Paystack Plan's amount is fixed when the Plan is created, so three new Plan
objects have to exist. The code is built so that shipping first cannot overcharge
anyone, but it can leave the wall unable to take a card.

**Two calls were put to the founder before any of it was built, and both changed
what shipped:**

1. **Label is buyable by card again**, reversing the 2026-08-30 decision that
   made it sales-led with no price at all. The spec's own acceptance line —
   "three annual prices and one 'Let's talk' card" — only adds up that way, and
   reversing a nine-day-old founder call on my reading of an acceptance bullet
   was worth confirming rather than inferring. **Group came back onto the page in
   the same move** to be that one card; it had been off both surfaces since
   Label took the sales-led slot.
2. **"Distribution included" is printed as written, and it is a FOUNDER OVERRIDE
   rather than drift.** Urganize does not distribute music — no DSP integration,
   and third-party platform integrations are on the v1 out-of-scope list — so the
   line breaks the standing rule that the pricing page never names an unbuilt
   feature (`perks` says so in as many words). The real thing behind the word is
   the Metadata scene assembling the ISRC, UPC, splits and credits a distributor
   asks for. Honest wording was offered and declined. Recorded at
   `UNIVERSAL_HIGHLIGHTS` in `packages/pricing` so the next reader takes it back
   to him rather than quietly correcting it.

### Nine things worth knowing before editing this

1. **THE SHAPE IS THE ENFORCEMENT.** `prices` is `{ annual: TierPrice }`, not a
   `Record<BillingInterval, …>` with the monthly key left empty. There is no
   monthly figure in the data at all, `getTierPrice` answers null for any
   interval but annual, and `formatTierPrice` takes NO interval argument. The
   acceptance bar was "nowhere a monthly figure", and a type holds that better
   than a sweep of the call sites can.
2. **`BillingInterval` KEEPS 'monthly', and must.** Real rows in
   `subscriptions.billing_interval` hold it and those subscriptions still renew
   on a monthly cycle. What ended is SELLING one. `SELLING_INTERVAL` is exported
   so nothing has to write the literal, and `resolveBillingInterval`,
   `advancePeriodEnd` and `PERIOD_DAYS` are all untouched.
3. **`purchasableTiers()` NEEDED ONE MONTHLY CODE REMOVED, and that was the
   single sharpest way this reprice could have taken checkout down with no test
   failing.** It required BOTH a monthly and an annual Plan code, on the sound
   reasoning that the wall's interval toggle was always live. With the monthly
   prices gone that requirement makes every tier unpurchasable. Mutation-tested.
4. **NEW ENV VAR NAMES, AND THE NEWNESS IS THE SAFETY MECHANISM.** The live map
   reads `PAYSTACK_PLAN_{SOLO,MANAGER,LABEL}_YEARLY_NGN` — names nothing has
   set. Reusing `..._ANNUAL_NGN` would have been far worse than untidy: it is
   already set and points at the ₦80,000 Plan, so a deploy before minting would
   advertise ₦5,000 and charge ₦80,000. That advertise-versus-charge gap has
   shipped **five** times here, every time caught by a person. An unset name
   inverts the failure into a withheld card. **`_YEARLY_` is not `_ANNUAL_`**,
   they are English synonyms and different vars, and the old names now live in
   `SUPERSEDED_TIER_PLAN_CODE_ENV_VARS` where only the renewal sanity check reads
   them.
5. **`isGrandfatheredRate` is the "new prices only apply to new subscriptions"
   half, and it compares against `subscriptions.amount`.** That column is the
   last full period charge, written by the initial purchase and every renewal and
   deliberately NOT touched by a prorated top-up — so it means "what a period of
   this subscription costs", which is the question. **Nothing new is stored:** no
   column, no cutoff date, no flag, and it self-maintains through the next
   reprice because the comparison is always against whatever the package says
   today. It FAILS TOWARD GRANDFATHERED on every uncertainty, because wrongly
   refusing costs a support message while wrongly allowing takes the wrong amount
   of real money. One accepted false positive: between an upgrade and the next
   renewal `amount` still holds the old tier's price, so a second change inside
   one period refuses — which is also exactly when the founder still has a
   Paystack swap to perform by hand.
6. **THE PRICE LOCK IS A PROPERTY OF PAYSTACK, NOT OF THIS CODE.** A subscription
   is bound to its Plan when it is created, so repointing an env var changes what
   a NEW customer is charged and nothing about an existing one. The guard above
   exists for the one place our code could still get it wrong: quoting a plan
   CHANGE off list prices the account has never paid.
7. **A REAL BUG SHIPPED FOR A DAY INSIDE THIS WORK AND IS FIXED HERE.**
   `readSalesLedPlanName` did one lookup against the tier table, on the reasoning
   that every sales-led id is also a tier id. True, and not sufficient: `label`
   is a valid id in BOTH generations and they now disagree about it — the TIER is
   a ₦50,000 self-serve plan while the LEGACY `label` is still sales-led with
   `PAYSTACK_PLAN_LABEL_NGN` holding a mislabeled ₦750,000 Plan. One lookup
   answered "not sales-led" for both, so a flag-off request would have charged
   ₦750,000 while recording ₦800,000. It asks which generation the request is
   read in now. **The pinning test did not catch it** — it asserted "every
   sales-led legacy id is also a tier id", which stayed true the whole time — so
   it is rewritten to assert the thing that matters.
8. **ABSENT AND EMPTY NOW MEAN DIFFERENT THINGS on the wall's tier list.**
   `offeredTiers` read `fromServer && fromServer.length > 0`, so an empty list
   fell back to offering everything. Right for ABSENT (an older server, an
   unreadable payload, and a walled team must never be left with no way to pay);
   wrong for EMPTY, which is the server saying it cannot charge any of them —
   there the fallback turns a withheld card into a radio that ends in a 500. It
   matters most in exactly the window a reprice opens. When the list is empty the
   wall now says card payment is unavailable and points at the full-weight Talk
   to us card beside it, and the Subscribe button is HIDDEN rather than disabled
   (the seat-cap lesson: a greyed button with no explanation is worse than none,
   and here the server has already given the reason).
9. **`minimumTierWith` SKIPS SALES-LED TIERS NOW.** Its doc always said the
   answer is used as an upgrade target, and the skip was implicit only because
   the displayed order happened to carry no sales-led tier between 2026-08-30 and
   this change. Group rejoining the page made `minimumTierWith('sso')` start
   answering 'enterprise' for an entitlement nothing implements.

### Smaller decisions

- **"/year" spelled out, not "/yr"** (founder copy rule: fifth-grade readable).
- **`annualSavingCopy` and `ANNUAL_MONTHS_BILLED` are deleted**, along with every
  "2 months free" badge. There is no monthly figure left to save against.
- **`/pricing` went back to a SERVER component.** It only needed `'use client'`
  for the interval toggle's `useState`. Four cards now, `sm:grid-cols-2
  xl:grid-cols-4`, the shape this page used the last time it carried four.
- **`SELF_SERVE_TIERS` on the marketing page is derived from `contactSales`, not
  a hand-written Set.** It went stale the same day Label got a price — the card
  would have shown ₦50,000 above a "Let's talk" button. Same derivation the
  in-app wall already makes.
- **`BILLING_PLANS` (the legacy generation) is untouched**, and the legacy picker
  in `TeamWall` keeps its monthly figure. That branch only renders with pricing
  v2 OFF, which is the documented rollback state, and its numbers are what real
  legacy subscribers renew against. A comment at that JSX says so, so the next
  sweep does not "finish the job" by editing their prices.
- **`/terms` §04 moved with it**, since it is a contract: billed once a year
  rather than monthly-or-annually, and it now states the price lock outright.
  `LAST_UPDATED` bumped.
- **`/for-labels` stopped saying we price each roster deal by hand.** What
  survives is the part that was always the real substance of Label and is not
  self-serve at all: the founders set the roster up with you.
- **`/pricing`'s "How a demo works" became "How the Group plan works."** With
  Label back on a card checkout, Group is the only card those three steps
  describe.

### What "app store listing text" turned out to mean

The spec asks for it and **there is nothing in this repo to change.** No store
listing copy exists anywhere: `docs/mobile/codemagic-setup.md` says in as many
words that screenshots, descriptions and privacy answers are App Store Connect
and Play Console dashboard work, and the CI pipeline only builds and uploads the
binary. No store release has ever shipped either. So that item is a founder task
in those two dashboards, not a code change.

### Verified

**2995 tests passing** (up from 2983; ~35 rewritten across `billing-plans`,
`plan-change`, `entitlements`, `billing-summary` and `tier-limits-guard`, since
those files encoded the old contract), `eslint .` **byte-identical to the
measured clean-tree baseline** (3 errors / 81 warnings in `apps/web`, all
pre-existing in `WorkspaceView.tsx`; 0 / 2 in `apps/homepage`) with **zero** new
findings, `tsc --noEmit` clean apart from the documented pre-existing
`confirmed-action.test.ts` errors, and `next build` green **by exit code** for
both apps with `apps/web` built in BOTH pricing-v2 states and `/auth`,
`/dashboard`, `/locked`, `/onboarding`, `/settings` all still `○ Static` in each.
`/pricing`, `/terms` and `/for-labels` still `○ Static` too.

**The acceptance bar was checked against the PRERENDERED HTML rather than the
source**, which is this repo's habit for anything a page renders: `/pricing`
and `/` each carry exactly `₦5,000/year`, `₦22,000/year` and `₦50,000/year`,
each prices Group as "Let's talk", and each has **zero** occurrences of
"Monthly", "/mo" or "months free". `/changelog` reads the new version.
**"Distribution included" is on `/pricing`'s four cards and deliberately not on
`/`** — the landing strip calls `tierHighlights(id).slice(0, 3)`, so the three
countable-limit lines fill the slice and the universal line falls off the end.
That slice is pre-existing (#481, the landing rebuild), and the strip is a
teaser rather than a second price table, so it is by design and not a gap.

**Two grep lessons from checking it, and they are the same lesson twice.** An
apostrophe in prerendered HTML is not one string: `/pricing` emits React's
hex-escaped `Let&#x27;s talk` (from the tier data's straight quote) while `/`
emits a typographic `Let’s talk` (a hand-written JSX string), so a grep for
either alone reports zero on the other page and looks like a missing card. And
a hit count is not a card count: `/pricing`'s two are the Group card's price
line **and** its CTA, while one of `/`'s two is the serialized RSC payload
rather than anything visible. Extract the region and strip the tags before
believing a count.

**Three mutation passes, each printing APPLIED first and each killing exactly its
own tests:** making `isGrandfatheredRate` fail open on an unreadable amount,
putting the monthly requirement back into `purchasableTiers`, and reverting
`readSalesLedPlanName` to its single lookup.

### Not verified

**Nothing has run against real Paystack or a real database.** No card has been
charged at a new price, no renewal has extended, no plan change has been quoted
or refused, and the grandfathered guard has only ever run as a pure function. The
wall has not rendered in a browser: this sandbox cannot mint a Supabase session
and has no route to either urganize domain (the proxy answers 403 to CONNECT).
The absent-versus-empty distinction in point 8 has no unit test either, because
it lives in a `useMemo` and this repo has no component tests.

### Activation — DO THIS BEFORE MERGING

1. ~~**Mint THREE new annual Paystack Plans**, in NGN: Solo ₦5,000/year, Manager
   ₦22,000/year, Label ₦50,000/year.~~ — **done 2026-09-09 (founder).**
2. ~~**Set `PAYSTACK_PLAN_SOLO_YEARLY_NGN`, `PAYSTACK_PLAN_MANAGER_YEARLY_NGN` and
   `PAYSTACK_PLAN_LABEL_YEARLY_NGN`** on the Vercel `Web` project.~~ — **done
   2026-09-09 (founder).** ⚠️ For anyone reading this later: `_YEARLY_` is not
   `_ANNUAL_`, and `PAYSTACK_PLAN_LABEL_YEARLY_NGN` is not
   `PAYSTACK_PLAN_LABEL_NGN` (that one holds a stale ₦750,000 Plan).
3. ~~**DEACTIVATE the old monthly and annual Plans in the Paystack dashboard, and
   do not delete them.**~~ — **done 2026-09-09 (founder).** Deactivating stops anyone new landing on one; the
   subscriptions already bound to them keep renewing at what they signed for,
   which is the price-lock half of the spec and needs no code.
4. **Leave the old `_ANNUAL_` and `_MONTHLY_` vars set.** They are read only by
   the renewal sanity check now, and clearing them makes a pre-reprice
   subscriber log a warning on every renewal.
5. Merge. The ledger entry and the version bump are already in this change,
   because pricing v2 is on and this is live the moment it deploys.
6. **Verify with a real card**: buy Solo, confirm Paystack quotes ₦5,000 and
   `subscriptions.billing_interval` reads `annual`; then confirm an existing
   paying account's next renewal still charges what it always did.

**The merge-early caveat is spent, and what it bought is worth recording.** It
read: merge before steps 1 and 2 and nothing breaks and nobody is overcharged,
because `purchasableTiers()` finds no code, the wall says card payment is
unavailable and points at Talk to us, and the public page shows the new prices.
That held. **The order it did NOT protect against is the one that happened:
config first, code second.** With the Plans minted and the `_YEARLY_` vars set
while the deployed build still read `_ANNUAL_`/`_MONTHLY_`, production was
selling the OLD prices against Plans that had just been deactivated — so the
window between the founder finishing activation and this merge landing is the
one genuinely exposed moment in the whole reprice, and it is short only because
the merge followed within the hour. **Next reprice: land the code first and set
the vars second.** New var names make that safe (an unset name withholds the
card), which is exactly what they are for.

### One thing to decide, which no code can settle

**The prices went DOWN, hard — Solo ₦80,000 to ₦5,000 a year, Manager ₦350,000 to
₦22,000 — so "existing paying accounts keep their current price" now works
AGAINST them.** A lifetime lock normally shields a customer from an increase;
here it holds a handful of accounts at up to sixteen times what a new customer
pays. The spec is explicit and this is built exactly as asked: nothing touches an
existing subscription, and `isGrandfatheredRate` refuses to quote them a
self-serve change, routing them to a human instead. That human can move anyone
down whenever you want (`/admin/teams` can mark a team paid at any amount). It is
an operations call rather than a code one, which is why it is written down here
rather than asked about.

## Group tier removed; "Most teams" moved to Solo (2026-09-09, shipped as v1.40.0)

Founder call, one day after Group ("Let's talk", id `enterprise`) rejoined the
ladder in the annual-only reprice above: remove it entirely, not merely take it
off the page or flag it dark. Then move the "Most teams" recommended badge from
Manager to Solo. Both are copy-and-type changes with no migration and no new
flag — the pricing package and its five downstream consumer modules already
carry every mechanism this needed.

**THE INSTRUCTION WAS "REMOVE ENTIRELY", AND THAT IS A DIFFERENT ASK FROM EVERY
PREVIOUS GROUP CHANGE ON THIS LADDER.** Group had already been added, taken off,
added back and repriced-around three times in nine days (2026-08-30 add,
2026-09-02 to -08 off while Label held the sales-led slot, 2026-09-08 back on
for one day). Every one of those was a DISPLAY change — `PRICING_TIER_ORDER`
gained or lost an entry while `PRICING_TIERS.enterprise` kept existing
underneath. This is not that: `'enterprise'` is gone from the `PricingTierId`
UNION TYPE itself, so nothing anywhere in the codebase can construct, store, or
render one any more — not behind a flag, not hidden from an array, deleted.

### Six things worth knowing before touching this again

1. **THE SHARPEST BEHAVIOURAL CONSEQUENCE: a stray `'enterprise'` string is no
   longer "sales-led", it is UNRECOGNISED.** Every gate that used to answer
   "yes, and here is why" for that string now answers "no, never heard of it" —
   because each one keys off `isPricingTierId`/`isBillingPlanId`, and neither
   recognises a string that was removed from the type entirely.
   `resolveCheckoutPurchase({ plan: 'enterprise', ... })` used to refuse with
   *"Group is quoted per contract..."*; it now refuses with the generic
   *"plan must be..."* message, same as any garbage string. `isContactSalesPlan`
   used to be `true` for it; it is `false` now, and — because Label is
   self-serve again and nothing else is sales-led — **`isContactSalesPlan`
   currently returns `false` for every real input that exists.** The function
   and the `contactSales` field it reads both stay as generic infrastructure for
   whenever a sales-led tier returns, per the removal note in
   `packages/pricing/src/index.ts`, but there is nothing left today for either
   to say yes to.
2. **`quotePlanChange`'s refusal reason is UNCHANGED for this string, but for a
   different reason now.** It refuses a target tier with `!isPricingTierId(target)`
   BEFORE it ever checks `contactSales`, so `'enterprise'` and a genuinely
   made-up id like `'platinum'` hit the exact same branch and the same
   `'sales_led_target'` reason code. That reason code already meant "not a real,
   buyable tier" more than it meant "sales-led specifically" — Group's removal
   just makes that the only reading left.
3. **TWO THINGS WERE DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE, both defensive rather than
   load-bearing.** `subscriptions_plan_check` (the Postgres CHECK constraint in
   `20260823100000_pricing_tiers.sql`) still PERMITS the string `'enterprise'` —
   no migration narrows it, because narrowing a constraint read by every billing
   path is real risk for a value nothing writes any more, and the existing
   fail-open behaviour already covers a stray row safely (see point 4).
   `getPlanExpiry` in `billing.ts` also still checks
   `plan === 'custom' || plan === 'enterprise'` as a **plain string comparison**,
   unrelated to `isPricingTierId` — untouched on purpose, so a pre-2026-09-09 row
   that somehow still carries `'enterprise'` keeps its far-future expiry instead
   of falling through to a one-month default.
4. **`resolveTeamTier` was ALREADY safe for this before today, and stays
   safe.** `isPricingTierId('enterprise')` now returns `false`, so it falls
   through to the same "unknown plan" branch every other retired legacy id
   takes, resolving to `'label'` (uncapped) rather than throwing. Nothing had to
   change in `entitlements.ts` for this — it was already written to fail open on
   an unrecognised plan, and Group's removal just moved which branch catches it.
5. **`isRecurringPlan('enterprise')` and `isSelfServeTier('enterprise')` were
   ALREADY `false` before today**, since neither function's literal-comparison
   list ever included `'enterprise'` even while the tier existed (it was
   `contactSales`, so it was never recurring or self-serve in the first place).
   Their behaviour for this string is unchanged; only the comment explaining WHY
   moved from "it's sales-led" to "it no longer exists, and this is now a
   defensive branch for a stray pre-removal row."
6. **The "Most teams" badge move is the simple half.** `recommended: true` moved
   from the `manager` entry to the `solo` entry in `PRICING_TIERS`. Every
   consumer (`TeamWall.tsx`'s `DEFAULT_TIER`, `PricingTierCards.tsx`,
   `PricingStripSection.tsx`) already reads `tier.recommended` rather than
   hardcoding a tier name, so this needed no consumer-side changes beyond
   `TeamWall.tsx`'s `DEFAULT_TIER` constant (which tier).

### Every test file touching a tier was rewritten, not patched

`entitlements.test.ts`, `billing-plans.test.ts`, `tier-limits-guard.test.ts`,
`billing-summary.test.ts`, `plan-change.test.ts` and `billing.test.ts` all had
assertions built on Group actually existing (`PRICING_TIERS.enterprise.label`,
`for (const tier of ['label', 'enterprise'])`, an expected `'contact'`/`'Group'`
CTA or error string). Each was rewritten to assert the new reality — mostly "a
stray `'enterprise'` value now behaves like any other unrecognised plan" — rather
than deleted, since a stray legacy row reaching one of these functions is a real
scenario worth a test even though nothing writes the value any more.

### Verified

The full vitest suite (3190 passing, 30 skipped — apps/web), `eslint .`
**byte-identical to a freshly-stashed clean-tree baseline in both apps**
(3 errors / 78 warnings in apps/web, all three pre-existing in
`WorkspaceView.tsx`'s single-release auto-scope ref access; 0 errors / 2
warnings in apps/homepage, the pre-existing `RoadmapPageClient.tsx` finding)
with **zero new findings** in either — confirmed by stashing this work,
re-linting the reset branch, and comparing counts rather than trusting a
remembered number, since `origin/main` had moved one commit (an unrelated
guided-tours feature, #576) between this branch's base and this work landing.
`tsc --noEmit` clean apart from the documented pre-existing
`confirmed-action.test.ts` errors. `next build` green **by exit code** for both
apps, with `/auth`, `/onboarding`, `/settings`, `/dashboard` (apps/web) and
`/pricing`, `/for-labels`, `/` (apps/homepage) all still `○ Static`.

**Not verified:** nothing has run against real Paystack or in a browser. No
checkout was attempted, the wall has not rendered, and the four-card-to-three-card

build and the copy sweep, not on anything observed. Worth one look after deploy:
