## Deploy Configuration (configured by /setup-deploy)
- Platform: Vercel — monorepo, TWO projects from this one repo:
  - `Web` → https://app.urganize.app (builds `apps/web`)
  - `the-urganization` → https://www.urganize.app (builds `apps/homepage`; **`www.urganize.app` 308s to the bare `urganize.app` apex** — this line said the reverse until 2026-08-13, when a post-deploy health check measured the real chain: `www` → 308 → apex → 200. The "reconcile that doc" note under the URG-118 section is now discharged.)
  - **`the-urganization` HAS an Ignored Build Step and `urganize` does NOT (measured 2026-09-11 from the commit statuses on #579 and #582).** So a push rebuilds the product app always, and the marketing app only when the change reaches it. This bullet said both use `npx turbo-ignore @urganize/<app>`, then said the field was empty on both (founder, 2026-09-08); the first was never true and the second was true until something was installed on the marketing project two days later. The evidence, what it cannot tell you about WHICH command is installed, and the value still to install on `urganize` are all under Hosting above and in *"A docs-only merge no longer costs four deployments"*.
- Production URL: https://app.urganize.app (product) / https://www.urganize.app (marketing)
- Deploy workflow: auto-deploy on push to `main` (production); PRs get preview deployments
- Deploy status command: none (no vercel CLI installed) — poll the production URLs
- Merge method: squash
- Project type: web app (SaaS product + marketing site, Next.js App Router)
- Post-deploy health check: `https://app.urganize.app/auth` must return 200 (public page that exercises the web app end to end); `https://www.urganize.app/` must return 200

### Custom deploy hooks
- Pre-merge: `pnpm test && pnpm lint && pnpm build`
- Deploy trigger: automatic on push to main
- Deploy status: poll production URLs until the new deployment serves (script asset hashes change)
- Health check: `curl -sf https://app.urganize.app/auth` and `curl -sf https://www.urganize.app/`

### Versioning (reversed 2026-07-13 — the repo now tracks a version)

The earlier decision (2026-07-10) NOT to version was an early-stage call and has been **reversed**. The product now has a tracked, incrementing version.

- **Single source of truth:** `packages/changelog/src/index.ts` (the `@urganize/changelog` workspace package — corrected 2026-08-04; this section previously named `apps/homepage/content/changelog.ts`, which is now only a re-export shim of the package, so edits must go to the package). The **top entry's `version`** is the current product version, exported as `CURRENT_VERSION` (derived from `changelog[0].version`, so it can't drift). There is no separate VERSION file — the ledger is the record.
- **All `package.json` versions mirror it.** Root + every workspace (`apps/*` — including `apps/mobile` — and `packages/*`; 10 files as of 2026-08-04) carry the same number. They are bumped together with the ledger, never independently.
- **App-only scope (founder decision, 2026-07-18):** the changelog and the version track the product app (`apps/web`) ONLY. Marketing-site (`apps/homepage`) changes, however visible on the site (homepage copy, pricing display, OG/share images, brand/team/press/roadmap pages), never earn a ledger entry or a version bump. Pricing display updates count as marketing under this rule. Applied retroactively on 2026-07-18: marketing entries were purged from the ledger and the version recalculated (0.14.7 dropped to 0.14.3). Removed numbers stay retired, survivors keep their historical numbers, and gaps in the sequence are expected.
- **Current version:** whatever the ledger's top entry says, always read it from there. Do not restate the number in this file: an earlier revision hardcoded `0.10.0` here and drifted. Versions before v0.10.0 in the ledger are reconstructed milestones; strict per-release semver applies from v0.10.0 forward.
- **`v1.0.0` SHIPPED 2026-08-24 (founder call).** It was reserved for AI activation, and the founder called that met once UrgAns was running on a real tool-calling model in production (RodiumAi, `openai/gpt-4o-mini` — see the AI integration section). Note "AI activation" was judged on the assistant rather than on all three surfaces. **Corrected 2026-09-07, twice in one day.** It first said both the planner and the status generator were still behind their own flags; the correction to that said only the planner still was. Both readings were wrong in the same direction: the status generator had been live since v0.33.0 (2026-07-26) and the planner since v0.53.0 (2026-08-14), so all three AI surfaces were already on when 1.0.0 shipped, and the caveat was unnecessary rather than merely imprecise. There is nothing left here to flip for a second 1.0.
- **Bump rules (from 1.0 on):** patch (`1.0.x`) = fixes/polish; minor (`1.x.0`) = new user-facing feature(s); major = a breaking change. Before 1.0 the middle number was the feature counter and the same rules applied one place to the right.

### Release procedure (how to ship a version)

When shipping a **user-facing app change** (a new feature, visible behavior change, or bug fix in `apps/web` that a user of the product would notice):

1. Add a release entry at the **top** of `changelog` in `packages/changelog/src/index.ts`: `{ version, date, highlights }`. Bump `version` per the rules above; `date` is a display string (e.g. `"July 13, 2026"`). Batch same-day changes into one entry rather than minting a version per commit.

   **Voice rules for `highlights` (founder call, 2026-08-24 — the v0.61.0 entry was rejected as "too bogus and technical" and rewritten):**
   - **A fifth grader has to understand it.** Short everyday words. If a sentence needs a second read, rewrite it.
   - **Straight to the point.** One or two short sentences per highlight, and few highlights. Do not explain the mechanism, the trade-off, or the reasoning — say what the user can now do. The pre-2026-08-24 entries are the wordy house style this rule replaces; leave them as the historical record and do not copy their tone.
   - **Say "you", not "users" or "your team can now".** No jargon, no file names, no flag names, no feature-branding.
   - **NEVER put a marketing-site (`apps/homepage`) change in here.** This is the in-app announcement, and it covers the product app only. The app-only scope rule under Versioning already said so and it was broken anyway on v0.61.0 (a pricing-page bullet), so treat this as the second, louder statement of the same rule: if the change is on urganize.app rather than app.urganize.app, it does not go in the ledger at all.
2. Set every `package.json` `version` (root + all workspaces) to the new number.
3. That's the whole ceremony — no git tag, no separate CHANGELOG.md. Production still deploys continuously from `main`; the ledger renders publicly at `/changelog` with a "current version" badge.

Skip internal-only work (refactors, dependency bumps, test/tooling, docs) AND all marketing-site (`apps/homepage`) work, however visible on the site: neither earns a ledger entry, and neither requires a version bump (see the app-only scope rule under Versioning). gstack `/ship`'s version step now **applies** here (steps 1–2 above) rather than being skipped, but only for `apps/web` changes; PR titles still use plain conventional-commit prefixes (no `vX.Y.Z` prefix).

### Reading the ledger backwards (2026-09-07)

The ledger is also the only in-repo record of **when a feature flag was
flipped**, because the procedure above puts the entry at the flip rather than
at merge. Four sessions have now used it to settle a stale "not yet activated"
claim, and it is worth writing down what it can and cannot answer, because the
test is weaker than it first looks.

**A ledger entry is strong evidence when it ANNOUNCES a capability** — "Added
Notes", "You can pitch your songs to playlists from inside Urganize", "You can
plan EPs and albums now" — and stronger still when it reports a BUG in a flow,
since nobody observes a bug in a surface that 404s. v0.56.2's *"used to walk
you through the seven rollout questions and then stop with 'there is already a
release plan'"* is the sharpest example: it pins a flag state by naming a
message only a reachable route can produce.

**It is NOT evidence when it ENUMERATES a set in passing**, and this was
proven rather than assumed. v1.1.3 (2026-08-25) reads *"Collect metadata, your
calendar, files and your press kit were being squeezed into a narrow strip"* —
while the working-notes section written for that very pass says outright that
`NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_FILES` **is off in production** and that the file scene
was deliberately left out of the fix. Six entries between v0.39.0 and v1.1.3
name Files as a live release surface and it has been off since v0.16.4. So a
list of scenes in a layout entry is the full possible set, not the switched-on
set, and reading one as a flag state gives a false positive.

**A NEGATIVE only narrows.** No entry means the flip was never recorded, which
is a documented failure mode here rather than proof the flag is off — the
mobile shell, Web Push, the team brief and `workspace-summary.ts` all shipped
with no entry at all, and Fan capture's switch-ON is still unrecorded while
its switch-OFF is in v1.21.0.

**And it dates a flip, never the present.** A flag can be switched off later
with no entry (metadata, capture and the content calendar were switched off
WITH one, in v1.21.0, which is the exception). So the honest form of a resolved
status is "LIVE from vX.Y.Z on <date>; nothing records it being switched off;
whether it is on today is not answerable from the repo" — which is what the
sections corrected in this sweep now say.

## UrgAns tailoring reliability + a persona (2026-09-08, v1.32.0)

Founder report: a plan `generate` came back *"UrgAns could not tailor it this
time, so nothing was changed."* That is the generic one-off-failure copy in
`PlanScene.tsx`, not the "not switched on" one, so the gateway was configured
and a real tailoring call failed. He also asked for two follow-ons: give
UrgAns a real character (strict, bossy, a creative who wants things *done*),
and make sure its output always reads clean.

**The retry bug.** `lib/ai/provider.ts`'s `generateStructuredAiOutput` and
`generatePlainTextAiOutput` only marked a failure `retryable` when the gateway
returned a classified 429/5xx, or when running on OpenRouter's free
auto-router. A client-side `AbortError` — our own timeout firing — went
through neither path and fell back to `retryable: isFreeAutoRouter`, which is
`false` for every real deployment (RodiumAi is not the auto-router). So a
timeout was fatal on attempt one no matter how high `maxRetries` was set —
directly contradicting the planner route's own comment, which sets
`maxDuration = 60` on the stated assumption that `PLANNER_TIMEOUT_MS` (25s) ×
`PLANNER_MAX_RETRIES` (2) attempts actually happen. Fixed by making an
`AbortError` retryable on its own merits in both functions, the same as a
429/5xx — a slow response says nothing about the next attempt. Covered by the
new `lib/ai/provider.test.ts` (mocked `fetch`: one abort then a success
confirms a second attempt fires; a second case confirms it still gives up once
`maxRetries` is exhausted).

**The persona.** `lib/chappi/system-prompt.ts`'s `ROLE` and
`lib/release-planning.ts`'s `buildSystemPrompt` (the tailoring call that
writes the plan's `rationale`, `reason`, `warnings` and rewritten "why" lines
— everything the manager reads as coming from UrgAns) both gained the same
"Who you are" / "Voice" paragraph: strict, a little bossy, a creative who
cares about one outcome — getting the release out — and pushes rather than
just reports. `system-prompt.test.ts`'s coverage tests (every registered tool
named in `ROLE`, no unregistered name mentioned) and its two content
assertions (`compare_releases`/`get_team_workload` named, ideation sanctioned,
the no-streaming-data admission) all still pass — the persona text is plain
prose with no snake_case tokens, so it cannot trip the stale-tool-name check.

**The formatting bug.** Assistant replies render as raw `whitespace-pre-wrap`
plain text (`ChappiConversation.tsx`) — there is no markdown renderer anywhere
in this stack, and adding one was out of scope (boring-stack rule). So any
`**bold**` or `#` heading the model wrote was showing up as literal
punctuation. Both prompts above now explicitly forbid markdown syntax in every
string value (no asterisks, no headers, no backticks) and ask for a plain
`"- "` prefix when a list genuinely helps.

`release-planning.test.ts`'s exact-substring assertions on `buildSystemPrompt`
(`'You cannot add tasks.'`, `'NEVER drop a task whose "optional" is false'`,
the phase-scoping line) were checked against the edit and still pass — the
persona paragraph was inserted around them, not through them.

**Not verified against production or a real model call** — this session has
no route to either urganize domain and cannot mint a session, so the retry fix
rests on the traced bug plus the new unit tests, and the persona/formatting
change rests on the prompt text plus `vitest`/`eslint`/`tsc` passing clean.
Worth one real pass once deployed: generate a plan for a release with a tight
budget vs. a comfortable one and confirm the rationale reads differently and
in voice, and watch whether "could not tailor" gets rarer. No migration, no
new flag — both surfaces (Chappi, the release planner) are already live.

## The side menu is draggable too, and "New release" is "New rollout" (2026-09-09, v1.34.0)

Founder: make the side menu adjustable like the UrgAns window, horizontal axis
only, and change the copy from "new release" to "new rollout". Two unrelated
asks in one message; the first is the one with consequences.

**No migration, no route, no new flag** — the card is already behind
`NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_IDENTITY_PANEL`, and the rename is copy.

### The width contest is now two-way, and that is the whole of it

The rail's own module already argued why its maximum exists: it is a flex
SIBLING of `<main>`, and two release scenes swap layout on CONTAINER queries of
that centre column (Content at 45rem, Timeline at 34rem), so a column dragged
too wide silently degrades a week grid into the phone list on a desktop.
Making the OTHER column draggable turns that one-way reservation into a
negotiation, and getting it wrong is invisible on screen.

1. **`resolveRailBounds`'s second parameter is a WIDTH now, not a boolean.**
   `IDENTITY_PANEL_TOTAL = 272` was fine while the card was a fixed 240px; a
   card dragged to 420 leaves it under-reserving by 148px, and every one of
   those pixels comes out of `MAIN_MINIMUM`. **It was also 32px short at 240
   all along**, having counted the card's `mr-8` and forgotten its `ml-8` —
   both are real horizontal space, which is why `sidebarTotalWidth` exists and
   why nothing should hand this function a hand-built number.
2. **`MAIN_MINIMUM` moved into `lib/layout-columns.ts`.** It was private to
   `lib/rail-width.ts`, and a second copy in the sidebar's module is exactly
   the drift this repo keeps correcting. One floor, two columns that respect it.
3. **THE TWO CONSTRAINTS SETTLE RATHER THAN OSCILLATE, and the reason is that
   every clamp only ever shrinks.** Worked through at the tightest real case,
   1280px with both columns present: open the rail against a 420px menu and the
   menu's max drops to 304, so it shrinks; the rail's own max then recomputes
   against 304+64 and lands on 320; `<main>` comes to rest at exactly 560. No
   feedback loop, because nothing in either direction ever grows a column.
4. **`lib/sidebar-width.ts` is deliberately NOT one parameterised module with
   the rail's.** They share the floor and nothing else: opposite edges, so
   opposite drag signs; different ranges, because a nav column and a
   conversation column want different amounts of room; and only one of them
   collapses. A "which edge" flag threaded through every function is how the
   sign gets flipped by accident, which is the single failure the rail's module
   already singles out for a test. Both directions are now pinned, and a test
   asserts they run opposite ways.
5. **The menu reserves the rail's RAW stored width, not the rail's clamped
   one.** They converge on the next frame, and while they disagree this
   over-reserves — which is the safe direction, since it shrinks our own
   maximum rather than main's floor.

### Six things worth knowing before editing the control

0. **UNTIL THE VIEWPORT IS MEASURED, the stored width renders UNCLAMPED — and
   this one was a real defect caught in review rather than a precaution.** A
   viewport of 0 means "not known yet", not "too small", and the locked
   fallback's `max` is the MINIMUM, so clamping against it painted the card at
   208px and jumped it to 240 the moment the measure effect landed. **The rail
   never had to deal with this because it is CLOSED on first paint**; this card
   is visible immediately. The handle is withheld while unmeasured either way,
   so there is nothing to drag against a bound nobody has worked out yet.
1. **NO `relative` on the `<aside>`.** It is already `sticky`, which is a
   positioned ancestor, so the handle anchors to it as it is. Adding both
   leaves which one applies up to Tailwind's utility ordering — and losing
   `sticky` un-pins the whole card. (The rail's aside carries both and works
   only because Tailwind happens to emit `sticky` last; do not copy that.)
2. **The width transition is removed while dragging.** It animates `width`, so
   every frame would lag the cursor — the same trap the rail records, and the
   most likely way for this to look broken.
3. **The handle is withheld while collapsed**, as well as when the viewport
   cannot pay for any movement: 64px has nothing to grow into, and a control
   that cannot move is worse than none.
4. **The corrective clamp is skipped while collapsed.** The card is 64px then,
   so the stored expanded width is not on screen and must not be rewritten by a
   bound it is not currently subject to — otherwise collapsing on a tight
   viewport would quietly shrink the width the user chose for the expanded one.
5. **`collapsed` moved out of local state into `stores/useSidebarStore.ts`,
   which reverses a documented call.** That note said it stayed local "because
   nothing outside this panel toggles it" — still true of WRITES, and no longer
   true of reads: `ChappiSidePanel` has to know this column's effective width,
   and that is 64px whenever it is collapsed. The storage key and version are
   unchanged, so an existing account keeps its collapsed choice. Writes are
   guarded, because `writePersistedState` does not wrap `setItem` (Safari
   private mode, full quota) and a width that cannot be saved should still
   apply for the session.

**A side effect worth knowing rather than fixing: collapsing the menu now
raises the RAIL's ceiling.** It follows from the reservation being real, and it
is the mechanical version of what the card's own comment already claimed —
that collapsing is the user's own fix for a squeezed centre column.

### The rename, and the keyword it required

"New release" → **"New rollout"** on the topbar pill, the mobile "+"
(aria-label and title), the below-`sm` column button, the create modal's
heading, the UrgAns chip and its tooltip, and the deterministic reply.

**IT IS NOT A GLOBAL FIND-AND-REPLACE, and the two strings left alone are the
line.** The release is still the release — the central object, in the schema and
in every other surface — so `ReleaseCombobox`'s "New release will be created
inline and selected automatically" stays: that hint is about a release RECORD
being created in a picker, not about the CTA. So does the changelog's own
history, which is a log. What changed is the name of the ACTION.

**The functional half: `resolveIntent` matched `'release'` and NOT `'rollout'`,
so renaming the copy alone would have broken a control.** `buildHelpReply`'s
suggestions are clickable and are fed straight back through that function, so
"Create a new rollout" would have answered with the help card it came from —
the "a control that visibly does nothing" failure this repo keeps recording.
`'rollout'`/`'roll out'` are in the release branch now, which also means
someone who reads the new button and types what it says gets the create form.
With the planner ON the planner branch above claims those words first, so the
addition is only ever reached with it off, which is exactly the state that
renders that suggestion. Pinned by a test that asserts the ACTUAL suggestion
string rather than a paraphrase, so renaming the copy again without the keyword
fails there.

**21 comment references to `"New release"` were updated too.** They quote the
control by its label, which is what a future grep for the button hits, and a
stale quoted label is the drift this file records elsewhere (the confirmation
gate named `revoke_epk_link` for months after that tool was deleted).

### Verified

**3012 tests** (27 new: 25 in `lib/sidebar-width.test.ts`, 2 on the rail's new
coupling, 2 on the router keyword), `eslint .` at **3 errors / 80 warnings**
against a measured clean-tree baseline of 3 / 81 — **one FEWER**, and the
per-file diff confirms it is a removal rather than a swap: **zero new
findings**, and the old collapse-hydration effect's `set-state-in-effect`
warning went away when it became a store action. `tsc --noEmit` clean apart
from one pre-existing stale `.next/types/validator.ts` reference to the EPK
route deleted 2026-09-05. `next build` green **by exit code** with the identity
panel and Chappi flags ON and with them OFF, `/auth`, `/onboarding`,
`/settings` and `/dashboard` all still `○ Static` in each — `/settings`
particularly, since the card is mounted app-wide and this added a store read to
it. Compiled output checked rather than trusted from source, this repo's habit
for anything CSS-dependent: `cursor:col-resize`, `touch-action:none` and
`user-select:none` are all in the emitted CSS, and "New rollout" plus the
handle's label are in the client chunks.

**Three mutation passes, each printing `APPLIED` first and each failing exactly
its own tests:** reversing the sidebar drag direction (4), making the rail
ignore the menu's real width (3), and removing the `'rollout'` keyword (1).

**NOT verified, and it is the whole remaining risk: nothing has rendered in a
browser.** This sandbox cannot mint an authenticated session and has no route
to app.urganize.app, so the handle's feel, the two columns settling against
each other, the keyboard path and the double-click reset all rest on unit tests
plus the build. Worth one pass at two widths: drag the menu wider on a 1280px
window with the UrgAns rail open and confirm neither column strands the centre;
collapse the menu and confirm the rail can then go wider; reload and confirm
the width came back. Do NOT try to check the flag from the bundle — both
ternary branches compile in, a false positive this file records six times.

## Pitching gets a page; press kits move to Settings (2026-09-09, v1.36.0)

Two founder messages, one PR. A third in the same batch — "fold shows to be
possible inside per release" — was **withdrawn before any code was written**
("shows should be seperate, i change my mind"), so shows are untouched; the
research that went into it is worth keeping and is at the end of this section.

### Press kits left every menu (founder: "only accessible through settings")

Removed from all four surfaces that carried it: the identity card's nav row,
the topbar icon, the mobile bar's trailing tab, and `lib/app-pages.ts`'s search
catalog. `lib/prefetch-routes.ts` lost it too, since it is no longer a nav
destination and `/settings` is already a base route.

**THE PAGES DID NOT MOVE, and that was the whole design decision.** They still
live at `/dashboard/press-kits`, reached from one new `PressKitsSection` in
Settings → Profile. Moving the route under `/settings` was the other option
and is materially worse: it breaks `PostPlanKitPrompt`'s "Open the press kit"
CTA, any UrgAns `navigate` action pointed there, and every bookmark, and it
would put a heavy client page with its own modals and stores inside a route
whose skeleton contract requires it stay `○ Static`.

Three things worth knowing:

1. **The search catalog entry went, but findability did not.** "Press kit",
   "epk" and "bio" now match SETTINGS, through its keyword list — the same
   mechanism that already makes "billing" find Settings, and for the same
   stated reason ("a manager looking for their card details types 'billing',
   and nothing in the app is labelled that"). Settings is the honest answer to
   those words now. A test asserts both halves: no press-kits page entry with
   the flag ON, and those three queries reaching `/settings`.
2. **It sits in the Profile tab rather than Account** because a kit belongs to
   an artist on the roster, which is what the artist rows in that tab are
   already about. Above `ReleasesSection`, which is destructive and stays last.
   (That tab's label became **Profile** in v1.35.0; its file is still
   `tabs/WorkspaceTab.tsx`, so the code name and the label disagree by design.)
3. **`PostPlanKitPrompt` was deliberately left alone.** It is a contextual,
   self-suppressing banner after a plan is approved (it renders nothing unless
   the kit exists and has real proposals), not app chrome — and it is the one
   moment a manager has a reason to think about a kit at all.

### Pitching became app-wide, which needed a page first

The founder asked for pitching in the phone's bottom bar, the desktop side
menu and the top bar. **That was not buildable as asked, and the reason is the
useful part: the team side of pitching was a release SCENE** (`?scene=pitch`),
so every entry point to it required a release already scoped. A menu item
pointing at it had nowhere to go. The only pitching entry in the nav was the
dual-account crossing to `/curator`, which is the opposite direction.

So `/dashboard/pitching` is new: every pitch this team has sent, grouped by
release with each curator's answer, plus a composer that sends a new one once
you pick the release. **The release scene stays** (founder call) — one tap from
the release you are working on, and both surfaces render the same two
components, so they cannot drift into offering different fields.

**Seven things worth knowing before editing this:**

1. **THE TEAM-WIDE READ IS FILTERED TWICE, and the second filter is the one
   that matters.** `releaseOwnerIds` is a TEAM boundary, not a per-release one,
   so `.in('owner_user_id', ownerIds)` alone would hand an artist-scoped
   teammate every pitch their team ever sent, including for releases they are
   not allowed to see. The referenced releases are loaded in one query and each
   row goes through the shared `decideReleaseAccess` — named for releases and
   generic in fact, the same rule the events list uses for the same reason.
   Cloning it as SQL is how eleven route groups drifted apart.
2. **That filter FAILS CLOSED**, unlike nearly every counter in this app. A
   release that cannot be read back is one this caller should not be told
   about; the cost of being wrong is showing somebody another artist's work
   rather than refusing an action they could retry.
3. **A pitch whose release was deleted survives on the owner check alone.**
   `playlist_pitches.release_id` is `on delete set null`, so a pitch outlives
   its release by design, the curator may still answer, and hiding the row
   would lose that answer. `groupPitchesByRelease` collects them into one last
   group and the page labels it "Release removed".
4. **`SENT_PITCH_COLUMNS` gained `release_id`, and `lib/pitching-columns-guard.test.ts`
   exists because of it.** The curator's own list (`CURATOR_PITCH_COLUMNS`)
   carries no release, owner or playlist id ON PURPOSE, so their read path
   cannot follow anything back into a team's data. The two lists are now nearly
   identical, which makes "share one constant" a tempting and completely wrong
   tidy-up that no comment could stop. Mutation-tested: adding `release_id` to
   the curator list fails.
5. **`groupPitchesByRelease` keys on the release ID, never the title.** Two
   releases can share a name, and merging them would show one release the
   other's answers. Ordered by each group's NEWEST pitch rather than by release
   date, so the release actually being worked on rises to the top. Both
   mutation-tested, along with the orphan group's position.
6. **The page reads NO search params**, so it stays `○ Static` (verified in the
   build) and needs no Suspense boundary — the trap recorded for `/auth` and
   for `MobileNavBar`. The release picker's value is DERIVED rather than seeded
   by an effect: the manager's choice when they have made one, the first
   release otherwise, falling back again if a chosen release disappears from
   the catalog. An effect would have cost a `set-state-in-effect` warning AND
   left a render where nothing was selected and the composer sat disabled.
7. **The two pitching entries must stay distinguishable.** `/dashboard/pitching`
   is Pitching, glyph `Radio` (the release pill's own mark); `/curator` is
   Playlist pitches, glyph `Inbox`. The mobile bar's labels are `sr-only`, so
   the glyph is the whole visual difference — and that bar's curator label was
   widened from the bare "Pitches" to the fuller "Playlist pitches" so a screen
   reader does not hear two near-identical names in one bar. That also fixed a
   pre-existing disagreement, since the side menu already called it that.

- **The nav count is FLAT in every surface**, which is what made this cheap:
  Pitching took the slot Press kits left, in all three. The mobile bar's worst
  case is still seven (Home, UrgAns, Notes, Shows, Pitching, Directory, and
  Playlist pitches for a dual account); the topbar's control count is unchanged,
  so its documented width budget still holds.
- **Two real bugs fixed in the assistant's `list_pitches`, both silent.** It
  sent `?release=` where the route reads `releaseId`, so **that tool answered
  400 on every call it has ever made**; and it read `pitch.curatorReply` where
  the payload's field is `reply`, so the curator's answer — the only thing worth
  asking it for — would have come back null even once the request worked.
  `releaseId` is optional there now, matching the route, so "what have we
  pitched" is answerable at all.
- **`SentPitch` gained two fields additively** (`releaseId`, `releaseTitle`), so
  persisted `pitch` scene payloads from before this still parse; the scene does
  not read either.

### Verified

**3015 tests** (22 new: the grouping and scope helpers in `lib/pitching.test.ts`,
the column guard, and the two nav-list suites), `eslint .` at **3 errors / 82
warnings** against a **measured** clean-tree baseline of 3 / 81 — the one new
warning is the fetch-on-mount `set-state-in-effect` downgrade, confirmed
byte-identical in shape by linting `TeamsAdminPageClient.tsx` rather than
asserting the precedent. `tsc --noEmit` clean apart from the documented
pre-existing `confirmed-action.test.ts` errors. `next build` green **by exit
code** with both flags on and with both off, `/auth`, `/onboarding`,
`/settings`, `/dashboard` and `/dashboard/pitching` all `○ Static` in each.

Runtime probes on `next start`, rebuilding between flag states because
`NEXT_PUBLIC_*` is inlined at build time even server-side: **flag off**, the
team-wide `GET /api/pitching/pitches` returns **404** with body exactly
`{"error":"Not found."}` while the ungated `/api/releases` **401**s; **flag
on**, both the team-wide and the per-release form **401** unauthenticated. That
404-vs-401 discrimination is what proves the gate rather than a routing
accident.

**Four mutation passes, each killing exactly its own tests** and each printing
`APPLIED` first (the recorded lesson that a mutation which never landed is
indistinguishable from a survivor): grouping by title instead of id, orphans
first, orphans dropped entirely, and `release_id` added to the curator column
list.

**A FIXTURE BUG CAUGHT BY ITS OWN TESTS, worth recording because it is the
second instance of this shape in this repo.** Two of the new grouping tests
failed on first run and the implementation was correct: the fixture built its
nullable fields with `??`, which coalesces an explicit `null` to the default —
so the two cases named after a deleted release and an unresolved title were
never actually passing null. It uses `'field' in over` now. The directory's
Phase 5 hit the mirror image (a fixture ordered so "last wins" accidentally
picked the right row).

### NOT verified

**Nothing has rendered in a browser.** This sandbox cannot mint a session and
has no route to app.urganize.app, so the page, the picker, the grouped list,
the Settings row and all three nav entries rest on the build, the unit tests
and traced call paths. **No pitch has been sent and no team-wide read has run
against a real database**, so the double filter in point 1 has never been
exercised with real rows — which is the one thing most worth a real pass.

Manual pass at merge: open Pitching from each of the three menus; confirm the
list groups by release and a curator's reply shows; send a pitch and confirm it
appears in the right group; open Settings → Profile → Press kits and confirm
the page opens; confirm no Press kits row, icon or tab remains anywhere; and on
a dual account confirm Pitching and Playlist pitches are both present and go to
different places.

### Shows inside a release: researched, then withdrawn

Recorded so the next person asking does not re-derive it. **There is no
release↔event edge in the schema at all**: `events` carries `artist_id` and no
`release_id`, and the only join is `songs.release_id` → `setlist_items.song_id`
— a path nothing on the release side populates, because the release "Song"
scene writes to `assets` rather than to `public.songs`. So a per-release Shows
scene could only ever have listed the release's ARTIST'S shows, identically for
two releases by the same artist.

It would have been cheap to build (`GET /api/events` takes no params, loads the
whole accessible set and filters in memory, and `CreateShowModal` already
accepts a one-artist array), and it runs straight into three dated decisions:
the 2026-08-30 scope expansion that made Event a SIBLING of Release rather than
a child, Principle 1's amendment recording that, and
`WorkspaceIdentityPanel`'s own comment that Shows "is not a release scene and
never carries `?release=`". Adding one is a founder call against that record,
not a default — and the founder withdrew it.

## The menu drags all the way into its collapsed rail (2026-09-09, v1.38.0)

Founder, the day after the menu became draggable: *"make it so it is
collapsible up until it's in collapsed view - remove teamate and release count
from there as well so it matches closed and open, then team names and artist
should be on the same line as the logo, horizintally so it all matches closed
and opened"*.

Three asks, one theme: **the expanded card and the collapsed rail should read as
one thing in two sizes.** No migration, no route, no new flag — the card is
already behind `NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_IDENTITY_PANEL`.

### The first ask REVERSES a decision recorded a day earlier, deliberately

`lib/sidebar-width.ts` said of `COLLAPSED_SIDEBAR_WIDTH`, in as many words,
that it is **"NOT a bound: a collapsed card is not resizable at all (64px has
no room for a label to grow into)"**, and the handle was gated
`!collapsed && bounds.resizable` to match. Both halves are now reversed on a
founder call, and the constant's comment records the reversal rather than being
edited into looking like it always said this — the old reasoning was sound, and
it is still exactly what keeps the card from rendering at any width in between.

**Five things worth knowing before editing this:**

1. **ONE threshold serves both directions.** `SIDEBAR_COLLAPSE_AT = 160`:
   cross it moving left and the card becomes the rail, cross it moving right
   and the rail comes back at `MIN_SIDEBAR_WIDTH`. A separate expand threshold
   would give the control hysteresis nobody asked for and two numbers to keep
   in step.
2. **It sits BELOW the minimum, not at it**, so collapsing takes a clear 48px
   overshoot rather than happening to anyone who drags the card as narrow as it
   goes. Through that overshoot the card is pinned at 208 and then snaps — it
   is never drawn in between, which is `MIN_SIDEBAR_WIDTH`'s own reasoning
   ("a worse version of the collapsed icon rail it already offers") doing its
   original job rather than being overridden.
3. **A COLLAPSED STATE CARRIES NO WIDTH.** `SidebarState` is a union
   (`{collapsed:true} | {collapsed:false; width}`), not a `{collapsed, width}`
   pair, and that is the point of it: the width the user dragged to has to
   survive a collapse so expanding restores it rather than the default, so a
   collapsed result that carried a width would be the one shape able to clobber
   it. Mutation-tested.
4. **A drag STARTS from what is on screen.** For a collapsed card that is the
   rail's own 64px, never the stored expanded width — otherwise the first pixel
   of movement jumps the card to a width the user cannot see. It is also why a
   nonsense coordinate returns the start state **unchanged** rather than
   clamping it: clamping 64 lands on the minimum and silently expands a card
   nobody touched. That one has its own test, and the mutation for it kills
   exactly that test and nothing else.
5. **The crossing goes through React; the width does not.** The drag still
   paints a CSS variable per frame, but a collapse is a change of SHAPE rather
   than of width, so `previewCollapsed` state is set on a CROSSING only — at
   most twice per gesture. Without it the card would sit unchanged under the
   pointer and only snap on release, which is not what "collapsible up until
   it's in collapsed view" describes.

The keyboard got the same twin (`sidebarStateFromStep`), because otherwise the
gesture would be reachable with a pointer and not without one on a control that
is deliberately keyboard-operable everywhere else: one step narrower than the
minimum collapses, widening out of the rail returns, and `End`/`Home` are now
the two real ends of the range. It does not reuse the drag's overshoot — a
keypress is deliberate where a drag can be a slip. `aria-valuemin` is the
rail's width now rather than `MIN_SIDEBAR_WIDTH`, which is simply honest: the
bottom of this control's range moved.

**The handle stays withheld when the viewport cannot pay for any movement**,
and that case needs no special pleading: it is also the case where expanding is
impossible, so nothing is lost but the footer's collapse button.

### One shared mark, which is what the other two asks really wanted

The counts paragraph is gone, and the logo, team name and artist are one
`flex items-center gap-3` row at the collapsed state's 40px mark. That left the
two branches rendering the same thing, so they now genuinely are the same
thing: `TeamMark` is one implementation with a `className` for the collapsed
`mx-auto`. `min-w-0` on the text column is load-bearing — without it the column
takes its content's width and pushes the mark out instead of truncating.

**The dedup proved itself in the lint numbers rather than by inspection:** the
file went from five findings to one, and the whole repo from the measured
3-error/81-warning baseline to 3/77. Two of those four came from collapsing two
`<img>` copies into one. The other two came from a real bug the copies were
hiding — **`// eslint-disable-next-line` was sitting above a two-line
explanation, so it landed on a comment and suppressed nothing while the rule
fired anyway.** Both original copies had it. The directive has to be the line
DIRECTLY above the element; the explanation goes above the directive.

Also fixed in passing: the panel's own JSDoc had drifted **above the helper
functions**, so it read as documentation for whichever one came first, and it
still promised "a couple of at-a-glance counts" (just removed) and pointed at
"Settings -> Workspace identity" (renamed Profile by the 2026-09-09 positioning
pass). Moved to the function it documents and corrected.

`WorkspaceSkeleton` needed no change, checked rather than assumed: it reserves
only the identity panel's PRESENCE (breakpoint shifts for its own release
rails), never the identity block's internals. The in-file skeleton branch is
what the loading-skeleton-sync rule applies to here, and it moved to the same
row shape.

### Verified

**3131 tests** (net +12: 18 new, 6 retired with `sidebarWidthFromDrag`), so a
baseline of **3119**. Re-measured on the merged tree, and the numbers here are
NOT the ones this work was verified against before merging — three PRs landed on
`main` while the branch was open (#571's rollout rename, #572's Pitching page,
#573), which is also why it ships as v1.38.0 rather than the v1.36.0 it was
written as. The delta is derived rather than stashed this time, and it is safe to
derive: `lib/sidebar-width.test.ts` is the ONLY test file that differs from
`main`, at 37 tests against its 25. `eslint .` at **3 errors / 77 warnings**
against a measured 3/81 — measured on this tree by swapping `main`'s copy of the
panel in, linting it (5 findings), and swapping mine back (1), confirming the
change is a reduction rather than a swap and **zero** new findings.
`tsc --noEmit` clean apart from the documented
pre-existing `confirmed-action.test.ts` errors. `next build` green **by exit
code** with the identity panel flag ON and OFF, `/auth`, `/onboarding`,
`/settings` and `/dashboard` all still `○ Static` in each — `/settings`
particularly, since this added state to a component mounted app-wide, and the
`ScopedArtistLine` Suspense isolation that keeps those static was left alone.
Compiled chunks confirm the panel's counts copy is gone rather than merely
hidden. One "active rollout" string does survive in the bundle and is a
different surface — `DashboardPageClient`'s own line, the LegacyDashboard kept
as the documented revert path — so grep for it expecting exactly that one hit.

**Five mutations, each printing `APPLIED` first and each killing exactly its own
tests:** the collapse comparison reversed, the threshold moved up to the
minimum, a collapsed outcome carrying a width, a nonsense coordinate clamping
instead of holding, and the keyboard step's direction flipped while collapsed.

**A probe error of my own, recorded because the shape recurs.** A first pass
reported `space-y-1.5` MISSING from the compiled CSS and nearly sent me fixing
a non-bug: the probe matched `.<class>{`, and `space-y-*` compiles as
`.space-y-1\.5>:not([hidden])~:not([hidden]){…}` — a child selector, so the
pattern could never match. Same class of mistake as the multi-byte
box-drawing grep this file already records. **Check what the utility actually
compiles to before believing it is absent.**

### Not verified

**Nothing has rendered in a browser.** This sandbox cannot mint an
authenticated session and has no route to app.urganize.app, so the feel of
dragging into the rail and back out, the live crossing under the pointer, the
one-row identity block at the 208px minimum, and the keyboard path all rest on
unit tests plus the build. Worth one pass: drag the menu's right edge left until
it collapses, drag it back out, and confirm the width you had before the
collapse is what returns.

## Two guided tours (2026-09-09, flag-off)

Founder request, alongside the rollout rename: show a new manager around
instead of leaving them to find out. Two short Bitwarden-style walkthroughs —
a spotlight cutout, an anchored card, "1 of 3", Next and Skip — behind
`NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_TOURS`, default `false`. **No migration, no route, no new
table**: "seen" is one localStorage key per account per tour.

- **Tour A (catalog)** runs ONCE per account, unasked, on the first visit to
  `/dashboard` in a session.
- **Tour B (rollout)** is OFFERED, never auto-run: an inline card after
  **Approve plan**, which is the moment a release becomes a rollout. It
  replaces the `NewReleaseGuide` banner while the flag is on; flag off, that
  banner is byte-identical to before.

Both are replayable from the `?` help menu (`md+`) and Settings → Account —
the second is what makes replay reachable on a phone, the same reasoning that
put issue reporting there.

### Most of this was already built, and reusing it is the point

`#569`'s pullout system solves three of the four hard problems an overlay has,
and the tours reuse rather than re-derive:

- **`placeHelpTip` (`lib/help-tip-position.ts`) IS the placer.** It already
  prefers a side, flips when there is no room, clamps to a viewport margin and
  never returns a negative offset, and it has its own tests. `TourOverlay`
  calls it with `prefer: 'bottom'`. **Do not write a second one** — a duplicate
  over the same function is the drift this repo keeps correcting.
- **`HelpTip.tsx` is the model for the DOM traps**, both of which it records by
  name: portal to `document.body`, and reposition on **capture-phase** scroll.
- **`lib/help-copy.ts` is the precedent for copy living in `lib/`** with a
  guard over it — vitest reaches `lib/` and nothing else, so copy inline in a
  `.tsx` is copy no guard can hold. The steps live in `lib/tours.ts` for that
  reason, and `lib/tours.ts` is in `rollout-vocabulary.test.ts`'s guarded list.

**What `HelpTip` does NOT do, and the reason this exists at all:** it is
explicitly not a modal — no backdrop, no spotlight, `pointer-events-none` —
because it answers "what is this field" on demand. A tour answers "where am I,
what do I do first", unasked, once. They compose; neither replaces the other.
**Watch the copy overlap:** `help-copy.ts` already explains the side-menu rows
on hover, and Tour A's first two steps sit on those same anchors. The tour
points and moves on; it must not restate the pullout.

### Seven things worth knowing before editing this

1. **"On the catalog" is true by construction, not by matching a pathname.**
   `useCatalogTourAutoStart` is mounted in `WorkspaceView`, not `AppShell`, and
   that placement is the decision: it needs the scoped rollout, its activity
   count and the release list to build the contextual last step. It also
   handles a thing that would otherwise be wrong — `#568` made UrgAns the
   post-auth landing, so a first-run user does not arrive at the catalog at
   all until they tap, and a tour keyed on "landing" would fire on the wrong
   page or never.
2. **Every input to `decideCatalogTourAutoStart` is a reason NOT to start**, so
   it fails toward silence: flag off, already seen, auth unresolved, a curator,
   releases not loaded, another modal holding the body scroll lock, or an
   UrgAns conversation already in progress. That last one matters — the
   assistant is itself an activation path and must not be talked over.
3. **Seen is marked at START, not at finish.** A tour somebody walks away from
   mid-way has still been offered, and re-offering it on the next navigation is
   exactly the interruption this feature exists to avoid. Replay is how they
   ask again. **The consequence, accepted rather than engineered around:** a
   tour whose steps all fail to resolve is burned. It cannot really arise —
   Tour A's first two anchors are nav chrome that exists wherever the overlay
   is mounted, and Tour B is offered from inside the scoped rollout whose panel
   carries its anchors.
4. **The last step of Tour A is contextual**, resolved by
   `resolveCatalogTourCta` in precedence order: plan the scoped rollout
   (planner on, nothing scheduled yet), create the first one, or just open one.
   So it hands off into real work rather than ending on a shrug. Planning beats
   creating, and a mutation reversing that fails a named test.
5. **The backdrop swallows a click and does not skip.** A tour is three steps
   and an accidental tap losing it is worse than a stray click doing nothing;
   Skip is right there and says what it does. Escape does skip.
6. **No body scroll lock**, unlike every dialog in this app — the anchors live
   in scrollable panels and `scrollIntoView` has to work. Z-tiers are
   `z-[210]`/`z-[211]`: above sheets (170) and toasts (200) so neither can
   cover the card, below the heavy dialog tier so anything the user
   deliberately opens wins.
7. **A running OR requested tour holds back the first-release prompt.**
   `useFirstReleasePrompt` gained both halves: `tourBlocking` (subscribed) on
   the ARMING effect, so the ~30s countdown starts after a tour ends rather
   than running underneath it, and `tourBlocksPrompts()` as a fifth fire-time
   guard. `pendingReplay` counts, because the prompt must not fire into the gap
   between asking for a tour and landing where it runs.

### Anchors

`data-tour="…"` is a new convention — none existed before. Eight names, listed
in `TourAnchor`, carried by `MobileNavBar` (via a new optional `dataTour` prop
on `NavTab`), `AppTopbar` (both Catalog branches, all three UrgAns renderings,
the "You" link, both create buttons), `WorkspaceIdentityPanel` (derived in the
row renderer from `TOUR_ANCHOR_BY_HREF`), `PlanReleaseCard`, `TasksPanel` (the
`<aside>`, the mobile hamburger and the desktop pill row) and
`WorkspaceReleaseCard`. Several are carried in more than one place on purpose —
`pickVisibleAnchor` takes whichever one is actually on screen at the width the
tour is running at, which is what makes the same step work on a phone and at
`lg+` without a viewport branch. **They are inert with the flag off**, which is
why they are unconditional markup rather than gated.

### Verified

3190 tests, of which 27 are new in `lib/tours.test.ts` (written red-first), `eslint .` at
**3 errors / 78 warnings** against a baseline of **3 / 77** measured on a clean
`origin/main` worktree — the one new warning is `TourOverlay`'s portal mount
guard, byte-identical in shape to the finding `DeleteReleaseDialog` already
carries, and there are **zero** new errors. `tsc --noEmit` clean apart from the
documented pre-existing `confirmed-action.test.ts` errors. `next build` green
**by exit code** in BOTH flag states, with `/auth`, `/onboarding`, `/settings`
and `/dashboard` all still `○ Static` in each.

**Four mutations, each killing exactly the tests written for it** and each
printing `APPLIED` first, per the standing lesson that a mutation which never
landed is indistinguishable from a survivor: dropping the seen check (1),
making `decideCatalogTourAutoStart` ignore `bodyLocked` (1), demoting the CTA's
planner branch (2 — its own case plus the precedence one), and making
`pickVisibleAnchor` accept a zero-size rect (1). The file was restored
byte-identical after each, checked with `diff` rather than assumed — an earlier
attempt at this let three mutations stack, which made the failure counts
cumulative and meaningless.

**One defect caught in review rather than by a test, worth recording:**
`useCatalogTourAutoStart` first used the latest-ref pattern, which is a
`react-hooks/refs` ERROR in this config (a ref assigned during render). Every
input is a dependency now instead, which is cheap — `attempted` short-circuits
the effect after the first go and `consumeReplay` is a no-op with nothing
parked — and it removes a ref that had to be kept in step with props for no
gain.

### NOT verified, and it is the whole risk

**Nothing has rendered in a browser.** This sandbox cannot mint an
authenticated session and has no route to app.urganize.app, so the spotlight,
the card placement against real anchors, the capture-scroll reposition and both
replay paths all rest on unit tests plus the build. Do not try to prove the
flag from the bundle — both ternary branches compile in, a false positive this
file records six times.

**Manual pass at the flip, which is the real verification:** a fresh account
lands on UrgAns, taps through to the catalog and gets Tour A; its last step
opens the intake or the create modal; the first-release prompt does NOT appear
during it and does appear ~30s after it ends; approve a plan and the offer card
shows instead of `NewReleaseGuide`; replay both from the `?` menu on a desktop
and from Settings → Account on a phone.

### Activation

Merged flag-off, so nothing changes for anyone at merge. Flip
`NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_TOURS=true` on the Vercel `Web` project with a commit that
rebuilds `apps/web` (the `turbo-ignore` trap — a version bump suffices, since
`apps/web/package.json` is part of that package). **The ledger entry and the
version bump land AT THE FLIP, not at merge** (the EPK precedent), and the
right entry is about what a person sees: a short guide showing them around the
first time.

## The audience narrowed to artists and managers (2026-09-11)

> **REVERSED 2026-09-24: labels are back in the audience.** The founder's long
> description ends "For artists, managers and labels.", so `AUDIENCE` has three
> entries again and the guard's "for labels" and triple patterns are gone ("small
> labels" stays retired). Two things this section did were NOT undone, because
> the brief did not ask: `/for-labels` still redirects to `/pricing`, and the two
> label search keywords were not restored. See "Everything after the music" at
> the end of this file.

Founder call, later on the same day the category widened: the product is for
**artists and managers**, and nothing on the marketing site may say "for
labels" — header, footer, everywhere. Every line that read "AI Music Business
Manager for artists, managers and labels" reads "AI Music Business Manager for
artists and managers" now: the h1, the footer tagline, the share card, every
meta description and JSON-LD schema, the app's own description and manifest,
the UrgAns prompt. The category, the promise and `URGANS_LINE` are untouched,
and artists still lead.

**No migration, no flag, no API change, and no changelog entry or version
bump.** The same class as the category widening earlier that day:
`apps/homepage` is outside the app-only scope rule, and the `apps/web` half is
the shared positioning constants, the UrgAns prompt, a tier subtitle, two
sentences on the team wall and a `package.json` description — none of it a
feature a user can see. Production stays at v1.41.0.

**THE MODULE DID THE WORK AGAIN.** `AUDIENCE` went from three entries to two,
its join already produces "artists and managers" for two items, and so
`CUSTOMER_LINE`, `ONE_LINER`, `SHORT_DESCRIPTION`, the homepage h1
(`HeroSection` renders `{PRODUCT_CATEGORY} for {AUDIENCE_LINE}.`), the footer
tagline, `LANDING_DESCRIPTION` (159 → 151 characters, back inside the band
`seo.ts` asks for), the four JSON-LD schemas, every page description composed
from the constants, the share card's alt text, the web app's `appDescription`
and the PWA manifest all moved with no edit of their own. Only
`CANONICAL_DESCRIPTION` needed a hand rewrite, being prose.

### Three things confirmed with the founder before any code

1. **`/for-labels` is gone**, with its "For labels" Product-menu link, its
   sitemap entry and the two "See Urganize for labels" cross-links on
   `/for-managers` and `/for-executives`. Its URL **redirects to `/pricing`
   with a 307, never a 308**: the page sat in the sitemap at 0.8 for weeks so
   inbound links exist, `/pricing` is where the Label plan it sold still lives,
   and a permanent redirect is cached by the reader's browser forever, which is
   wrong for a copy decision the founder could reverse (the EPK handover's own
   reasoning).
2. **The Label TIER keeps its name and its id.** Only its card subtitle moved
   — "For a label or a team running a roster." became "For a team running a
   roster." — in `packages/pricing`, so `/pricing`, the homepage strip and the
   in-app picker changed together. `BILLING_PLANS.label`, the frozen legacy
   table whose "For labels and managers…" description renders only on the
   flag-off rollback picker, is untouched, and so is the FAQ's "Label has no
   limit".
3. **The category stays "AI Music Business Manager"**; only the audience
   changed. The founder's Title Case ("Artists and Managers") was taken as
   dictation rather than as a style change: house copy is sentence case, and
   the h1 and the footer already rendered the audience lowercase.

### Seven things worth knowing before editing any of this

1. **Three RETIRED patterns hold it in place** in
   `lib/positioning-guard.test.ts`: `/artists, managers and labels/i`,
   `/\bfor labels\b/i` and `/small labels/i`. That guard reads `README.md` and
   `docs/store-listing.md` as RAW prose, and it bit within the hour: the store
   listing's own header said "(founder call: it is not for labels)" and failed
   the build. Reworded to "labels are no longer an audience". A sentence ABOUT
   a retirement has to avoid the retired phrase — the constraint
   `URGANS_COPY_RULES` already lives under.
2. **Two SEO keywords left with the audience, and that is the A&R rule, not
   the category rule.** `"label management software"` and `"record label
   software"` are out of `LANDING_KEYWORDS`, and `label` is out of the Apple
   keywords in the store listing. A CATEGORY rename keeps its keywords because
   the searcher still types the old word (the reason "AI music manager"
   survived the widening that same morning); a keyword that recruits an
   AUDIENCE the brief no longer names sends the wrong person to a page that
   tells them so — which is exactly why `"A&R software"` went when that
   audience did. Both comments say so beside their lists.
3. **The share card was regenerated and LOOKED AT.** `MAIN_LINE` in
   `generate-og-image.mjs` is eight characters shorter, the break still falls
   exactly at the end of the accented category (spring-green category on one
   line, cream "for artists and managers." on the next), and the script wrote
   identical bytes to both apps' `public/opengraph-image.png` (md5 checked).
   `SHARE_IMAGE_VERSION` is `2026-09-11-artists-and-managers`; the alt
   composes from the constants and followed on its own.
4. **`/pricing`'s hero is composed from the constants now**, the `/brand`
   Positioning-paragraph pattern: `Urganize is an {CUSTOMER_LINE}.` and
   `Built for {AUDIENCE_LINE}.` It was the one marketing page that spelled the
   whole customer line out by hand, so it had to be found by grep on the
   widening AND on this narrowing; it follows the module next time.
5. **The other hand-written copies are the sweep, and the list is the reusable
   part:** `/terms` and `/privacy` "Who we are" (`LAST_UPDATED` NOT bumped —
   renaming who we say we are for changes nobody's rights, the same call as the
   widening), `/signup`'s target-user paragraph, `/community`'s description,
   `/brand`'s "Who it's for" and its press boilerplate, the two `TeamWall`
   sentences in the app ("Running a bigger roster, or prefer an invoice?"),
   `README.md`, `PROJECT_SUMMARY.md`, `REFACTOR_NOTES.md`, the four
   `package.json` descriptions, and the UrgAns `ROLE`, whose test asserts
   `toContain(CUSTOMER_LINE)` and failed correctly until it moved.
6. **Left alone, deliberately:** the tier name and id; `WaitlistForm.tsx`'s
   "Label manager" option (a respondent's self-description feeding a stored
   enum, not positioning copy); `/for-ai-artists`' "Nothing assumes a label, a

## The plan is built, not drafted (2026-09-15)

Founder call, verbatim: *"Remove the plan review they should just automatically
create the plan they can edit it manally themselves if they want after it has
already been created. And the plan has to aligned with what they type or
select during the asking question stage before the plan is created. if someone
says they want a normal release no marketing then it should tailor to that,
Then to help this let's use a open ai model that can do this very well."*

Four forks were put to the founder and answered before any code changed:
finishing the interview in chat **builds the plan straight away**, no card, no
draft; a model failure **holds and asks to try again** when the manager typed
real notes (nothing is created, the answers are kept), and quietly proceeds
from the selected answers alone when they typed nothing; the planner model is
**`openai/gpt-5.4`** via RodiumAi; and "no marketing" means **the whole
campaign**, not just the optional edges of it — release day and getting the
music to stores stay in every plan regardless.

**Why the old build could not honour "no marketing" at all, measured before
writing a line of this:** the single-release playbook has 64 tasks, 37 tagged
`marketing`, and 27 of those are `optional: false`. The AI contract only let
the model drop OPTIONAL tasks and rejected the whole delta if it touched a
required one, so the most any instruction could ever remove was 10 optional
marketing tasks out of 37. The guidance was also keyed wrong — every intake,
even a well-funded one, was told "No budget: drop the optional paid promotion
tasks" — and a manager's free-text answer reached the model as "anything else
they said" with no rule that it actually bound the output. A "normal release,
no marketing" request was structurally unable to produce one.

### The exclusion model replaces "the AI decides what to drop"

`PLAN_SCOPES` (`lib/release-planning.ts`) is five buckets a manager's words map
onto — `marketing`, `press`, `paid_ads`, `events`, `physical` — each carrying a
playbook tag (`SCOPE_TAGS`) and a plain label. `KEEP_TAGS = ['release_day',
'distribution']`: a task carrying either tag survives every scope, whatever
else it is tagged, because release day and the distributor handoff ARE the
release — a rollout with no marketing still goes out and still reaches stores.
`isTaskInScope(task, scope)` is the one test: the scope's tag present, no keep
tag present.

**Removal is CODE, not a model suggestion.** The intake's `exclusions` field
(a manager's explicit "leave this out" chips) and `budget === 'none'` (which
silently adds `paid_ads`) are applied by `applyScopeExclusions` before the
model ever sees the draft. The model can still propose `exclude_scopes` from
free text — "keep it low-key, no press push" becomes a press exclusion with a
reason — but a required task can only be dropped when it falls inside a scope
the manager or the model actually named; `validatePlannerDelta` rejects the
whole delta otherwise, and a keep-tagged task can never be dropped by any
scope, ever (`lib/release-planning.test.ts` pins both, mutation-tested — see
Verified below).

### One pipeline, no draft: `createReleasePlan`

`lib/release-planning-actions-server.ts` replaces the old
`generatePlanDraft` + `approvePlanDraft` pair with one function, called from
three doors that now all do the same thing: `POST /api/releases/[id]/plan`
(the workspace card), `generate_release_plan` (the chat tool), and
`release.draft_plan` (the embedded action). In order: resolve the release
date (writing it if the intake supplied one and the row lacked it); refuse a
second plan on a release that already has one; build the deterministic
template draft and propose owners from past assignments; apply the
deterministic exclusions (intake + budget-none); ask the model for a delta
over the REMAINING tasks only; **insert-or-claim** on `release_plan_drafts`
(the row is now purely an idempotency lock and an audit trail — nothing reads
it as a document to review) so two racing requests can't both build; and
instantiate straight into `tasks` in the same call. `generate/`, `approve/`
and `regenerate-phase/` route files are deleted outright.

**The AI-failure policy is the "hold and ask to try again" fork, made
precise** (`decidePlanCreationOnAiFailure`, pure and tested): with the
gateway simply not configured, proceed untailored — the deterministic result
is still a valid plan. With a real failure (timeout, rate limit, bad output)
and the manager had typed real notes (`extra_notes` or `goal_text`), refuse
with 503 `tailoring_unavailable` **before writing anything** — the notes are
the one thing code cannot fall back to interpreting, so a manager who wrote
"keep it minimal, we're skipping the video shoot" gets told to try again
rather than getting a plan that silently ignored what they wrote. With no
typed notes, proceed with the deterministic + selected-answer result and a
warning that the rest could not be tailored.

### The provider, and why an OpenAI model needed new plumbing

`lib/ai/provider.ts` gained `jsonSchema` (strict `json_schema` response
format, with a one-time fallback to `json_object` if a gateway 400s on the
newer shape), `reasoningEffort` (sent only to models `supportsReasoningEffort`
recognizes as accepting it — `openai/gpt-5.4` does, `openai/gpt-4o-mini` does
not — with its own one-time fallback if a gateway rejects the parameter), and
a `deadlineMs` that shortens each retry's timeout as the budget runs down and
skips a retry with under 8s left rather than starting one it cannot finish.
`lib/ai/planner-model.ts` resolves `openai/gpt-5.4` as the RodiumAi default
(env override `AI_PLANNER_MODEL` unchanged) and `'low'` as the default
reasoning effort (`AI_PLANNER_REASONING_EFFORT`). Every prompt string still
carries no model or provider name, per the existing test that forbids it.

### The scene is gone; the manager edits real activities instead

Deleted: `PlanScene.tsx`, `usePlanDraft.ts`, `PlanApproveBar.tsx`,
`PlanPhaseSection.tsx`, `PlanTaskRow.tsx`, the plan-scene skeleton, and every
`openScene('plan', …)` call. `'plan'` is out of `SceneName` entirely, so the
compiler — not a runtime check — is what caught every call site that still
assumed a review scene existed. `PlanReleaseCard` now has three states
(`fresh` → the intake, `generating` → a short wait, `failed` → try again,
answers kept) and the primary button in every one of them is the questions,
because there is nothing else to open. A new `PlanBuiltBanner` is the ONLY
place a manager learns what the model removed and why — it renders once,
dismissible, listing every dropped task's reason and every applied exclusion,
because "trust me" without a list of what changed would violate the file's
own "visible state changes" principle.

### Chat: finishing the interview is the go-ahead

The system prompt's interview grew from seven questions to eight — the new
one asks what to leave out, answered only when the manager plainly says so
and never suggested by the model — and reading the eight answers back for a
yes is now the ENTIRE approval step; there is nothing after it.
`approve_release_plan` and `discard_release_plan` are deleted from the tool
registry, `ChappiToolName`, and every gated-tool list in this file (the
"Currently sixteen" bullet under "The confirmation gate" is fourteen now).
`generate_release_plan` is ungated (per the founder's call) and, when called
with no `releaseId`, creates the rollout and builds its plan in one request —
the usual shape, since most of the time the release does not exist yet when
the interview starts.

### The embedded action needed a new primitive: `oneShot`

`release.draft_plan` used to run `execute()` (draft) then a separate `apply()`
(commit); now `execute()` does the whole job and there is nothing left to
apply or discard. Rather than special-case this one action,
`UrgansActionDefinition` gained `oneShot?: boolean` and `apply`/`discard`
became OPTIONAL methods (`lib/urgans-actions/types.ts`); `runUrgansAction`
checks `action.oneShot` and, on success, inserts the `urgans_actions` row
**already** `status: 'applied'` with `applied_result` set from the same
output, rather than `'drafted'` waiting for a later settle call.
`findLatestDraftedActionId`, `markChatActionApplied` and
`markChatActionDiscarded` are deleted — nothing calls them once the planner
stopped needing a settle step, and a settle function with no drafted row to
settle is a function nothing can safely reach for. `presskit.draft_section`,
the OTHER embedded action, is untouched and still uses the two-step shape —
`oneShot` is an option this framework offers, not a direction it forces every
action toward.

**Rebased 2026-09-25, after ten days of unrelated drift, and the founder
re-confirmed the direction before it landed** — this branch sat unmerged while
`main` built further ON TOP of the review step it removes: share to socials'
`shareAction`, the embedded-actions admin console, and a `share_release` tool
name landing right beside the two this section deletes
(`approve_release_plan`, `discard_release_plan`) in the same enum. None of
that changes what already shipped here; the rebase kept `shareAction` and
`share_release`, dropped `showPlanPill`/`hasPlanDraft` (the review-step pill
this section retires), and re-derived the version number rather than trusting
the branch's own stale v1.42.0 claim, which had since been taken twice over by
other work. See "Everything after the music" and the rest of this file's
2026-09-15-to-25 entries for what else moved underneath it.

### Verified

**Re-run after the rebase, numbers below are from before it and are the
build-time record — re-verified counts follow in the same order:** full
vitest suite **3689 passed, 30 skipped**, zero failures; `eslint .` **3 errors
/ 78 warnings** in `apps/web` (the same three pre-existing `WorkspaceView.tsx`
errors, and one warning FEWER than a clean `main` checkout's own 79, measured
by linting both); `tsc --noEmit` clean apart from the same 8 documented
`confirmed-action.test.ts` errors; `next build` green by exit code with
`NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_RELEASE_PLANNER` both on and off, `/auth`, `/onboarding`,
`/settings` and `/dashboard` all still `○ Static` in each; and the same
404-vs-401 runtime discrimination on `/api/releases/[id]/plan` confirmed again
post-rebase.

`vitest run` in `apps/web`: **3256 passed, 30 skipped**, zero failures.
`eslint .`: **3 errors / 77 warnings** in `apps/web` (all three errors the
documented pre-existing `WorkspaceView.tsx` ref-during-render finding, zero
new warnings) and **0 errors / 2 warnings** in `apps/homepage` (the documented
pre-existing `RoadmapPageClient.tsx` finding) — both baselines matched
exactly. `tsc --noEmit` clean in `apps/homepage`; clean in `apps/web` apart
from the 8 documented pre-existing `confirmed-action.test.ts` errors. `next
build` green **by exit code** for both apps, and `apps/web` built clean with
`NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_RELEASE_PLANNER` both on and off, `/auth`, `/onboarding`,
`/settings` and `/dashboard` all still `○ Static` in every combination.

**Runtime probes on `next start`, rebuilt between flag states:** flag off,
`POST` and `GET /api/releases/<id>/plan` both answer **404** with body exactly
`{"error":"Not found."}` while the ungated `/api/releases` still **401**s —
the discrimination that proves the gate is real rather than a routing

**Compiled output checked directly, this repo's habit for anything the build

The store listing's stated character count was remeasured with `wc -m` after

**Two mutations run, each printing `APPLIED` first, each restored

### Not verified, and it is the whole product risk

**No live model call.** RodiumAi is egress-blocked from this sandbox and no

## UrgAns replies show markdown as formatting, not literal punctuation (2026-09-24, v1.42.1)

Founder report, with a screenshot: a phase-breakdown reply rendered on screen
as `- **Setup:** 26 tasks`, asterisks and all. `ChappiConversation.tsx` draws
assistant text raw inside a `whitespace-pre-wrap` div, and `apps/web` has
never had any markdown handling — the system prompt's own no-markdown rule
(`lib/chappi/system-prompt.ts`, since v1.32.0) tells the model not to do
this, and the model (`openai/gpt-4o-mini`) does not reliably follow it. A
prompt-only fix had already been tried and had not held.

**Founder decisions:** text in `**double asterisks**` shows as **bold**;
every other markdown symbol is removed rather than rendered. Scope is the
**chat only** — replies, the copy button, and the deterministic status-update
branch that already renders through the same component. Text UrgAns saves
elsewhere (notes, activities, the plan, press kit sections, emails) is
explicitly OUT of scope and stays unsanitized.

**`lib/model-markup.ts` (new, pure, no React/Node imports)** is a hand-rolled,
deliberately conservative markdown-to-segments parser — no dependency added
(boring-stack rule). `parseModelMarkup(text)` returns a flat
`{text, bold}[]`; `stripModelMarkup(text)` is defined as the joined plain text
of those segments, so the two cannot drift apart. A no-markup input returns
untouched as one segment (not merely equal), which is what makes "no markup
in, no markup out" a structural guarantee: every deterministic reply UrgAns
already writes renders byte-identically to before.

**Six things worth knowing before touching this again:**

1. **`_` uses a STRICTER flanking rule than `*`, and this is a real bug this
   pass found and fixed, not a stylistic choice.** Full CommonMark treats
   punctuation (a quote, a period) as a valid emphasis boundary, which is
   exactly what makes a CommonMark-faithful parser read `"__init__.wav"` as
   emphasis around "init" — quote before the opener, period after the closer
   both count. That silently eats the underscores off a dunder filename,
   which this assistant is far more likely to write than to actually mean
   "underline" (the house convention for emphasis is `**word**`). So `_`
   only counts as a delimiter against actual whitespace or a true line
   boundary, never against punctuation alone; `*`/`~~` keep the wider rule,
   since they collide with no common identifier convention.
2. **A censored word (`f**k`, `B**** …`) and a truncated bold marker
   (`**Setup: 26 tasks`, cut off mid-reply) look identical as PLAIN TEXT
   after the fact, so the two cannot be told apart by a regex over the final
   string.** The distinction is made DURING pairing, from whether the run was
   ever a genuine delimiter candidate (`canOpen`): a wholly-unmatched 2-3
   length `*` run that WAS a candidate is dropped (the model got cut off
   mid-bold); one that never was (flanked by letters on the wrong side) is
   left exactly as typed.
3. **Bold does not span a line break** (`**Setup\n26**` stays literal) — a
   deliberate, pinned limitation. Inline markup is resolved one line at a
   time, so one unclosed `**` can never swallow a whole multi-line reply.
4. **The pairing algorithm supports a single closer run satisfying two
   different openers** (`**Do this *today***` → one bold span, no stray
   marker), the one piece of real complexity here: an opener only partially
   consumed stays on the stack rather than being popped, so a later closer
   can still use what's left of it.
5. **History sent back to the model is cleaned, not just the render.**
   `lib/chappi/runner.ts`'s new `toModelHistory()` strips markup off
   ASSISTANT turns only (never the user's own words) before they go back as
   conversation history — without this, UrgAns's own past `**` replies stay
   in front of it as an example it keeps imitating, since the raw text
   rendered on screen is also what gets resent every later turn.
6. **The reveal (word-by-word fade-in) wraps per SEGMENT, not per word.**
   `lib/chappi/reveal-tokens.ts`'s `buildRevealGroups` keeps one word counter
   running across bold and plain segments alike (so timing doesn't care where
   the bold boundary falls), and `components/chappi/ReplyText.tsx` wraps each
   segment's words together in one bold span. Wrapping bold per WORD instead
   would change the whitespace between words from un-bold to bold width the
   instant the reveal finishes, which can re-wrap a line.

`ReplyText.tsx` is its own component (not inlined into `ChappiConversation`)
so a throwaway harness page could render it standalone for a browser check
with no auth required — confirmed there, then deleted before this landed.
The system prompt (`lib/chappi/system-prompt.ts:45`) keeps its plain-text
rule but no longer quotes `**asterisks**` as the example of what it forbids
(the same em-dash-in-a-rule-about-em-dashes trap this file already records
elsewhere), and states a reason that stays true now that the renderer
handles bold: markdown handed to a TOOL (a note, an activity, a press kit
section) is still saved and shown exactly as written.

**Verified:** the full vitest suite (3294 passing; the one failing file,
`vercel-ignore-build.test.ts`, is a pre-existing, unrelated PowerShell/WSL
bash-availability quirk in this sandbox, not something this change touched —
confirmed via `git status` showing the file untouched), `eslint .` at the
exact 3-error/78-warning baseline (all three pre-existing in
`WorkspaceView.tsx`) with zero new findings in any touched file, `tsc
--noEmit` clean apart from the 8 documented pre-existing
`confirmed-action.test.ts` errors, and `next build` green **by exit code**
with `/auth`, `/onboarding`, `/settings` and `/dashboard` all still
`○ Static`. **Three mutation passes, each failing exactly its own tests**:
letting `*` open after a letter (2 tests), dropping the `canOpen` guard so
any unmatched `**` gets deleted regardless of context (3 tests), and
skipping the strip in `toModelHistory` (both of its tests). **Rendered and
inspected in a real browser** (the built-in preview pane): the screenshot
reply's phase labels compute to `font-weight: 600` with zero stray
asterisks; a censored word and a dunder filename both survive with their
punctuation intact; an unclosed `**` at a simulated cutoff drops cleanly; the
word-by-word reveal's delays increment continuously across bold and plain
segments with no visual jump.

**Not verified:** no live model call — this sandbox has no route to either
urganize domain, so whether `openai/gpt-4o-mini` still occasionally reaches
for other markdown this parser doesn't yet have a rule for (nested lists, a
markdown table with more exotic alignment syntax) rests on the parser's
conservative "when in doubt, leave it as plain text" design rather than on
having observed a live reply. Worth one look after deploy: ask UrgAns a
phase-breakdown question on a real rollout and confirm the labels render bold
with a working copy button.

**Noticed but explicitly out of scope, flagged rather than fixed:** the press
kit "Draft this section" action passes the model's raw string straight to
`parseDraftOutput`, whose signature expects an already-parsed object — every
run of that action ends in a 502. It is dark today behind
`NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_URGANS_ACTIONS`, unrelated to this fix's scope, and is
being flagged as a separate follow-up task rather than folded in here.
