## Share to socials (2026-09-23; switched on 2026-09-24 as v1.42.0)

Founder request: when somebody creates a rollout for the first time, let them
share it as an Instagram post, a WhatsApp status and a message they can DM to
anybody, and "if, at any time, they create a release, always ask questions for
clarity". Four founder answers shaped it before any code was written:

1. **The sheet opens by itself ONCE, after the first rollout.** After that every
   rollout carries a Share button, and UrgAns can open it.
2. **It always asks four questions first:** who is posting (the artist, "my new
   single", or the team, "Dorian’s new single"), whether the date can be public,
   a link for fans, and one extra line.
3. **The DM link is the link they give us** (a pre-save or smart link). No link
   means just the message.
4. **The images carry a small, quiet "Made with Urganize" mark.**

Behind `NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_SOCIAL_SHARE`, default `false`, and **ON in
production since 2026-09-24** (see Activation below). **No migration, no new
table, nothing stored server-side.** Scope reasoning is in the 2026-09-23
paragraph under "v1 scope".

### What it makes

Three things, from the rollout's own facts plus the four answers:

- **An Instagram post image** (1080x1350) and its caption. The caption never
  carries the raw link, because Instagram does not make one tappable; it says
  "Pre-save link in bio." (or "Listen at the link in bio." once it is out).
- **A WhatsApp status image** (1080x1920) and a shorter caption that DOES carry
  the raw link, because a status makes it tappable.
- **A message to DM anybody**: "Hey! …" plus "Pre-save it here: <link>" (or
  "Listen here:"), sent through WhatsApp, copied, or handed to Instagram's inbox.

The copy rules live in `lib/social-share.ts` and are enforced by its tests
rather than by review, because this is the one surface in the product whose
words the user PUBLISHES as their own:

- **Fans read it, so it says single, EP or album, never "rollout", never
  "workspace", and never "Urganize" in a caption.** The mark is on the image
  only. In-app copy around it says rollout as everywhere else.
- **A secret date never leaks.** "Not yet" turns every date into "Coming soon",
  on the image and in all three texts; a date that has passed is simply "Out
  now", whatever the answer.
- **No em dashes, typographic quotes and apostrophes throughout.**
- **An untitled rollout drops its placeholder title** ("Untitled rollout" never
  reaches a post), and the artist carries the headline instead.

### Seven things worth knowing before editing this

1. **"First" is decided on the SERVER, in `POST /api/releases`, and returned as
   `firstRelease`.** The client's copy of the catalog may not have loaded, so it
   cannot know. Test rollouts never count either way, which is why
   `decideFirstRelease` reads the metadata of up to 10 earlier rollouts when
   there are some; a failed read answers "not the first", because silence
   costs nothing and the Share button is still there. Always `false` with the
   flag off, so nothing downstream needs a flag check of its own.
2. **One helper puts the sheet into every create flow:
   `components/share/withFirstShareOffer.ts`.** The three create flows (the
   workspace, the UrgAns page and the topbar's modal) each end in their own
   continuation, and the sheet slots in AFTER the compulsory team-login step and
   BEFORE the rest (the planner intake, the new-rollout guide, a navigation),
   which runs when the sheet closes. Flag off, or not a first rollout, it is the
   continuation untouched. One helper because those three flows have drifted
   apart before.
3. **The once-only offer is spent only when a sheet actually showed it.** The
   sheet is a lazy chunk in AppShell, so a very quick first create on a slow
   connection can finish before it mounts. `useShareStore.open` answers whether
   a sheet took the request; when none did, the flow carries straight on and a
   pending marker is left instead. Mutation-tested.
4. **Onboarding creates most first rollouts, and uses the same pending marker**
   (`markPendingFirstShare`, sessionStorage, 30 minutes). The sheet's host picks
   it up once the person lands in the app, but only at a quiet moment: never
   over another modal (the body scroll lock), never over a guided tour, and it
   gives up after about a minute, because an offer arriving long after the
   moment is an interruption. "Offered" is remembered per account in
   localStorage and fails toward "already offered".
5. **The images are rendered on request by
   `GET /api/releases/[releaseId]/share-card`**, with `next/og` and the recap
   card's fonts (so `next.config.js` carries an `outputFileTracingIncludes`
   entry for it; an ENOENT on a .ttf in production means that entry, not the
   code). Team read access through the shared helper, enlisted in
   `release-access-guard.test.ts`; auth runs before any validation, so a
   signed-out request learns nothing. The response is private and `no-store`,
   overriding `next/og`'s public cache default, because the image can carry an
   unannounced title. Cover art is used only when it is a PNG or JPEG under 12
   MiB and never the workspace logo; a render that fails with the art is retried
   once without it, so a strange file costs the art, not the post.
6. **The images are fetched BEFORE the tap, and the tap does nothing async
   first.** Web Share only opens inside a user gesture, so the File is ready
   when the button shows, the caption is copied synchronously, and
   `navigator.share` is the first await. Files are only offered to the share
   sheet on a touch device (`pointer: coarse`) whose browser says it can take
   them; everywhere else the image is saved, which is the honest answer on a
   computer. The native app needs the share plugins; the one APK on record
   predates them, so it says so ("Sharing needs the newest version of the app.
   Open Urganize in your browser to share.") rather than offering a button that
   does nothing.
7. **UrgAns reaches it three ways:** the `share_release` tool (kind read; it
   posts nothing, so it is not confirmation-gated, and it is NOT in the MCP
   allow-list, since its whole effect is a client action), a typed "share to
   socials" command for when no model is running, and `create_release`, which
   marks its navigation with `offerFirstShareFor` when that was a first rollout
   so the same once-only sheet comes first. The typed phrases are narrow on
   purpose: a bare "status" means the status update and "share the recap" means
   the recap card, and a test pins both.

### The sheet itself, and what looking at it found

`components/share/ShareSheet.tsx`, mounted once in AppShell and opened through
`stores/useShareStore.ts`, following the house sheet contract (z-[170], portal
to `document.body`, swipe to dismiss, Escape and a Tab trap on the dialog
itself). Two steps: ASK, then SHARE, and the answers are remembered per rollout
so a second visit is one tap.

It was checked in a browser through a throwaway preview page (a faked user and
rollout, pre-rendered posters in place of the route, deleted afterwards), at
375 and 1280, in both themes. That pass found eight real problems, all fixed,
and several are worth knowing as house lessons:

- **`bg-bg-elevated` is the SAME colour as `bg-bg-surface` in light mode and two
  shades off it in dark**, so the option tracks vanished on cream and the
  selected option read only by its text. The fix is the Shows modal's pattern:
  a `bg-bg-base` well with a `bg-bg-surface` thumb, the one pairing that reads
  as raised in both themes (`TRACK_CLASS`).
- **The shared `.input` class fills with white at 4%, invisible on cream, and
  its radius outranks `rounded-xl`**, so the fields came out square. The sheet
  uses its own `FIELD_CLASS` instead. Other inputs in the app are untouched and
  still border-only in light mode, which is worth knowing if one ever looks
  missing.
- **The app-wide `:focus-visible` ring outranks a bare `outline-none`**, so the
  panel, which takes focus only to carry the keyboard into the dialog, arrived
  wearing a green rim whenever it opened with no click before it, which is
  exactly how the first-rollout sheet opens. `focus-visible:outline-none` fixes
  it.
- **Changing step unmounted the focused button**, dropping focus to `<body>`,
  where Escape and the Tab trap (both on the panel) stop hearing anything; the
  new step also kept the old one's scroll position. A layout effect now resets
  the scroll and hands focus to the selected tab or the panel.
- **On a phone the share step holds one height**, so moving between the tabs no
  longer makes the sheet drop by a third of the screen, and **the main button is
  pinned to the bottom of the question step**, which was below the fold on a
  1280x800 laptop.
- **A failed image turns the main button into "Try again"**; it used to sit
  disabled still saying "Making your post…" under an error that said otherwise.

### Where it lives

`lib/social-share.ts` (the rules and the copy), `lib/social-share-card.tsx` (the
posters), `lib/social-share-server.ts` (cover art), `lib/social-share-offer.ts`
(first-rollout, the once-only offer, the pending marker, saved answers),
`stores/useShareStore.ts`, `components/share/` (the sheet, its image fetcher and
`withFirstShareOffer`), the image route, and the Share button in the rollout's
header on desktop and in the release menu on a phone (ranked after Files, as the
first of the "send this outward" items). Analytics: `social_share_opened`,
`social_share_made` and `social_share_sent`, none of which carry any text.

The copy guards read it: `lib/press-kit-copy-guard.test.ts` (the em dash and the
banned words) and `lib/rollout-vocabulary.test.ts` (the sheet's in-app copy
says rollout).

### Verified

3309 tests passing / 30 skipped, 109 of them new, against a baseline of 3200.
`eslint .` at the exact 3-error / 78-warning baseline, confirmed per file against
the committed versions rather than by the totals alone. `tsc --noEmit` clean
apart from the documented `confirmed-action.test.ts` errors. `next build` green
by exit code in both flag states, with `/auth`, `/onboarding`, `/settings`,
`/dashboard`, `/dashboard/urgans` and `/locked` all still `○ Static`, and the
sheet's arbitrary classes confirmed in the compiled CSS (where the minifier folds
`calc(40dvh*0.8)` to `32dvh`, which reads as missing to a naive grep). Runtime
probes on `next start`: flag off, the image route answers 404 with body exactly
`{"error":"Not found."}` while the ungated control answers 401; flag on, 401.
**Nine mutations, each killing its own test**, and the one that survived at
first was a real test weakness, not a failed application: the recap test used a
phrase the share branch would never have claimed anyway.

### Not verified

No real share has happened. Nothing here has handed a file to Instagram or
WhatsApp on a real phone, rendered a poster through the route with a real
session, or run the onboarding hand-off end to end; this sandbox cannot mint a
session and has no route to either urganize domain. The posters were rendered
and looked at through the same renderer the route uses, which is not the same
as the route serving one.

### Activation

1. ~~Set `NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_SOCIAL_SHARE=true`~~: done 2026-09-24 with the
   Vercel CLI, on the `urganize` project's **Production** environment only,
   non-sensitive, matching the other feature flags there. Preview deployments
   still build with it off. The order was the variable first and the rebuild
   second, the order the textile flip recorded as the one that works.
2. ~~Changelog entry and version bump~~: done as **v1.42.0**, whose commit is
   the rebuild that inlines the variable. The quick proof it took needs no
   session: `GET /api/releases/<any uuid>/share-card` answers 401 with the flag
   on and 404 with it off.
3. **OPEN:** the manual pass that matters, on a real phone: create a first rollout and
   confirm the sheet opens after the team-login step; answer the questions; tap
   "Share to Instagram" and confirm Instagram opens with the image and the
   caption pastes; tap "Post to status" and confirm WhatsApp offers My status;
   send the message on WhatsApp; then open the Share button on a second rollout
   and confirm the answers came back.

### X and Snapchat, and per-artist brand colors (2026-09-24, v1.43.0)

Founder ask, on top of the shipped sheet: add X and Snapchat, and let each
artist set their own colors for the images. Two additions, treated
differently, because one rides the flag above and the other is genuinely new:

- **X and Snapchat are two more tabs in the SAME sheet, and they ship live at
  merge with no flag of their own.** `NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_SOCIAL_SHARE` was
  already `true` in production, and these tabs are inside the component that
  flag already gates — the same "an addition rides an already-on flag" shape
  as UrgAns's own tool registry growing. There was nothing to flip.
- **X posts the same 4:5 image as Instagram**, with its own post text (a 280
  character counter, X's own weighting: a link always counts 23 regardless of
  length) and an "Open X with this post" link (`x.com/intent/post`, no account
  or approval needed on our side, the WhatsApp button's precedent). Instagram's
  caption still says "link in bio"; X's carries the raw link, because X makes
  one tappable.
- **Snapchat posts the same 9:16 image as the status**, with a plain sentence
  and no link in the text — Snapchat takes no text or link from another app,
  so the link is copied separately for its own link sticker (the paperclip),
  and the sheet says so.
- **Brand colors are genuinely new and stay behind their own flag**,
  `NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_BRAND_COLORS`, default `false`. Two optional colors per
  ARTIST (a background and an accent), set in Settings under their name, used
  only on these images. **The text color is never chosen** — `resolveSharePalette`
  in `lib/social-share-colors.ts` picks cream or ink, whichever reads better
  (WCAG contrast), so no pair of colors a manager picks can make the words
  unreadable. **An accent too close to its background is taken OFF the words**
  (the eyebrow, the artist line, the date) and kept only on the rule and the
  small square beside the extra line, where it cannot hide anything — so a bad
  pair makes an image plain, never broken. One palette function, three
  consumers (the poster renderer, the image route, the Settings preview), so
  what a manager sees in Settings is what gets posted.
- **Migration:** `20260924120000_artists_brand_colors.sql` — two nullable,
  CHECK-constrained columns on `artists` (`brand_background`, `brand_accent`,
  `'#RRGGBB'` uppercase). **Applied to production 2026-09-24.** Additive and
  safe either order: every read falls back to Urganize's own colors on any
  failure, including before the migration ran.
- **`PUT /api/workspace/artists/[artistId]/brand-colors`** saves both slots at
  once (null in a slot means "use Urganize's"); `GET /api/workspace/artists`
  carries a `brandColors` field per artist only while the flag is on. Both
  gated the same way the artist rename route already is: found on the caller's
  OWN roster, so an artist on another team is indistinguishable from one that
  does not exist.
- **The sheet links straight to the editor** once it knows a poster's colors
  (`BRAND_COLORS_SETTINGS_HREF`, `/settings?tab=workspace#brand-colors`),
  saying "These use Dorian's brand colors. Change them." or "Want your own
  colors on these? Set brand colors." — never before the image route has
  answered, since the honest sentence needs to know which is true first.

**Verified:** the full vitest suite (3454 passing), `tsc --noEmit` and
`eslint .` at the same baselines this section already records, `next build`
green with the new flag both off and on. Runtime probes against `next start`
in both states: the new brand-colors route answers 404 with the flag off and
401 (unauthenticated) with it on, the same discrimination the image route
above already relies on. Driven in a throwaway preview (deleted after): all
five tabs render, an artist's saved colors reach the Settings preview and the
actual rendered poster identically, X's counter and post-link button work,
Snapchat's link-copy flow works, and "Change them" correctly routes into
Settings.

**Activation:**
1. X and Snapchat needed no flip — live the moment this merged (v1.43.0), since
   the parent flag was already on. Confirmed against `/api/version` reporting
   that exact commit on production.
2. Migration applied 2026-09-24, by hand in the Supabase dashboard, before the
   flag was touched.
3. `NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_BRAND_COLORS=true` set on the `urganize` project's
   Production environment via the Vercel CLI, non-sensitive, the same pattern
   as every flag above it. **Set AFTER v1.43.0 had already deployed**, so that
   commit's own build did NOT inline it — the trap this file records for every
   flag flip. This entry's own version bump (v1.45.0) is the deliberate
   follow-up rebuild that actually picks the variable up; do not assume a var
   is live just because `vercel env ls` shows it.
4. **OPEN:** the same manual pass as the section above, plus one artist's
   brand colors actually reaching a real posted image on a real phone.

## Saved UrgAns chats (2026-09-24, LIVE as v1.44.0)

Founder ask: *"we need to start saving conversations and storing chat history
both on the front end and the back end."* UrgAns conversations were ephemeral
(the transcript lived only in the in-memory `useChappiStore`, and a reload or a
second device started fresh), and "cross-session persistence" had sat on the
Chappi "Still deferred" list since the assistant shipped. So this **completes an
already-sanctioned surface rather than expanding scope**: nothing moves off the
out-of-scope list, and it hangs off the assistant, whose every tool is about a
release.

Behind `NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_URGANS_HISTORY` (default off, only meaningful with
`NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_CHAPPI`), read through `isChappiHistoryEnabled()` in
`lib/chappi/conversation-history.ts` so the two env names are typed once.
Migration `20260924100000_urgans_conversations.sql`, **not applied anywhere
yet**.

**Four founder decisions, asked before building:**
1. **Resume if recent.** Reopening UrgAns (reload, next sign-in, another
   device) brings back the last chat if it was used in the past six hours;
   otherwise the usual greeting, with older chats one tap away.
2. **A full chats list,** titled from the first thing the user said (the Apple
   Notes model, like Notes itself), with open and delete. On the UrgAns page and
   from the side rail.
3. **Kept until the user deletes them.** In the account data export
   (`urgans_chats`), removed with the account by the `auth.users` cascade.
4. **An answer that arrives after you leave its chat is saved to that chat.**
   Its suggestions, approval card and page jump are skipped, because they
   belong to a screen nobody is looking at.

Default taken without asking, on the Notes precedent: **chats are private to
their owner.** No teammate read path, no share link.

### The design in one paragraph

One row per chat, holding the transcript as a JSON array (the
`release_plan_drafts` "document read and written whole" precedent), written by
a **revision-checked "replace the tail" save**: "you were at revision R; keep
your first K messages; put these after them". **The browser is the only
writer** — history is exactly what the user saw, and `/api/urgans` stays
stateless. One row per MESSAGE was rejected because the side rail mounts the
conversation on every page, so two tabs on one chat is a normal path rather
than an edge case, and insertion-ordered rows silently interleave two tabs'
turns where a revision check notices. The decisions are pure and live in
`lib/chappi/conversation-history.ts`; the rest is thin IO around them:
`lib/chappi/conversations-server.ts` (the table), `app/api/urgans/conversations/**`
(the routes), `lib/chappi/conversation-cache.ts` (the browser copy),
`stores/useChappiHistoryStore.ts` (the sync engine and the list), and
`components/chappi/ChappiHistoryBridge.tsx` (starts it for the signed-in user).

### An unflagged privacy fix that ships with it

**Sign-out never reset the UrgAns store.** It is a module-level store that a
client-side navigation to `/auth` does not tear down, so signing out and then in
as another account in the same tab showed the previous account's whole
transcript. `useChappiStore.resetForSignOut()` is now called from the
`SIGNED_OUT` branch of `lib/auth-store.ts`, and clears the scope picker too. The
store also carries an **epoch**, bumped whenever the transcript is replaced
rather than added to ("New chat", sign-out, opening a saved chat), and every
async reply in `ChappiConversation` captures it when its turn starts. A reply
whose epoch changed is never shown under a different conversation or account:
with history off it is dropped, with it on it is saved to its own chat.
**Behaviour change worth knowing:** "New chat" during a reply used to drop that
reply into the new chat; it no longer does. `isThinking` is derived from the
epoch too, so a switch never leaves the composer locked for up to a minute.

### Ten things worth knowing before editing this

1. **This tab only ever claims to know the server copy from something it SAW.**
   `serverIds` is set from a save that landed, a chat loaded onto the screen, or
   a conflict whose server side is a prefix of ours. When another tab is AHEAD,
   its state is adopted only by LOADING it; if the load fails the entry is left
   stale on purpose, so the next save is refused again and settled against
   what is on screen then. The obvious shortcut — adopt the conflict's ids and
   reload — lets a later save "replace the tail" and silently drop the other
   tab's message. `conversation-sync.test.ts` pins it; the mutation that
   reintroduces the shortcut fails exactly that test.
2. **Conflicts settle four ways** (`resolveConflict`): adopt (both agree),
   resend (the server holds a prefix of ours), reload (we hold a prefix of
   theirs), fork (they differ, so this tab's transcript becomes a new chat and
   neither side's words are lost). A reload that finds the user typed something
   meanwhile forks too.
3. **Forks can never loop.** A fork always saves from revision 0, and a 404 on
   a revision-0 save — or the flag-gate body `'Not found.'`, distinct from
   `'Chat not found.'` — marks the chat blocked instead of forking again. Without
   that, a server with the feature switched off turns one chat into an endless
   stream of new ones; the mutation removing the guard hangs its test until the
   timeout, which is the loop.
4. **Late answers follow their chat.** `appendToChat` appends to the live
   transcript if that chat is back on screen, else to its detached copy (every
   chat switched away from is kept in memory for the session), and saves. A
   forked chat's old id maps to its new one (`renamed`), so an answer still
   addressed to the old id lands in the right place; a chat deleted here is
   tombstoned, and an answer for it is dropped. Upload and recap cards that
   finish after their chat left report into it the same way.
5. **Retry is only offered on a reply added THIS session.** `restoredCount` on
   the transcript store marks how many messages were loaded rather than added;
   regenerating yesterday's reply would re-run its tools and bill an action. The
   same count is why the first-release prompt, the catalog tour and the usage
   strip now read `selectLiveTurnCount` instead of `messages.length` — a
   restored chat is not a conversation in progress. Both are identical to the
   old behaviour with history off, where `restoredCount` is always 0.
6. **The browser copy is whole or nothing** (`urganize.cache.urgans-chats`, the
   account's user id inside the payload). A transcript that does not fit the
   storage budget is dropped WHOLE, keeping its sync state: a partial prefix
   would make the next save truncate the server copy to match. Sign-out wipes
   it, and `resetChappiHistory()` runs BEFORE `resetForSignOut()` in
   `lib/auth-store.ts` — the other order reads the reset as "leaving a chat"
   and saves it again under the account signing out. The wipe is deliberately
   unconditional, so a copy left by a session when the flag was on still goes.
7. **Saving is never metered.** An UrgAns action is billed where the model runs
   (`/api/urgans`); saving what the user already saw costs them nothing. The
   routes use `requireActiveAuthenticatedUser`, so a curator is refused and a
   read-only team keeps its reads while its writes get the standard 403. Every
   background request carries `x-urganize-prefetch`, so a 402 never redirects
   anyone to `/locked`; a 402 or 403 stops saving for the session and says so
   above the composer, and nothing on screen is lost.
8. **Resume never moves someone who has started.** On arrival the browser copy
   restores a chat used in the last six hours (keeping its real last activity —
   reloading every few hours must not keep a chat "recent" forever); then the
   list loads, and a newer chat from another device opens only if the user has
   not sent, opened or started anything and nothing local is unsaved. An auto
   open that is still fetching gives up if the user does something meanwhile.
9. **With the flag on, message ids are uuids.** They are compared position by
   position across tabs and devices, so they must be unique everywhere; the old
   `<ms>-<counter>-<role>` form would collide between two tabs opened at once.
   History off keeps the old form. The request to `/api/urgans` also sends only
   the last `CHAPPI_HISTORY_LIMIT` messages now — the route already forwarded
   only those to the model, and a restored chat can be hundreds long.
10. **The bridge starts from the persisted identity**, not from auth resolving,
    so a recent chat is restored while the UrgAns page still shows its skeleton
    — never a flash of the greeting and then the chat. A persisted session that
    turns out to be dead signs out, and the sign-out wipe removes what was
    restored. The skeleton reserves a transcript when the browser copy says one
    is coming (`useKnownResumableChat`).

### Where it shows

At **xl+** the UrgAns page gains a 256px chats column beside the conversation —
xl rather than lg because the side menu already holds the left column at lg.
Below xl a "Chats" toggle in the page's header row (which now shows at every
width, since it carries the phone's only way in) swaps the region between the
list and the conversation. The side rail gets a history button in its header
that does the same. In both, **the conversation is hidden, never unmounted**,
while the list shows: its upload and recap cards and any reply still on its way
live in it. The in-conversation "New chat" row steps aside at xl where the
column carries its own. The dock is untouched; production runs the mobile nav,
where it renders nothing. When saving has stopped, one quiet line sits above
the composer ("Not saved yet. We'll keep trying." from the second failed
attempt, so a two-second blip does not flash; "This chat can't be saved right
now."; "This chat is too long to save. Start a new chat.").

### Tests

127 new, all in `lib/` because vitest collects only `lib/**` and `app/**`:
`conversation-history.test.ts` (68, the pure decisions), `conversations-server.test.ts`
(18, the table against a recording fake), `conversation-cache.test.ts` (10), a
full-loop `conversation-sync.test.ts` (17) that drives the REAL store against an
in-memory server answering with the same `applySync` rules the route uses, and
`conversation-history-guard.test.ts` (14): every query on the table is scoped to
its owner, the routes are never metered and check the flag before auth, the
stores cannot form an import cycle with the auth store, and the table has row
level security and cascades from its owner. The new UI and server files joined
the press-kit copy guard as a new surface born under the house rules;
`ChappiConversation` deliberately did not, since it predates them. **Mutation-
tested:** adopting another tab's ids before reloading, removing the fork-loop
guard, ignoring renames, dropping the owner check from the delete, and moving
auth above the flag each fail exactly the test written for them.

### Verified

3327 tests passing (3200 before), `eslint .` at 3 errors / 79 warnings against
a measured 3/78 — the one new warning is `useKnownResumableChat`'s mount-effect
read, the same shape as the three hooks beside it in `known-counts.ts` (a second
one, the delete dialog's portal mount guard, was removed rather than accepted:
that dialog only ever opens from a click on a client-rendered list). `tsc
--noEmit` clean apart from the documented pre-existing
`confirmed-action.test.ts` errors. `next build` green **by exit code** in both
flag states with `/auth`, `/onboarding`, `/settings`, `/dashboard` and
`/dashboard/urgans` all still `○ Static` in each. Runtime probes on
`next start`, rebuilding between states: flag off, all four chat handlers answer
404 `{"error":"Not found."}` while `/api/releases` answers 401; flag on, all four
answer 401. The delete button's hover reveal was confirmed in the compiled CSS
(the `@media (hover:hover)` block, the group-hover variant, and `focus-visible`
for keyboard users).

### Not verified

**Nothing has run against a real database or in a browser.** The migration is
unapplied, this sandbox cannot mint a session, and there is no route to
app.urganize.app — so no chat has been saved for real, no list has rendered, no
two-tab conflict has happened outside the fake server, and resume has never
restored a real chat.

### Activation checklist

1. ~~Apply `20260924100000_urgans_conversations.sql`~~ — done by the founder
   2026-09-24, confirmed independently rather than taken on trust: an
   unauthenticated PostgREST `GET` against `urgans_conversations` returned
   **200** with `[]` (RLS hiding every row from an anon caller, not a
   missing-relation error), and an anon `POST` was refused with **42501** —
   proof the table and its owner-scoped policies are both real.
2. ~~Set `NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_URGANS_HISTORY=true`~~ — done 2026-09-24 via
   the Vercel dashboard on the `Web` project's Production environment
   (Config, non-sensitive, matching every other flag there), with an
   explicit no-build-cache redeploy of the then-current production commit.
   Confirmed against production itself rather than the dashboard alone:
   `/api/urgans/conversations` flipped from 404 to 401, and `/api/version`
   reported the fresh `builtAt`.
3. ~~Changelog entry + minor version bump~~ — done, this commit, **v1.44.0**.
4. **STILL OPEN:** the privacy page (`apps/homepage/app/privacy/page.tsx`)
   should say UrgAns chats are kept until deleted and removed with the
   account; bump its `LAST_UPDATED`.
5. ~~Manual pass~~ — **PARTIAL**, in the founder's own real account (he
   signed the browser session in himself). Confirmed: a real message
   round-tripped through a genuine `PUT`, survived a full page reload (not
   client-side routing), and appeared in the history list with the right
   title and timestamp; delete was confirmed through the real `DELETE`
   route and the list correctly returned to "No saved chats yet" after —
   the UI button's hover-reveal itself did not register a click across
   several attempts from this sandbox's browser automation, with nothing in
   the network log suggesting the button is actually broken, so a real click
   is still worth doing. **NOT exercised:** the two-tab conflict path,
   switching chats mid-reply, signing out and in as a different account,
   offline queuing, a read-only team's notice, the export including chats,
   and a rigorous pass across all three responsive layouts against the
   skeleton (only the narrow and xl layouts were seen, in passing).

### Known limits, stated plainly

- A chat switched away from and not yet saved is lost if the tab closes within
  a round trip; the chat on screen is protected by the browser copy, and a
  hidden page flushes with `keepalive` where the body fits.
- No rename, no search, no pinning, no live cross-tab refresh beyond conflict
  handling, no MCP access to chats, no auto-purge, no admin view. All out of
  scope on purpose.
- The router fallback (no model configured) answering after a chat switch is
  dropped rather than routed, since it acts on the screen it runs on.

## Everything after the music (2026-09-24)

Founder brief: Urganize is no longer described as an "AI Music Business
Manager". You make the music; Urganize is where your team does everything
after. Three lines, the founder's, used verbatim:

- **Core line:** "Urganize is where your team does everything after the music is made."
- **Short line** (page titles, meta titles, tight bios): "Everything after the music."
- **Long description:** "You make the music. Urganize is where your team does
  everything after. Plan the release, assign the work, keep files and metadata
  in one place, pitch to curators, book shows and put the release out. For
  artists, managers and labels."

Done in two steps at the founder's request: a find-only list first (file, line,
current text, proposed text), then the edits after a "go". **No feature work, no
pricing change, no migration, no flag, and no changelog entry or version bump**,
the same class as the 2026-09-11 positioning passes: most of it is
`apps/homepage`, which the app-only scope rule excludes, and the `apps/web` half
is descriptions, an email sentence and two footers.

The copy rules the brief set, and which every string below follows: no em
dashes, fifth-grade reading level, never "workspace" in customer copy, deliver
rather than ship, rollout is the work and release is the unit (never "music
rollouts"), never "Global standard, from here." or "Let's build.", and end on
the call to action or just stop.

### What moved

- **`lib/positioning.ts` and its homepage mirror.** New `CORE_CLAUSE` ("where
  your team does everything after the music is made"), `CORE_LINE` and
  `SHORT_LINE`. `PRODUCT_CATEGORY`, `CUSTOMER_LINE` and `PROMISE` are DELETED
  rather than repointed, so nothing can keep composing the old category by
  accident. `ONE_LINER` is the short line, `SHORT_DESCRIPTION` the core line,
  `CANONICAL_DESCRIPTION` the long description, `BRAND_LINE` is "Urganize:
  Everything after the music", and `AUDIENCE` is artists, managers, labels.
  `CORE_CLAUSE` exists so a sentence that already names Urganize ("the privacy
  policy for Urganize, where your team...") can say the line without the name
  twice.
- **The homepage hero:** h1 is the short line with the accent on "after the
  music" (found in the string, not typed as fragments, with a fallback to an
  unaccented line), subhead is the core line. Rendered in headless Chromium at
  1280 and 375: one line on desktop, two on a phone, nothing clipped.
- **SEO:** homepage title is `BRAND_LINE`; `LANDING_DESCRIPTION` is the long
  description, 232 characters, so Google cuts it partway through the list of
  what the product does. Accepted rather than trimmed: the part that says what
  Urganize is always survives the cut. `applicationCategory` in the JSON-LD went
  back to schema.org's "BusinessApplication", since there is no category name
  left to carry.
- **All 19 marketing page descriptions**, plus the brand page (positioning
  paragraph = core line, press boilerplate = long description, "Who it's for"
  names labels), the "Who we are" paragraph in `/terms` and `/privacy`
  (`LAST_UPDATED` deliberately not bumped: renaming how we describe ourselves
  changes nobody's rights), `/signup`'s "Who Urganize is for" (labels added) and
  the `/pricing` lead. The pricing page's "Built for..." line follows
  `AUDIENCE_LINE` on its own and now names labels.
- **The share card** was regenerated (short line as headline, core line under
  it), looked at, written with identical bytes to both apps, and
  `SHARE_IMAGE_VERSION` bumped to `2026-09-24-everything-after-the-music`. The
  generator's accent split used to assume the accent was a PREFIX of the line
  (`MAIN_LINE.slice(ACCENT.length)`); it finds the accent anywhere now, and uses

- **The app:** `apps/web/app/layout.tsx`'s description is the long description,

  second sentence is the core line (imported, so it cannot drift), and the
  public press kit and credits pages end "Made with Urganize. Everything after
  the music." instead of "the operating system for music business".
- **Docs:** `docs/store-listing.md` rewritten (Play and App Store app name is

### UrgAns is held, on purpose

**RESOLVED 2026-09-25: UrgAns says the new line too** (founder call, the day
after: "update UrgAns to use the new line too"). The original text after this
note is the record of the one day it was held, and every item on its undo list
is done.

- **What it says now.** `ROLE` in `lib/chappi/system-prompt.ts` opens "You are
  UrgAns, the personal AI for music professionals inside Urganize, where your
  team does everything after the music is made." Asked what Urganize is, it
  answers with the core line word for word, and adds the long description word
  for word if they want more.
- **Two mechanisms, on purpose, and the comment above `ROLE` says why.** The
  opening sentence is prose, so `ROLE` still reads as one block, and the test
  holds it to `CORE_CLAUSE` (the 2026-09-11 convention for this file). The
  quoted lines are interpolated from `lib/positioning.ts` instead, because "word
  for word" is only true by construction if the words come from there. That
  also keeps the long description's "release" (the founder's word for the unit)
  in the module that owns the line, and "word for word" is what stops the model
  rewording it to "rollout" under `URGANS_COPY_RULES`.
- **The outcome prompt** (`lib/task-outcomes.ts`) introduces UrgAns and Urganize
  from `URGANS_LINE` and `CORE_CLAUSE`, retiring a third description of the
  product ("a rollout planning app for music teams").
- **Tests.** `system-prompt.test.ts` asserts against the shared constants again,
  and checks the RENDERED prompt for the old category, which the positioning
  guard cannot do: it scans source, where the quoted lines are only `${...}`
  holes. `task-outcomes.test.ts` gained the same check. In
  `positioning-guard.test.ts`, "AI Music Business Manager" is an ordinary
  RETIRED pattern now; `HELD_CATEGORY`, the one-file exemption and the tripwire
  test are deleted. Three regressions were put back one at a time (the old
  opening, dropping the quoted long description, the old outcome line) and each
  failed exactly the tests written for it, the first one failing the guard too.
- **No changelog entry or version bump,** the 2026-09-11 precedent: how UrgAns
  describes the product is prompt copy, not a feature.

**Found on the way, not fixed here: the rollout-vocabulary guard never actually
reads `ROLE`.** `lib/rollout-vocabulary.test.ts` lists
`lib/chappi/system-prompt.ts`, but `findObjectWordViolations` skips a whole
segment when any allowed phrase appears anywhere in it, which defeats the
per-match window check after it. `ROLE` is one 12,000-character template
literal that names `create_release`, and it also trips `looksLikeCode` (it
contains `);`), so it is skipped twice over. Measured by running the guard's
own rules against the file: 11 places where the prompt calls the object a
"release" in prose ("link to a release", "one release in full", "the last few
releases") are invisible to the guard that lists it. The same early-out can hide
a real hit in any long segment of the other guarded files that also says
"release date". Suggested as a separate task rather than widened into this one.

**FIXED 2026-09-25, the same day**, in its own change: see the AMENDED note on
`lib/rollout-vocabulary.test.ts` in "The object is a rollout" (2026-09-09). The
11 passages say "rollout" now, and the guard finds that kind of hit.

The brief said to flag, not rewrite, anywhere Chappi or UrgAns calls Urganize the
AI Music Business Manager. Two lines in `lib/chappi/system-prompt.ts` (the ROLE
opening and the "if you are asked what Urganize is" answer) and the outcome
prompt's self-description in `lib/task-outcomes.ts` were left exactly as they
were. So until the founder decides, **the assistant still answers "what is
Urganize?" with the old category** while every other surface says the new line.
That is known, not a bug.

Three things hold that state in place and are the undo list when the decision
lands:

1. `system-prompt.test.ts` pins the held wording as a LITERAL (it used to assert
   against `CUSTOMER_LINE`, which no longer exists). It fails when the prompt
   changes; point it back at the shared constants then.
2. `positioning-guard.test.ts` retires "AI Music Business Manager" everywhere
   through `HELD_CATEGORY`, exempting that one file by path.
3. A tripwire test in the same file asserts the prompt still contains the held
   phrase, so the exemption cannot outlive its reason. Delete the exemption in
   the same change.

A "WhatsApp plan" describing UrgAns was also named in the brief. It is not in
this repo: not in any file, filename, commit message, issue or pull request, so
there was nothing to flag.

### The guard, and why one pattern is case-sensitive

New RETIRED patterns: "Music Business AI" (the old store app name), "operating
system for music", "plan, organize and execute" (the old promise), "Let's build",
and **`/\bAI Music Manager\b/` matched case-sensitively.** The title-cased form is
how the category was written in copy; the lowercase keyword "AI music manager"
stays in `LANDING_KEYWORDS` and the store tags on purpose (nobody searches for
our new line), and a case-insensitive pattern would fail on it. The page rule now
requires every declared marketing description to say "everything after the
music" in words or through a positioning constant. "For labels" and the triple
left RETIRED with the audience change; "small labels" stays.

### A compiler trap worth knowing

On `/terms`, `{CORE_LINE} It is operated by...` rendered as "made.It is": the
compiled JSX dropped the space after the expression. The same pattern on
`/pricing` kept it; the difference is that the terms text contains HTML entities
(`&ldquo;`) later in the same text node. Fixed with an explicit `{" "}`, and
checked in the prerendered HTML. If an expression is followed by text that
contains an entity, make the space explicit.

### Left alone, deliberately

- Search keywords (`LANDING_KEYWORDS`, store tags and Apple keywords): typed,
  not read. The two label keywords removed on 2026-09-11 could return now that
  labels are in the audience; that is a founder call.
- `/for-labels` still redirects to `/pricing`, and the community page still says
  "A group chat for artists and managers running rollouts."
- Historical comments and the changelog, which are records.
- The onboarding role option "Music Manager" (a job title, not positioning) and
  the copy-scan test fixtures.

## The Expo shell (2026-09-24; finished 2026-09-25)

Founder call: move the mobile app from Capacitor to Expo, **keeping the same
approach** — the app still shows the live website, so every web change still
reaches phones with no store review. Offered and declined: a native core
(catalog, activities, UrgAns, notes as React Native screens) and a full native
rewrite. The reasons given: a more app-like feel, easier builds and store
releases, over-the-air updates, and offline/device features. **Not a new scope
expansion** — the same sanctioned mobile surface (2026-07-21), re-shaped. The
full design record is `docs/mobile/expo-shell.md`; read it before touching
`apps/mobile` or any of the website files it names.

**THE CAPACITOR APP IS ON REAL PHONES, which the first session missed, and it
decides the rollout order.** It never reached a store, but its APK (0.41.2) has
been at urganize.app/download since 2026-08-08, and the install card (live
since v1.18.0) sends Android browser visitors there. **That APK is signed with
a real key, not a debug one:** `C:\Users\penta\urganize-upload-key.jks`, issued
to Urganize, Abuja, SHA-256 `37:A4:CB:08…:33:DE` — measured with `apksigner`,
2026-09-25. So two lines in "Native mobile app" above are stale ("one debug
APK", "keystore still to generate"), and the first session's
`android-signing.md` was wrong to say letting EAS make a fresh key "is fine": a
phone only installs an update signed with the same key. The site no longer
speaks Capacitor, so once this is live the old app still signs in with email,
but "Continue with Google" finishes in the phone's browser (its
`allowNavigation` held only urganize.app hosts, so Google opened outside it);
it never had push or a share sheet, since that build predates both. **Swap the
/download APK in the same release**, for an EAS preview build signed with that
key; the four steps are "Switching people from the old app" in
`docs/mobile/expo-shell.md`. The
passwords are in `apps/mobile/android/keystore.properties` in the MAIN
checkout, inside the old Android folder this change deletes from the repo —
save them before anyone runs `expo prebuild --clean` there. **One piece of the
old shell is still recognised:** `isRetiredCapacitorApp()` in `lib/platform.ts`
(`window.Capacitor` exists, which no browser tab has), so the old app is never
read as a phone browser and offered to install itself. Delete it once no
Capacitor installs remain.

**Built in two sessions, and the handover is worth knowing.** The first session
(`expo-mobile-conversion-6b3287`) did the conversion on top of #598 and stopped
before committing, testing or recording anything under "Verified". The second
copied that uncommitted work onto main through a snapshot commit object (a
temporary index over the other worktree, so its folder was never touched),
resolved the one conflict, and finished it. The part of main the first session
never saw is the part that was broken: **share to socials (#602, #605) had
added four share helpers that still called Capacitor**, which the merge kept
and nothing compiled against any more. They go through the bridge now.

### Ten things worth knowing before editing this

1. **The website talks to the shell in exactly one place,
   `apps/web/lib/native-bridge.ts`**, and these modules sit on it:
   `lib/platform.ts`, `lib/external-link.ts`, `lib/native-push.ts`,
   `lib/share-file.ts`, the native branch of `loginWithGoogle` in
   `lib/auth-store.ts`, `components/providers/NativePushBridge.tsx` and
   `components/providers/NativeAppearanceBridge.tsx` (`CapacitorAuthBridge` is
   deleted: the OAuth result comes back as the answer to a request, so no
   listener is needed). Every other caller goes through those and did not
   change. Nothing else should read `window.__URGANIZE_NATIVE__` or post to the
   webview.
2. **The protocol is a package, `packages/native-bridge`, imported by both
   apps**, so the two halves cannot drift. It also holds the shell's pure
   helpers — the dispatcher (`createShellDispatcher`), `safeShareFileName`,
   `notificationPath`, `shouldRetryAfterReconnect`, the colour readers —
   because that is what puts them within reach of vitest, which only runs in
   `apps/web`. `apps/mobile/src/bridge.ts` is only a re-export. Tests:
   `apps/web/lib/native-bridge.test.ts`, plus `share-file.test.ts` and
   `native-appearance.test.ts`.
3. **Detection needs BOTH signals**: the injected `window.__URGANIZE_NATIVE__`
   AND `window.ReactNativeWebView.postMessage`. Either alone means something
   other than our shell, and with neither every export is inert and the website
   behaves exactly as before — which is why none of this needs a feature flag.
4. **Android injects the description LATE, sometimes, and two things cover it.**
   iOS runs `injectedJavaScriptBeforeContentLoaded` as a document-start script,
   before any page script. Android (react-native-webview 13.16) runs it through
   `evaluateJavascript` from `onPageStarted`, which is usually but not strictly
   before the page's first script — read in the library's
   `RNCWebView.callInjectedJavaScriptBeforeContentLoaded`, not assumed. So the
   shell also puts `UrganizeApp/<version>` in the user agent
   (`buildShellUserAgentSuffix`), and `isAndroidBrowser()` / `isIOSBrowser()`
   refuse to call the app a phone browser when they see it; without that, the
   app could offer to install itself. And `whenInShell()` runs code once the
   description arrives, polling for up to 3 seconds only when a post channel
   exists; `NativePushBridge` and `NativeAppearanceBridge` start through it,
   because a missed start loses the notification tap that launched the app.
5. **Capabilities, not versions.** The shell lists the request types it
   understands; asking an older shell for something new rejects at once with
   `UnsupportedRequestError` rather than timing out. Add a request type by
   adding it to `BRIDGE_REQUEST_TYPES` and `BridgeRequestMap`, a handler in
   `App.tsx` (the `BridgeHandlers` type makes a missing one a compile error),
   and a `shellSupports()` check on the web side. The dispatcher also answers a
   request it has no handler for with an error, and calls every handler inside
   the promise chain, so nothing the page sends can throw inside the webview's
   message callback.
6. **Only our own pages drive native code.** The dispatcher drops any message
   whose page URL fails `isFirstPartyUrl` (https, `urganize.app` or a
   subdomain), and any top-level navigation off those hosts goes to the system
   browser or the owning app, never into the webview. A pushed link must pass
   `isSameOriginPath`, which refuses `/\host` as well as `//host`: a URL parser
   reads a backslash after the first slash as a second slash, so the old
   `startsWith('/') && !startsWith('//')` check let `/\evil.test` through as a
   path. Mutation-tested four ways, each failing a named test: loosening the
   host suffix (so `evilurganize.app` passes), dropping the https check,
   skipping the check in the dispatcher, and letting any pushed link through.
7. **Push is React Native Firebase, not expo-notifications**, and that is
   forced: the server sends only through FCM HTTP v1, and Expo's iOS device
   token is a raw APNs token FCM refuses. RN Firebase gives an FCM token on both
   platforms, so the server did not change. Its config plugin only POINTS at a
   notification icon (read in its `setupFirebaseNotifationIcon.js`), so
   `apps/mobile/plugins/withNotificationIcon.js` writes the drawable and colour
   — without it the Android build fails on a missing resource.
8. **A shared file carries no caption.** Android's share sheet takes a file or
   text, not both, and `expo-sharing` shares only a file. The share-to-socials
   sheet copies the caption to the clipboard before it shares, on every path,
   so it is one paste away. Text alone (the DM message) goes through React
   Native's own `Share`, a new `shareText` request that needs no native module.
9. **App-bound domains were removed, reversing the first session's call.** It
   had set `WKAppBoundDomains` + `limitsNavigationsToAppBoundDomains` so a
   service worker could run in the iOS webview. Nothing needs one there today
   (Web Push cannot reach a webview, and `NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_OFFLINE` is off),
   and they narrow what the webview may load and run on a platform nobody can
   test from here. Put both back together if the offline layer is switched on
   and wanted in the app, and test the bridge on a real iPhone first.
10. **The escape in `buildDeliverScript` was a no-op, and the test now catches
    it.** Written `.join('\u2028')` in source, the replacement is the raw
    separator again. It needs a doubled backslash. Harmless on the engines the
    app runs on, but the comment claimed protection the code did not give.
    Worth knowing for anyone editing it: the file tools in this environment
    turn a typed `\uXXXX` into the raw character, so the fix went in through a
    script that builds the backslash from a char code.

### Smaller decisions

- **Native projects are generated, not committed.** `apps/mobile/android` and
  `ios` come from `app.config.ts` via `expo prebuild` and are gitignored.
  `google-services.json` moved to the `apps/mobile` root.
- **Builds are EAS** (`eas.json`: development / preview / production, remote
  auto-incremented build numbers). `codemagic.yaml` is deleted, and the
  hand-kept `versionCode` with it. The app version is read from
  `apps/mobile/package.json`, which mirrors the ledger. Root scripts are
  `mobile:start`, `mobile:build:android`, `mobile:build:ios`.
- **The EAS project id is a constant to paste** (`PASTED_EAS_PROJECT_ID` in
  `app.config.ts`), because `eas init` cannot write into a dynamic config. The
  first session read it from an environment variable only, which every EAS
  build and update would then have needed set; the variable is kept as an
  override.
- **OTA updates reach only the shell's own JavaScript.** The website already
  updates on deploy; anything native needs a store build.
- **Offline:** a native offline screen replaces the webview error page on a
  failed first load, and retries only when reachability TURNS true
  (`shouldRetryAfterReconnect`). The first session retried whenever it WAS
  true, which reloads in a tight loop when the load failed while online (the
  site down, a certificate problem).
- **Process death:** `onContentProcessDidTerminate` (iOS) and
  `onRenderProcessGone` (Android) reload the page instead of leaving a blank
  screen after the OS reclaims the webview's memory.
- **The splash** waits for the first page load, for at most 8 seconds.
- **Keyboard:** Android is edge to edge (`edgeToEdgeEnabled=true` in the
  generated `gradle.properties`), so the keyboard covers the webview instead
  of resizing it. A `KeyboardAvoidingView` with `padding` shrinks it on
  Android only, so the UrgAns composer stays above the keyboard; its
  relative-frame maths gives zero if the system resizes the window anyway, so
  it cannot double up. iOS moves the page itself.
- **Bar colours follow the page**, closing the first session's "ink bands in
  light mode" known limit: `NativeAppearanceBridge` reads the `--color-bg-base`
  token (a variable, so never a colour caught mid-transition), sends it as
  `appearance` on start and on every theme change, and the shell paints the
  safe-area bands and picks status bar text by luminance.
- **Permissions:** Expo's default storage and draw-over-apps permissions are
  in `blockedPermissions`, so notifications are the only permission the app
  ever PROMPTS for. The built manifest also carries install-time ones the
  libraries add (internet, network and wifi state, wake lock, vibrate, FCM
  receive), read with `aapt2 dump badging` rather than assumed. Checked
  against react-native-webview first: its file picker needs none of the
  blocked ones, and its storage check only guards its own download path,
  which this app does not use.
- **The preview profile is the /download build**, so it auto-increments its
  build number (a new APK installs over the last) and passes
  `ORG_GRADLE_PROJECT_reactNativeArchitectures=armeabi-v7a,arm64-v8a` —
  verified to override the generated `gradle.properties` with
  `./gradlew properties`, not assumed. Real phones only: `armeabi-v7a` stays
  because many low-end Android Go phones run 32-bit. **A React Native APK is
  big, and that is a real cost on mobile data:** measured, each chip type's
  native libraries are ~15 MB and the app code ~11 MB (R8 minification is
  off, the Expo default), so the two-chip APK should be around 40 MB against
  the Capacitor one's 3.2 MB. Turning on R8 could cut the code part but needs
  a device test first, since reflection-heavy modules can break under it.
- **TypeScript stays on 5** in `apps/mobile` (Expo 57 recommends 6), excluded
  from `expo-doctor`'s version check, to match the rest of the repo.
- **Vercel installs the whole workspace**, so both web projects now install
  React Native and Expo too. Harmless to the build (the mobile app has no
  `build`, `lint` or `test` task), but it costs install time; filtering the
  install command to `@urganize/web...` is a dashboard change if it matters.
- **Remaining known limits:** Android shows no notification while the app is
  foregrounded (as before), and pull-to-refresh is deliberately off because the
  app's pages scroll inside panels.

### Local Android builds on Windows hit the 260-character path limit

Recorded because it cost two failed builds and will look like a code problem.
`LongPathsEnabled` is 0 on the founder's machine, and inside a worktree under
`.claude/worktrees` the build creates paths of 280-285 characters inside
pnpm's nested store (`node_modules/.pnpm/<pkg>@<ver>_<hash>/node_modules/...`):
first `CreateProcess error=2` on a `prefab_command.bat`, then, from a shorter
folder, ninja's `manifest 'build.ninja' still dirty after 100 tries` because
it cannot stat prefab config files of 261-266 characters. EAS builds on Linux
and never sees this. What worked locally: copy the repo without
`node_modules` to `C:\Users\penta\ub`, add `node-linker=hoisted` to THAT
copy's `.npmrc` only (the flat layout cuts about 80 characters from every
package path), install, prebuild, build. The flat layout is not what EAS uses,
so the JavaScript bundle was checked separately with the project's real
nested layout (`expo export --platform android` in the worktree). Turning on
long paths in Windows would remove the need for any of this, and is the
founder's call, being a system setting.

**A third failure was self-inflicted and is the one to not repeat:** forcing
`-Pkotlin.compiler.execution.strategy=in-process` (to dodge the "Could not
connect to Kotlin compile daemon" the first session logged) runs every
module's Kotlin compile inside the Gradle process, whose generated default of
512 MB class space ran out (`OutOfMemoryError: Metaspace` across seven
modules). Leave the strategy alone and raise the memory instead:
`"-Dorg.gradle.jvmargs=-Xmx3072m -XX:MaxMetaspaceSize=1024m"` on the command
line. Gradle falls back to in-process compiling by itself when the daemon is
unreachable, so the memory is what actually needs covering.

**The test APK built here is signed with React Native's PUBLIC test key**
(`fac61745…` — the `debug.keystore` every Expo prebuild writes, used by the
template's release build too). It cannot install over the old app, and it must
never go on /download: anyone can sign an "update" with that key. It exists to
try the shell on the founder's own phone, after removing the old app.

### Founder-only steps

In order: save the key's passwords from `keystore.properties` into a password
manager and back up the `.jks`; `eas login` and `eas init` (paste the project
id into `PASTED_EAS_PROJECT_ID` in `app.config.ts`); `eas credentials` to
UPLOAD the existing key, answering No to generating one
(`docs/mobile/android-signing.md`, which also covers choosing to upload this
key as the app signing key when Play comes, or Play-installed updates cannot
reach sideloaded phones); build a preview APK. For iOS, add the iOS app in
Firebase, commit `apps/mobile/GoogleService-Info.plist` (iOS builds fail at
prebuild without it) and upload an APNs key. Then ship this change with the
/download swap and run the checklist at the end of `docs/mobile/expo-shell.md`.

**No changelog entry and no version bump in this change**, on the EPK
precedent: the entry lands with the /download swap, which is when the new app
reaches anyone. Merged on its own, this is inert for every browser and changes
only the old Capacitor app, as described above.

## A curator gets a public page to share (2026-09-15, flag-off)

A real playlist curator ("SoundRise Uncovered") posted
`https://app.urganize.app/curator/profile` to a WhatsApp status, telling
artists to pitch her there. **That link did neither of the two things she
thought it did.** It is her own private settings editor, and
`CuratorShell.tsx` redirects everyone else straight to `/auth`, the sign-in
screen — not her profile, not the landing page, nothing about her at all. The
gap behind it was total: `curator_profiles` and `curator_playlists` carried no
slug, no share token and no visibility column, and no share surface existed on
the curator side at all. Every other link in this product belongs to the team
side (`/k/`, `/credits/`, `/capture/`, `/pack/`, `/p/`); a curator had nothing
to hand an artist except the single-use admin-minted invite that let her in,
which cannot be handed on to anyone else.

**Not a new scope expansion.** Playlist pitching was sanctioned 2026-08-10;
this adds a public READ page for an object that already exists and opens no
new write path — the team logins / workspace-invite-links footing. Behind
`NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_CURATOR_PAGE`, default `false`, only meaningful alongside
`NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_PITCHING`.

**Founder decisions, taken before any code:** per curator, not per playlist —
one link listing every playlist she owns, so she never reposts it when her
roster changes — and the page recruits into the product rather than taking an
anonymous pitch. It is read-only; pitching still needs a real account with a
rollout. A public pitch form was the obvious alternative and was rejected:
`playlist_pitches.owner_user_id` is `not null references auth.users`, and both
its spam brakes (the ten-waiting-per-release partial index, the
one-waiting-per-release-per-playlist unique index) key on `release_id`, which
is nullable — a release-less pitch would land with no ceiling at all, and it
would need brand-new rate limiting this repo mostly does not have. Read-only
costs none of that.

### Six things worth knowing before editing this

1. **`/pitch/{slug}`, deliberately not `/curator/{slug}`.** That tree is the
   authenticated area whose shell bounces everyone signed out — nesting a
   public page inside it invites the exact confusion this bug came from.
2. **Two columns, not one, mirroring the press kit's slug/publish split
   verbatim** (`slug`, nullable, `press_kits_slug_shape_check`'s shape mirrored
   exactly; `published_at`, the gate). Unpublishing must not burn the URL she
   already posted, so only `published_at` moves — `DELETE
   /api/curator/profile/publish` never touches the slug. The slug is minted
   **at first publish**, not at profile creation, so curators who never
   publish do not squat names.
3. **THE PAYLOAD IS BUILT FIELD BY FIELD, NEVER BY SPREADING THE ROW, and the
   column-allowlist idiom (`CURATOR_PITCH_COLUMNS`) does not transfer here.**
   The query legitimately needs `user_id` (to find her playlists) and
   `photo_path` (to sign it), so the column list is not the boundary — the
   payload builder is. `buildPublicCuratorPayload` in `lib/curator-public.ts`
   reconstructs the response key by key, and a test asserts `Object.keys()` is
   **exactly** the allowed set, so a column added to the table months from now
   cannot leak through a spread. `user_id`, `invite_id` and `photo_path` never
   reach the client; the page carries a signed `photoUrl` and never a storage
   path, via `generateSignedUrl` (null-safe, memoized) rather than the raw
   `createSignedUrl` the authenticated profile route uses.
4. **Every failure answers the same `null`.** `lib/curator-public-server.ts`
   never throws: a flag that is off, a slug nobody had, an unpublished page
   and a database that is down all collapse to one `notFound()`. `robots:
   {index:false, follow:false}` on **both** branches, including not-found, or
   a guessed slug becomes an indexable page — v1 is noindex outright, the same
   posture `/k/` and `/p/` shipped with before their own `public_listed`
   opt-ins landed.
5. **The signup handoff rides sessionStorage, deliberately not
   `auth.user_metadata`.** The durable `pending_invite_token` mechanism exists
   because a failed invite claim strands an account permanently; this intent
   is only a *destination*, so losing it costs one navigation, not an account.
   `lib/pitch-intent.ts`'s `resolvePostSignupDestination` is one pure,
   order-checked resolver: card trial first (money), then a valid pitch
   intent, then `HOME_PATH` — `OnboardingPageClient.tsx`'s
   `finishToDashboard` was a hardcoded two-way branch before this and is a
   three-way call into that resolver now. The wizard already creates a
   rollout for every new artist (`runPostSignupHandoff`), which is what makes
   "land in the composer, already scoped to her" possible at all.
6. **The composer filter resolves a SLUG server-side, never a curator id, and
   the response shape does not change.** `/api/pitching/playlists?curator=`
   queries `curator_profiles` for the matching `user_id` and adds one `.eq(...)`
   to the existing query; an invalid, unpublished or unresolved slug returns
   an empty list rather than an error. That preserves
   `BrowsablePlaylist`'s documented promise — no curator id anywhere in that
   payload. `PitchingPageClient.tsx` reads the URL param **imperatively, in a
   pre-paint layout effect**, never via `useSearchParams` — that hook in a
   statically prerendered client component ships `loading.tsx` as the server
   HTML, the same weak-connection trap this repo keeps fixing.

### The copy guard had a blind spot, and fixing it found two pre-existing bugs

`lib/press-kit-copy-guard.test.ts` was extended to cover the new files, and a
verification mutation (an em dash dropped into the new page's JSX) was **not**
caught — proving the extension alone was insufficient. The guard's extractor,
`userFacingStrings`, only reads quoted string literals; every file this guard
exists to cover is majority JSX prose, so it had likely never actually checked
the pages it claims to. Swapped to `readableCopy` (the extractor the
positioning and rollout-vocabulary guards already use, which also reaches JSX
text and template literals). Re-running the same mutation now fails correctly.

**The stronger guard immediately surfaced two real, pre-existing em-dash
violations in code this session did not write** —
`lib/chappi/tool-families/press-kits.ts` and `app/k/[slug]/page.tsx` — both
fixed by swapping the dash for a colon. A known, accepted gap remains:
`readableCopy`'s JSX-text pattern cannot see text immediately following a `}`
(an expression container) on the same line, so an invented number placed
right after a ternary is invisible to it. Shared infrastructure, not something
to fix inside this feature, and nothing this feature ships hardcodes a number
— every follower count renders via `playlist.followerCount.toLocaleString('en')`.

A new `lib/curator-public-guard.test.ts` clones the transferable rules from
`lib/press-kit-public-guard.test.ts` (uniform failure, noindex both branches,
no `next/image` on a signed URL, the flag checked before auth). Its own first
draft had the same class of weakness: the "checks the flag before auth" test
compared whole-file `indexOf()` positions, which actually compared import
order rather than call order inside the handler bodies, so a mutation
reordering the real calls inside `POST` survived undetected. Fixed by slicing
each handler's body first and comparing call-site order within that scope.

### Verified

The full suite (3242 passing, 30 skipped), `eslint .` measured against a
freshly stashed clean-tree baseline (3 errors / 78 warnings, all three
pre-existing in `WorkspaceView.tsx`) — **2 new warnings**, both the documented
React-19 `set-state-in-effect` downgrade on a hydration-safe `mounted` guard
and a `window.location.origin` read in an effect, the same accepted pattern
dozens of other components in this repo already carry. `tsc --noEmit` clean
apart from the documented pre-existing `confirmed-action.test.ts` errors.
`next build` green **by exit code** in both flag states, with `/auth`,
`/onboarding`, `/settings`, `/dashboard` and `/dashboard/pitching` all still
`○ Static` in each, and `/pitch/[slug]` correctly `ƒ Dynamic`.

Runtime probes, rebuilding between flag states: flag off, `/pitch/{anything}`
renders the real not-found body (`NEXT_HTTP_ERROR_FALLBACK;404`, `noindex,
nofollow`) while the ungated `/api/releases` still 401s, and the new publish
route answers the exact `isFlagGateOff` body `{"error":"Not found."}`. Flag
on, the publish route and the curator-filtered playlists route both 401
unauthenticated (auth precedes the handler), and `/pitch/{unknown-slug}`
answers the SAME not-found shell as flag-off — this repo's documented
`force-dynamic`-flushes-before-data-resolves quirk (`/epk/`, `/credits/`,
`/capture/` all share it), which is also why a database that cannot be
reached from this sandbox and a slug that genuinely does not exist are
indistinguishable here, exactly as the loader's contract requires.

**Not verified, and it is the whole remaining risk:** nothing has run against
a real database or a real session — this sandbox has neither. No page has
ever rendered a real curator's name, photo or playlist list; no publish, copy,
rename or unpublish has executed; and the signup handoff has never been
followed end to end. The plan's four manual steps are the real test: publish
and copy the link as a curator, confirm the URL survives an unpublish and
republish; open it in a private window and confirm no sign-in is demanded;
follow the CTA through a brand-new signup and confirm it lands in the composer
already scoped to her; and open it as an existing signed-in manager and
confirm the same scoped landing.

### Activation

Flip `NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_CURATOR_PAGE=true` on the Vercel `Web` project with a
commit that actually rebuilds `apps/web` (the `turbo-ignore` trap). Changelog
entry and version bump land **at the flip, not at merge** (the EPK precedent),
and the entry is about what a person sees: playlist owners get a page they can
share so artists can find them.
## Shows leaves beta (2026-09-25, v1.46.0)

The finish of the Events/Shows surface (branch `shows-beta-removal`) and the
removal of the Beta pill. Not a scope expansion: Shows shipped 2026-09-02
(v1.20.0), and this closes the gaps that made it feel like a demo. The detailed
readiness ledger — every area, its case count and where each lives, plus the
bugs the tests found — is `docs/shows-readiness.md`.

**The core promise now works.** A DJ pack delivered no files. The public pack
page (`/pack/[token]`) and the download route now resolve each set row's file
(its chosen version, else the song's default), sign a URL and redirect, with
no-JS download links so a DJ can save each track. Filenames are padded for
running order and kept under a byte limit a phone can save.

**Fixes that earned the tag removal:**
- Pack passcodes removed — set but enforced by neither the page nor the
  download route, so the assistant and UI no longer claim protection that did
  not exist (14 passcode lines gone).
- Rescheduling a show re-dates its run of show and its pack links instead of
  expiring them early; "reopen for 3 more days"; one pack per set.
- Run of show is editable (new `run-of-show` routes) rather than six seeded
  rows stuck on "—"; each step keeps its clock time and its day relative to the
  show when the show moves, correct across a DST change and a zone change.
- Songs get edit/delete routes (typos were unfixable); set-item writes verify a
  chosen version belongs to the row's song and stay inside the artist's
  catalog, dropping the old song's file on a swap.
- Shared `ensureArtistAccess` across the create routes: guests blocked, scoped
  teammates kept to their artist; the list returns the bookable artists.
- Artist-deletion blockers now count shows and songs (and clear the song
  catalog and its files), so the "This artist has rollouts now" message is
  truthful.
- `useEventsStore` and `useArtistRosterStore` reset on sign-out — the same
  privacy fix already made for UrgAns and scene data.
- Timezone-correct set times (a time typed inside the spring-forward skipped
  hour used to land an hour early in US zones); upcoming-first list ordering;
  the song upload UI wired to the existing 3-step signed-URL backend.

Screens were rebuilt for plain wording and reachable states (Shows list, Book a
show, the set builder, the song catalog, the Send-the-tracks card, the DJ pack
page), with shared `ConfirmDialog` / `TimezoneSelect` / `useSongFileUpload`
primitives.

**The Beta pill was still on the Shows nav row** when the fixes landed, even
though the ledger opens "when Shows left Beta." Removed here — `beta: true`
dropped from the Shows row in `WorkspaceIdentityPanel.tsx` (Pitching and
Directory stay beta) — so the code matches the claim.

**Verified** on the merged branch: `vitest run` 4,168 passed / 30 skipped;
`eslint .` at the 3-error / 78-warning baseline (all pre-existing in
`WorkspaceView.tsx`, zero in any Shows file); `next build` green by exit code
with every Shows route compiling and the static routes still static. Coverage:
531 named tests added (~16,500 generated combinations) plus 11 mutation tests
each caught — see the ledger.

**Not verified:** the gate cannot exercise a logged-in Shows session or a real
file upload, and no session is mintable here — so booking a show, uploading a
file, sending a pack and opening it on a phone, and a reschedule re-dating the
links are the remaining manual browser and phone pass (checklist in the ledger).
